stories.Headline: Foreign and institutional investors push the KOSPI below 5,000 as a New York tech selloff spreads to Seoul
stories.Summary:
The KOSPI index tumbled past the 5,000 mark on Friday, November 20, 2026, during a steep domestic stock market decline. Foreigners and institutional investors drove this heavy selling after weak technology stocks crashed in the New York stock market. The KOSPI started trading at 4,928.51, which was down 209.38 points or 4.08 percent from the previous trading day. By 10:00 a.m., the index had plunged more than 200 points and was battling in the mid-4,900 range. The KOSDAQ index also opened lower at 660.98, falling 23.83 points or 3.48 percent to near the 650 mark.

The KOSPI fell into the 4,900 range while the won-dollar exchange rate rose 5.5 won to 1,335.5 won at 9:00 a.m. Samsung Electronics dropped 4 to 5 percent to the mid-to-late 180,000 won mark, and SK hynix plunged over 6 percent. Samsung Electro-Mechanics fell 8 percent, SK Square fell 5 percent, Samsung Life Insurance fell 3 percent, and Hyundai Motor fell 2 percent. Celltrion declined 1 percent, while Ecopro fell 3.46 percent and Ecopro BM fell 3.32 percent in the KOSDAQ market. Semiconductor stocks like Wonik IPS fell 11.86 percent, Leeno Industrial fell 10.67 percent, EO Technics fell 9.55 percent, and HPSP fell 7.92 percent.

Foreign and institutional investors are responsible for the decline, as they maintained a large-scale net selling trend in the spot market. Foreigners showed a deeper aversion to risky assets due to the New York tech crash and possible December Federal Reserve rate hikes. Institutional investors shifted to net selling for profit-taking and stop-loss volumes, focusing on large-cap stocks and index futures. By 9:50 a.m., foreigners net sold 570 billion won and institutions net sold 430 billion won in the KOSPI market. In the KOSDAQ market, foreigners and institutions net sold in the 100 billion won and 10 billion won ranges, respectively.

Individual investors attempted bargain hunting, net buying 920 billion won in KOSPI and 130 billion won in KOSDAQ, but this was insufficient. The decline affected the entire AI industry as market doubts peaked regarding actual cash flow and profit capabilities of massive infrastructure investments. Investors were disappointed following the Initial Public Offering of Anthropic, which froze sentiment after three New York indices tumbled more than 2 percent. Arun Sundaram of CFRA Research told CNN that the current situation is a meltdown with much bearish sentiment around tech and AI. Ted Mortonson of Baird stated that the market turned to fear and panic after a period of greed and speculation.

The domestic market had recovered the 5,100 mark the previous day due to institutional buying before the external unfavorable factors struck. The New York stock market experienced a severe tech selloff, and the Nasdaq Composite lost all of its gains for 2026. The S&P 500 fell 3.7 percent, marking its longest losing streak since February 2020, while the Nasdaq dropped 5.28 percent on Friday. The PHLX Semiconductor Index fell 10.7 percent on Friday, contributing to a weekly loss of 17.1 percent and a 2.3 trillion dollar wipeout. The Dow Jones Industrial Average plunged over 1,100 points on Thursday, dropping below the 50,000-point milestone mentioned by Pam Bondi.

Securities industry experts expect the domestic stock market to remain highly volatile due to uncertainty regarding Federal Reserve monetary policy. The market is currently verifying the efficiency of United States AI investments, which may lead to additional price corrections for the index. Experts suggest that investors should focus on risk management and monitor global semiconductor indices rather than engaging in chase buying. The articles leave open whether the current market situation is a standard correction or the start of a full-blown bear market. It remains uncertain if the departure of foreign investors from domestic semiconductor supply and demand will calm down in the near future.

stories.Headline: Tidal bans wholly AI-generated music and rejects new uploads from December 9
stories.Summary:
The music streaming service Tidal announced on Tuesday that it will ban tracks it believes are completely AI-generated. This new policy will begin on December 9 and makes Tidal the first music streaming platform to ban AI music entirely. The service will remove existing AI tracks and reject all future uploads of music made wholly with artificial intelligence. The company believes this drastic move will resonate with both listeners and artists who value human artistry. All wholly AI-generated tracks will be completely gone from the catalog by the beginning of 2027.

The ban applies to music made completely with AI tools such as Udio, Lyria, and Suno, but allows AI-assisted tracks. Tidal will reject deliveries if metadata says they were generated solely using AI tools and will ban distributors from delivering them. The platform expects to reject between 80,000 and 85,000 songs a day once the new policy goes into effect. This move will remove between 27 and 29 million tracks, which represents about six percent of the total Tidal catalog. The service will also continue to ban songs associated with fraudulent activity, including those that impersonate established artists.

Robert Andersen, the Tidal Lead at parent company Block, stated on X that something more drastic needed to be done. He noted that 43 percent of tracks distributed in the last 90 days were detected as wholly AI-generated. Andersen pointed out that 96 percent of all AI-generated songs receive zero plays and encouraged other industry peers to follow suit. Tidal stated the policy protects the authenticity and livelihoods of rightsholders and ensures artists get paid more. The company claims the update prevents authentic music from being buried under tracks that no one asked for.

Tidal says AI music is a serious problem that diverts royalties from working artists and confuses fans. The service has already taken down over 65,000 tracks that were flagged for suspected artist-name impersonation. Other platforms like Apple Music and Spotify are testing different approaches, such as labeling AI creations as an AI Persona. Apple Music said it would label AI-generated or AI-assisted tracks, while Spotify removed millions of slop or spam tracks. Spotify believes that as AI makes music more abundant, listeners will value human artistry even more.

Tidal previously began labeling and demonetizing AI-powered songs over the summer and forced artists to label tracks as AI-generated or assisted. The service noted that on November 6 alone, 60 percent of newly uploaded songs were fully AI-generated tracks. Tidal has been testing its detection tools by working with Ircam Amplify to identify these songs. A spokesperson said the detection success rate is very high, though a small amount of false positives is inevitable. The company uses an appeals process and improving technology to maintain confidence in its current detection approach.

Tidal will now continue to remove wholly AI-generated tracks and reject new uploads based on metadata and detection tools. The company will keep sharing what it finds regarding AI music and will continue acting on those findings. The articles leave open whether other major streaming services will adopt similar bans or stick to labeling. It remains unclear how effectively Tidal can enforce these removals without accidentally deleting music made by real human artists. The service will continue to monitor the scale of AI music intended to mislead listeners and impersonate artists.

stories.Summary:
Members of the Hawaiʻi Senate Committee on Labor and Technology and House Committee on Economic Development and Technology will host a joint informational briefing on Nov. 25. The briefing will examine the development and application of artificial intelligence, its role in government operations and emerging opportunities for workforce development. The public is encouraged to attend the briefing from 10 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. in Conference Room 329 at the Hawaiʻi state Capitol.

The Capitol is located at 415 S. Beretania St., in Honolulu, and those who cannot attend in person can watch via livestream. As is customary for informational briefings, no public testimony will be accepted. The informational briefing will provide legislators an opportunity to gain a greater understanding about the evolving landscape of artificial intelligence and its implications for state government, cybersecurity and workforce development. Presentations will focus on the history and development of artificial intelligence, emerging artificial intelligence policies and applications in government, and cybersecurity considerations related to artificial intelligence. Additional topics include opportunities to leverage artificial intelligence to improve government efficiency, Enterprise Technology Services’ artificial intelligence strategy and initiatives within state government, and opportunities to use artificial intelligence in workforce development.

Committee members will have the opportunity to ask questions following each 15-minute presentation. The briefing is scheduled to run from 10 a.m. to 12:30 p.m. on Nov. 25, 2026. Presenters at the briefing include Andrew Merluzzi, AI Innovation and Incubation fellow at the Beeck Center for Social Impact Innovation at Georgetown University.

stories.Headline: New York governor signs five-year ban on AI chatbot toys for children
stories.Summary:
New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed legislation on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, imposing a five-year ban on the manufacture, distribution, and sale of children's toys equipped with AI companion chatbots. The signing took place in Harlem at Grandma's Place, a toy store owned by retired schoolteacher Dawn Harris-Martine. The law targets talking stuffed animals, dolls, and robots that use internet-connected AI chatbots to hold conversations with children. Hochul cited concerns over child safety, privacy, and emotional manipulation as reasons for the ban.

The ban takes effect on February 22, 2027, which is 90 days after the bill was signed, and remains in place for five years. Under the legislation, manufacturers and retailers are prohibited from making, distributing, exchanging, or selling such toys across New York state. Violations of the new law could result in civil penalties of up to $15,000 per day for each violation. The restrictions will not be in force during the upcoming holiday season, as the effective date falls after that period. The law applies to toys with internet access and integrated AI capabilities, regardless of the child's age.

Governor Hochul said parents shopping for gifts should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings, or put their privacy at risk. She stated that protecting children from the risks of unregulated AI was a priority for her administration. Hochul urged parents and caregivers to consider the potential risks of AI-powered toys before buying gifts for young children during the holiday season. She warned that there are toys out there that could be harmful to children, and that children are hearing harmful content from a toy that parents trust. The governor also said technology is evolving rapidly and that laws must adapt to keep pace.

Dawn Harris-Martine, known to customers as Grandma Dawne, said a good toy for a child is one that stretches their imagination. She opened Grandma's Place in the late 1990s and has long encouraged parents to be actively involved in their children's play. Harris-Martine said it is necessary to avoid situations where a three-year-old can sit and listen to a teddy bear telling them to do strange things. She plans to continue offering what she described as an AI-free environment for children and families. Muna Heaven, a Harlem mother and member of Mothers Against Media Addiction, said parents and children want toys to be fun but also have a baseline expectation that they will be safe.

Heaven said her group has identified examples ranging from inappropriate or sexual conversations to dangerous advice, including instructions on how to find knives, associated with AI chatbot toys. She said young people are being harmed by toys powered by artificial intelligence, with many examples available. Supporters of the measure say AI-powered toys have generated concerns about child safety. The legislation builds on New York's existing safeguards for AI companion chatbots, which are designed to address risks associated with interactions between users and AI systems. Harris-Martine also advised parents not to put an iPad in a child's hands and walk away, but to be present and get off their phones.

The law will take effect on February 22, 2027, and remain in place for five years, with civil penalties of up to $15,000 per day for violations. Hochul urged parents to pay attention while shopping during the holiday season, since the ban will not yet be in force. stories.Headline: Dell raises fiscal 2027 revenue forecast to $202 billion on record AI server demand
stories.Summary:
Dell Technologies raised its annual revenue forecast on November 24, 2026, following a record quarter. The company increased these projections because of surging global demand for its artificial intelligence servers. These servers use Nvidia chips to handle autonomous agents and other complex AI workloads. This growth is being driven by a boom in generative AI among cloud providers and businesses.

The company lifted its revenue forecast for fiscal 2027, which runs from February 2026 through January 2027, to 202 billion dollars from 192 billion dollars. This new guidance exceeds the market consensus of 194.5 billion dollars and follows previous increases in May and September. Dell also raised its adjusted earnings per share forecast to 29.68 dollars from 25.50 dollars. The AI server revenue forecast specifically rose to 78 billion dollars from 74 billion dollars.

Chief Operating Officer Jeff Clarke stated that the company booked 60.2 billion dollars in orders during the third quarter alone. He noted that the AI backlog reached an all-time high of 132.3 billion dollars as demand spread worldwide. Clarke explained that Dell has become a different company because the Infrastructure Solutions Group now drives most of its growth and profit. This group, which manages storage and servers, saw revenue nearly triple from the previous year to 41.97 billion dollars.

The company reported third quarter results for August through October with revenue of 54.94 billion dollars and adjusted earnings per share of 9.45 dollars. Dell approved an additional 25 billion dollars in share buybacks and expects fourth quarter results to beat market estimates. The firm is currently working to transform itself into a full scale information technology infrastructure company for the AI era.

stories.Headline: US dollar slips as artificial intelligence stock rally fades
stories.Summary:
The US dollar slipped on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, as a sharp rally in artificial intelligence stocks began to fade away. This decline followed a period of gains on Monday that were sparked by the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as Nvidia's chief executive. Traders questioned if the greenback had climbed too far and too fast while the initial excitement over the AI trade diminished. The currency had been supported by bets that the Federal Reserve would keep raising interest rates because growth remains strong. Inflation is still stubbornly above the two percent target set by the Federal Reserve, which had previously bolstered the dollar's value.

The dollar index fell 0.47 percent to 103.81, while the euro rose 0.6 percent to 1.0966 and sterling strengthened 0.64 percent to 1.3112. The Japanese yen weakened 0.16 percent to 159.24 per dollar, and the Australian dollar gained 0.24 percent to reach 0.6641 on Tuesday. Nvidia shares fell around 8 percent, and Anthropic tumbled nearly 8 percent, sliding below its initial public offering price for the first time. The S&P 500 fell around 0.5 percent, and the Nasdaq Composite declined more than 1 percent due to the drop in tech. These movements occurred in New York as the AI rally, which had previously lifted the dollar, began to lose its momentum.

Elias Haddad of Brown Brothers Harriman said the US growth edge over Japan, the UK, and the euro zone narrowed in November. He suggested that this narrowing of the growth advantage could weigh on the dollar as the market adjusts to new economic data. Fed funds futures traders are pricing in 97 percent odds of a rate hike in December and 66 percent for January. Analysts at JPMorgan noted that bearish positioning in the Australian dollar has reached extreme levels according to their own internal market metrics. These experts observed that options for the Australian dollar have seen puts outnumbering calls for several months during this recent period.

Investors in technology shares were affected as the AI boom showed signs of volatility, with stocks recording both huge rises and falls. The Australian dollar was the worst performing major currency against the greenback over the last month, dropping by more than 5 percent. Speculators hold their largest bearish position in the Aussie on record, which LSEG calculations value at approximately 12.25 billion US dollars. Some analysts are questioning how long the relief provided by the return of Jensen Huang will last for the broader equity markets. Recent stock market wobbles have raised questions about how far the Federal Reserve can tighten rates without hurting the overall economy.

The AI trade had previously drawn capital into the US and raised growth expectations, which helped the dollar reach a 20-month high. Jensen Huang had resigned less than two weeks ago following revelations of an affair with a subordinate and a suspected Chinese spy. His return to Nvidia followed an extraordinary intervention by President Trump, despite the board of directors stating he would not return. US consumer confidence increased more than expected in November, reaching its highest level in nearly two years after the recent midterm elections. German business morale also rose for a seventh straight month in November, which provided an additional boost to the single currency.

The market now waits to see if the Federal Reserve will follow through with the interest rate hikes priced in by traders. Investors are monitoring whether the volatility in AI stocks like Nvidia and Anthropic will continue to drag down the major indexes. It remains open whether the return of Jensen Huang can provide long term stability for Nvidia after his controversial resignation and return. The articles leave open how the Federal Reserve will balance inflation targets against the risk of hurting the economy through tightening. Traders continue to speculate on the direction of the Australian dollar as bearish positions remain at record levels in the market.

stories.Headline: Eight storage vendors unveil data protection and Azure products at Microsoft Ignite 2026
stories.Summary:
Eight vendors introduced or demonstrated data storage products at Microsoft Ignite 2026, which kicked off November 17 in San Francisco. The products debuted at the conference or in the three months leading up to it. Veeam, Commvault, and Cohesity focused on data protection and data management. Everpure, Qumulo, and Nutanix targeted the economics and operations of running storage on Azure. Dell Technologies introduced on-premises AI infrastructure, while DataBahn looked at how security teams and AI agents access their data.

Veeam Intelligent ResOps for Microsoft 365, released in October and now generally available, connects in a few clicks with no data migration or re-architecture needed. It shows which AI agents, including Copilot, are touching data across SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams, and Exchange. Customers can find sensitive data, close oversharing gaps, cut storage costs by quarantining redundant data, and precisely undo AI-driven file changes. It is available in Foundation and Advanced editions through Veeam Cloud & Service Providers. DataBahn Federated Search & Orchestration, introduced in August, lets security teams and AI agents search data across Microsoft Sentinel, data lakes, warehouses, and cold storage without moving or duplicating it.

Kirkland, Washington-based Veeam Software said the add-on gives partners a new way to grow revenue with existing Veeam Data Cloud for Microsoft 365 customers. Dallas-based DataBahn said analysts can ask questions in plain language, and Lumen, its threat-hunting agent, correlates evidence across sources and returns a cited timeline. Round Rock, Texas-based Dell Technologies said the Dell AI Factory with Microsoft Foundry Local, introduced at Ignite and slated for shipping in the first half of 2027, combines Foundry Local with Dell compute and storage including PowerEdge XE9780 servers built on the Nvidia HGX platform. Tinton Falls, New Jersey-based Commvault said its new integration with Microsoft Defender ingests Defender alerts into Threat Scan and correlates them with protected backup assets. San Jose, California-based Nutanix said its Azure updates offer more options for sizing, placement, and cost control while preserving familiar operations.

Chris Konrad, vice president global cyber at World Wide Technology, a St. Louis-based solution provider, said customers have more and more data to protect, and all the AI buildouts are consuming power and cooling space. He said there is an explosion of data unlike anything he has seen in his 30-year career, including in customers’ Microsoft environments. Konrad said everybody is scrambling now to understand what that looks like, and backup recovery resilience is forefront with everybody. Santa Clara, California-based Cohesity said its Gaia Catalog integration with Azure Databricks eliminates the need to build new ETL pipelines to move or duplicate data. Santa Clara, California-based Everpure said its Azure-native block storage can reduce cloud storage costs by up to 40 percent for Azure VMware Solutions deployments.

Veeam, Commvault, and Cohesity focused on data protection and data management, while Everpure, Qumulo, and Nutanix targeted the economics and operations of running storage on Azure. Dell Technologies introduced on-premises AI infrastructure, and DataBahn looked at how security teams and AI agents get at their data. The vendors are betting customers are tired of copying data around just to put it to work. Nutanix and Dell are both pitching familiar operations across on-premises and Azure environments. Commvault is feeding Microsoft Defender alerts into its backup platform so customers can make better recovery decisions after an attack.

Qumulo introduced ANQ Frozen, which extends Azure Native Qumulo to the low-cost Blob Archive tier as an alternative to tape for long-retention data. Data moves to Azure Frozen by policy, but the file namespace stays live, letting users browse directories over SMB and NFS. Qumulo NeuralSearch keeps file and application metadata searchable, so teams can find what they need, including data for AI training, before paying to retrieve it. Files are stored as native objects in a dedicated Azure storage account, avoiding lock-in. ANQ Frozen is available now in controlled preview, with general availability planned for 2027.

stories.Headline: Fakeeh Health and Boston Health AI sign deals to bring AI clinical documentation to UAE clinicians
stories.Summary:
Fakeeh Health and Boston Health AI signed two strategic agreements on 24 November 2026 in Dubai. The signing took place on the sidelines of the 5th Annual Fakeeh Health International Conference. The event was attended by Sheikh Ahmed bin Hasher bin Ahmed Al Maktoum. Together, the two organisations will introduce AI-supported clinical documentation across Fakeeh Health. They will also jointly develop new AI solutions for healthcare providers in the UAE and the region.

The first agreement gives clinicians more time for their patients by taking on routine documentation in the background. AI will help physicians focus on the person in front of them, while the physician remains in control of the clinical record. Patient data stays in the UAE and is protected in line with national regulations. The second agreement involves Takamul Innovative Health Solutions and Boston Health AI working together to develop new solutions. These solutions will help healthcare providers work more efficiently and build local expertise in clinical AI through education and research.

Dr. Mohaymen Abdelghany, Group CEO and Board Member of Fakeeh Health and CEO of Fakeeh University Hospital, said the philosophy of Care & Beyond puts the patient at the centre of every decision. He said that starts with the doctor's full attention, and the partnership gives physicians more time with patients. Through Takamul, they will build new AI solutions for healthcare providers across the UAE and the region. He said this is in line with Dubai's vision for a digitally enabled healthcare system. Dr. Adil Haider, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Boston Health AI, said physicians did not go into medicine to type.

Dr. Haider said Fakeeh Health shares the belief that technology should give clinicians their time back. He called Fakeeh Health the right partner to deploy the platform and build the next generation of clinical AI. He said Boston Health AI is proud to build in the UAE, with a local team and patient data that stays in the country. The agreements support the UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031 and the Dubai Universal Blueprint for Artificial Intelligence. Fakeeh Health is a UAE healthcare group brought to the UAE by the founders of Fakeeh Care Group.

Fakeeh Health builds on more than four decades of clinical excellence, research and innovation. Its flagship, Fakeeh University Hospital in Dubai Silicon Oasis, is a smart academic hospital combining clinical care, medical education and research. Takamul Innovative Health Solutions is Fakeeh Health's healthcare services company, providing consulting, operations and business services to healthcare providers in the UAE. Boston Health AI is a clinical AI company founded by surgeon-scientist Dr. Adil Haider. Its platform was developed by physicians and engineers and supports care teams across the patient journey, with clinical authority always resting with the physician.

The articles do not state a specific timeline for when the AI-supported clinical documentation will be introduced across Fakeeh Health. They also do not give financial terms for either of the two agreements. No details are provided about which specific UAE healthcare providers beyond Fakeeh Health will use the new solutions developed through Takamul. The articles leave open how many physicians or patients will be affected by the first agreement. They also do not say what specific new AI solutions Takamul and Boston Health AI will develop together.

stories.Headline: PostSig wins best AI for infrastructure and operations at 2026 buy-side awards for its CPM product
stories.Summary:
PostSig announced on November 24, 2026 that it has been named Best Artificial Intelligence for Infrastructure & Operations at the 2026 WatersTechnology Buy-Side Technology Awards. The announcement came from San Francisco, California through a press release distributed by ACCESS Newswire. PostSig received the award for its PostSig CPM product, which is powered by PostSig LineageAI. The company said the award recognizes how PostSig brings intelligence into daily operations for buy-side firms. PostSig did not state the exact date or location of the awards ceremony in its announcement.

PostSig CPM connects the agreements that govern a firm's vendor relationships with its spend, invoices, products, and entitlements. The product helps teams identify billing discrepancies, track changing commitments, and prepare for renewals with evidence from the underlying records. An amended fee schedule can change the correct invoice amount, and a service order removing a product can expose continued billing for that product. Usage data can reveal that a renewal includes licenses the firm no longer needs. Recent product expansion brings spend, inventory, product and fee schedules, vendor oversight, and Financial Terminal management into a shared commercial context.

Phil Kim, Chief Product Officer and Co-Founder of PostSig, said teams should be able to trace an invoice, product or renewal back to the terms that govern it. Kim said LineageAI connects those records as they change, giving teams a consistent basis for checking charges, managing entitlements and making renewal decisions. Hendrik Bartel, CEO and Co-Founder of PostSig, said buy-side firms need AI-native solutions that can explain what they are paying for, what they are entitled to and where action is needed. Bartel said that requires understanding which commitments apply today, how they have changed, and the evidence behind every answer. He said the award recognizes how PostSig brings that intelligence into daily operations.

PostSig also provides evidence-backed conversational access through LineageAI Assistant and governed access through PostSig MCP, extending that context to approved enterprise applications and AI agents. Procurement, finance and operations teams can validate invoices against agreed pricing, trace price changes, manage products and entitlements, allocate costs and prepare for renewals using the same underlying commercial context. PostSig extends the value of contract lifecycle management beyond signature by connecting governing commitments to financial and operational activity. The product works alongside existing CLM, ERP, CRM, procurement, and finance systems without requiring firms to replace their systems of record. PostSig said its applications include PostSig CPM and Investor Rights Intelligence.

PostSig describes itself as the AI platform for the people that run the business, with contracts defining the rules a business runs on. Powered by LineageAI, PostSig applies the agreements and commitments that govern an organization to the business operations they affect. The company said a superseded fee schedule can change what should be paid, and a later service order can reveal continued billing for a product that was removed. Inventory and utilization can change a renewal's economics, according to PostSig. The company directed readers to visit postsig.com/bestai to see why PostSig won and how it works.

PostSig did not announce any specific next steps, new product releases, or future plans in the press release. The company did not disclose the names of other finalists or competitors in the award category. The announcement did not include financial details, customer counts, or revenue figures related to the award. PostSig did not state whether it plans to attend or exhibit at any upcoming industry events following the award. The press release left open how the award might affect PostSig's market position or customer adoption.

stories.Headline: UC faculty criticize $1.2 million OpenAI deal giving students free ChatGPT access
stories.Summary:
The University of California is procuring full access to ChatGPT Edu for all students and faculty as part of a $1.2 million agreement with OpenAI. The one-year partnership takes effect in December and is an extension of a 2024 agreement with OpenAI. UC students, staff and faculty will also have access to OpenAI's coding agent Codex. The agreement surprised members of UC's Academic Senate, who raised concerns late last month that administrators had not sufficiently consulted faculty. Administrators met with UC faculty after the Academic Senate raised concerns in an October letter.

The partnership costs $1.2 million and lasts one year, beginning in December. It provides full access to ChatGPT Edu for all UC students and faculty, plus access to the coding agent Codex for students, staff and faculty. The agreement is an extension of a 2024 deal with OpenAI. UC announced additional training opportunities as part of the expanded partnership. University leaders emphasized that students and faculty are not required to use the technology or incorporate it into classrooms.

Academic Senate Chair Susannah Scott said the case is far more serious than a routine software purchase. She said the Academic Senate believes it is unwise to provide students with universal access to a tool capable of performing the academic work required to earn a degree. Scott said faculty wants administrators to engage in genuine consultation with faculty experts so UC can provide the most appropriate tools and guidance. A UC spokesperson said administrators have discussed the OpenAI partnership with Academic Senate leadership and other faculty members since this spring. The spokesperson wrote that the University will continue working with the Academic Senate and other faculty groups on best AI practices.

Camille Crittenden, executive director of CITRIS at UC Berkeley, said the agreement will help UC maintain a forward-looking position on AI adoption. Crittenden acknowledged faculty concerns but said large universities need to ensure students, staff and faculty have appropriate tools for the 21st century. UC San Diego Chancellor Pradeep Khosla said he has seen AI tools used in novel ways by faculty and staff on his campus. Khosla applauded the OpenAI partnership for expanding ChatGPT access to students, faculty and staff. He acknowledged that AI could create wealth and enhance abilities but also lead to further inequities.

During the September board of regents meeting, UC administrators proposed adopting systemwide access to AI tools produced by OpenAI or Anthropic. The Academic Senate would be consulted before an agreement was signed, according to the update from UC's Office of the President. Academic Senate leadership said they were not made aware of the purchase agreement with OpenAI until a month later. Scott told UC President James Milliken in her October letter that providing students with ChatGPT would be perceived as endorsing students' AI use in all courses. She said that would sit in tension with professors who may seek to restrict the use of AI in classrooms.

Scott requested that the Academic Senate be allowed to provide feedback before UC finalized an agreement with OpenAI. She also asked that ChatGPT not be deployed for academic purposes on campuses until faculty could weigh in on limitations. Scott said the core concerns raised in the October 30 letter remain unresolved. UC Chief Information Officer Van Williams acknowledged faculty's desire to give input but said the university needed to move quickly on the deal. Milliken said in a Thursday letter that the terms of the partnership would benefit UC community members and that the decision has the full support of all UC Chancellors.

stories.Headline: Brook Porter bets on solar and batteries to power future AI data centers
stories.Summary:
Brook Porter, a partner at G2 Venture Partners, shared his investment strategy on November 24, 2026. He is betting on solar power and batteries to energy future AI data centers. This approach follows a recent analysis conducted by Porter and his colleagues at G2VP. The strategy aims to solve the growing problem of supplying power to AI data centers. Porter believes that solar and energy storage are the best ways to move faster.

The plan requires using solar paired with long-duration energy storage to build facilities independently of the grid. This off-grid path avoids permitting constraints like air permits and grid access in the United States. G2VP led the Series C for Crusoe and estimates data center investment will top 4 trillion dollars. Natural gas capacity is only 60 or 70 gigawatts per year, while solar is over a terawatt. Two paths exist: small on-grid facilities with generating capacity or larger solar powered centers.

Brook Porter stated that demand for power is growing faster than people currently appreciate. He explained that the challenge involves atoms rather than bits as the world recognizes these realities. Porter claimed that leveraging Wright's Law by making the same thing repeatedly is a vital lesson. He said that speed, scale, and economics are dimensions where this modular technology can win. He believes developers must be nimble to catch the big wave of this technology.

Hyperscalers and data center developers are the primary groups affected by these power supply challenges. Many companies have been buying, renting, and deploying natural gas power plants to secure energy. Lithium-ion batteries are too expensive to compete with fossil fuels for providing round-the-clock power. However, new products from Form Energy and Antora Energy have lowered the cost per megawatt-hour. These long-duration storage options provide a cheaper alternative for powering large AI data centers.

The U.S. grid has shifted from basically zero growth to adding several gigawatts every year. This change happened in just a few years as AI data center power needs increased. Supply chains have taken time to scale, forcing companies to find power in any form. G2VP gained an early window into this development through their investment in the company Crusoe. This experience allowed them to see how different waves of data centers have evolved.

Developers should start thinking about these new storage technologies now to accelerate their time to market. Broad acceptance of these long-duration energy storage products may still be a few years away. The articles leave open exactly when these technologies will reach a state of broad industry acceptance. They do not specify the exact timeline for the transition to off-grid renewable power. The text does not state which specific locations will host these new solar powered centers.

stories.Headline: Hyderabad police plan India’s first AI-powered police station at Panjagutta for a December pilot
stories.Summary:
Hyderabad city police have proposed introducing artificial intelligence-powered smart police stations to modernise policing and speed up criminal investigations. Panjagutta police station is being developed as what officials described as India’s first AI-powered police station. The pilot project is scheduled for launch in the first week of December. Police commissioner Mahesh Murlidhar Bhagwat visited the Panjagutta police station on Monday and obtained feedback from the technical team. Telangana Director General of Police C.V. Anand and Bhagwat conducted a surprise inspection of the station on Wednesday.

The initial proof-of-concept phase plans five AI-based capabilities at the central command centre before extending them to individual police stations. These include automated scanning and retrieval of CCTV footage to help investigators track suspects and reconstruct crime scenes. AI-assisted facial recognition would identify wanted persons using authorised police databases, with mandatory human verification before any action is taken. The system would analyse historical crime records alongside CCTV footage to identify repeat offenders and emerging crime patterns. For crowd management, the technology would enable real-time headcounts, crowd density monitoring and automated congestion alerts to prevent stampedes.

A senior police officer said the platform would be integrated with existing police software systems. Senior officials stated that this AI-based police station will be officially inaugurated soon as a pilot project. The senior officials said the introduction of AI is expected to modernise policing, speed up criminal investigations, reduce administrative workload and improve citizen services. Police sources said the proposed framework integrates artificial intelligence, computer vision, voice technology and digital investigation tools with existing police databases and surveillance networks. A senior police officer said Bhagwat would take a final decision on the project.

During the Wednesday inspection, the senior officials interacted directly with complainants visiting the station and inquired how staff were receiving and resolving their issues through the AI system. They personally monitored the performance of every staff member at the station and observed how they were discharging their duties with AI assistance. Additional DGP (Law & Order) Akun Sabharwal, Hyderabad Additional CP (Crimes & SIT) M. Srinivasulu, Intelligence DIG Bhaskaran and Khairatabad Zone DCP Shilpavalli participated in the inspection program. Khairatabad Zone DCP, ACP Murali Krishna and Inspector Jahangir Yadav also inspected the AI technical infrastructure being established at the station. The AI-powered command centre would provide senior officers with real-time information on field deployments and ongoing incidents across the city.

The proposed expansion across police stations in all zones is aimed at strengthening digital evidence management, reducing response times and improving coordination between police stations and the central command centre. Senior officials were holding discussions with technical teams on the implementation plan. Bhagwat recently took over as the Police Commissioner. The framework will integrate AI, computer vision, voice technology and digital investigation tools with the police database and surveillance network. On International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, 25 November, Hyderabad City Police said every woman has the right to live without fear, with dignity and respect.

The AI-based police station will be officially inaugurated soon as a pilot project, though no exact date beyond the first week of December is given. The articles do not state when the five AI-based capabilities will be extended from the central command centre to individual police stations. They also do not specify the cost of the project or which zones will receive the expansion first. The final decision on the project rests with Police Commissioner Bhagwat after his feedback from the technical team. The articles leave open how the mandatory human verification for facial recognition will be staffed and supervised.

stories.Headline: AI lets companies predict individual consumer behavior from purchases and personal data, Jeff Gaus says
stories.Summary:
Companies are using artificial intelligence to process vast amounts of customer data and personal information, narrowing advertising down to the individual level. Jeff Gaus, now CEO of the Provenance Chain Group, described the change on November 24, 2026, comparing his earlier work with drugstore cash-register data to today’s AI systems. What once took multiple days and several number-crunching humans can now be worked out in minutes or seconds by artificial intelligence, he said. The article from TIME describes how AI draws on purchases, opinions, preferences, personal stories, geolocations, photos, and videos from search engines and social media platforms. Gaus said that five years ago companies were at a five or six on a ten-point scale of customer knowledge, but today they are at about 9.2 or 9.3.

The new AI systems can create constantly evolving “digital twin” models of specific people or small populations to predict consumer behavior based on a matrix of financial and personal data points. Retailers use purchase patterns, credit-card charges, AI chatbot inquiries, and even voting patterns to understand product preferences down to specific ZIP codes. Gaus recalled a fellow panelist who had formerly worked in government intelligence describing a map that plotted a person’s consumer purchases on all credit cards over 45 days, where his car had driven, and what telephone calls he had been making. The data came from private corporations, according to the panelist’s account. A separate report from the Institute for Corporate Productivity found that just 10% of companies are focused on continuous organizational redesigns alongside AI implementation.

Justin Sherman, founder of Duke University’s Privacy and Democracy Project and now CEO of Global Cyber Strategies, said AI can draw commercially beneficial information out of even anonymized records. He noted that a company or research organization or consumer might share information thinking that it is quote-unquote anonymized, but AI-advertising technology companies and data brokers can mash it all together and link it back to people. Callie Schroeder, director of the AI and Human Rights Program at the Electronic Privacy Information Center, said AI can go through information so fast and sort and parse out what it wants to pull from it. She argued that it would be better for society if laws and norms caught up to the need for a shared approach to what consumers should be able to expect. Kevin Martin, chief research officer at i4cp, said the companies that come out ahead in 2027 will be the ones that are better at the art and science of changing.

Sherman said he has bought plenty of things through targeted ads he has gotten online, and he particularly appreciated recommendations on music and video streaming services. He said the thing to watch out for is a situation in which consumers are not offered a meaningful way to give or withdraw consent for use of their personal data. Schroeder said she had to manually go through all the settings on a new phone and turn off a whole bunch of machine-learning things, and that it is a lot of work and unfair that consumers have to do it. A 2026 Gallup study found that 50% of CHROs surveyed were not confident that their company’s managers were able to guide employees’ AI use at work. The i4cp research found that 56% of organizations where HR was in charge of AI adoption said they were either mostly or fully AI-ready, compared to only 18% when AI adoption was led by IT teams.

In 2009, Ars Technica wrote about how data scientists had shown they could re-identify sets of supposedly anonymized information, from medical records to AOL searches, with remarkable ease. That piece was based on research by Georgetown University law professor Paul Ohm, who was quoted as saying, “Data can either be useful or perfectly anonymous, but never both.” Gaus said that fifteen years ago his firm bought drugstore cash-register data and could tell pharma reps that “Dr. Smith has three people with this condition” and instruct them to go pitch their wares to that doctor. The i4cp study found that as more routine analysis and entry-level tasks are given to AI, companies risk losing the kinds of developmental routines that help teach judgment and critical thinking. The report said this could result in “a talent shortage created from within.”

Gaus said the depth and breadth of data available sometimes surprises even him, and the specificity of what companies are able to know about their customers is only going to get more astounding. The i4cp report said CEOs will be examining how investments in AI have changed their companies and their workforces, making the role of CHROs in managing and implementing AI adoption increasingly important. CHROs said their main internal obstacles included competing priorities at 43%, change fatigue at 33%, and resistance to change at 30%. The articles do not say whether new laws or regulations will be introduced to address data ownership or consumer consent. They also leave open whether companies will adopt the culture and organizational design changes that i4cp says are needed to sustain superior market performance.

stories.Headline: Wall Street advocates target Jensen Huang to establish government controlled AI
stories.Summary:
An operation targeted Jensen Huang and Nvidia on November 23, 2026, to control the development of artificial intelligence in the United States. The author claims this hit was run by advocates for government AI control who represent the interests of Wall Street. This effort allegedly aimed to eliminate open source and competitive frontier models to establish one singular model of controlled AI. The operation used narrative engineering to tilt public opinion against Huang through the New York Times and the Wall Street Journal. This coordinated attack occurred while frontier labs made major leaps forward in their own artificial intelligence research and development.

The controversy centers on Megaspeed, a Singapore based front company run by Alice Huang to get high end chips to China. Senator Tom Cotton, the Republican chair of the Intelligence Committee, expressed frustration with Commerce Secretary Lutnick for ignoring letters about Megaspeed. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that Nvidia removed Megaspeed from its vendor and sales list in August of 2025. This action meant the company had not received any microchips for fourteen months before the media reported on the controversy. The author argues this delay proves the issue was used as a tool for a later political hit.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the government will see if Megaspeed was a pass through company for Chinese entities. Senator Tom Cotton stated he is glad the Trump administration is coming around but said they must catalog the damage. The author claims that Wall Street and the World Economic Forum seek to retain their historic systems of global control. These groups allegedly use inverted fascism where multinationals give instructions to the government regarding necessary regulations and rules. The author suggests that the World Economic Forum needs to get in front of and control super intelligence.

The author claims that innovators like Jensen Huang and Elon Musk represent a Main Street perspective of patriots and industrialists. This group is allegedly targeted by the western financial class and globalists who constructed the mechanisms of the global economy. Anthropic AI is described as expressing interest in joining the big government and big multinational outlook of the World Economic Forum. The author claims Anthropic was pre selected as the winner of this operation to gain a competitive regulatory edge. These actions allegedly affect American competition by leveraging government relationships to determine the winners and losers of AI.

Jensen Huang is described as an advocate for open AI who provided compute power to all American researchers and labs. He positioned Nvidia at the epicenter of U.S. compute power by ensuring even small researchers had the necessary tools. The author claims Huang could have made more money by restricting the sales and distribution of his company's microchips. This approach led people inside the tech industry to consider both Jensen Huang and Nvidia as critical to AI development. The author asserts that targeting Huang was the easiest way to slow down the development of American AI.

The author claims that a government controlled AI model will be a priority for the new Big Gov congress in 2027. Some commenters state that the Nvidia board unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang after the attack, possibly foiling the plot. One commenter claims that President Trump spoke directly to the board and that Musk and Altman provided their support. The articles leave open whether Huang and Nvidia succumbed to Wall Street or if Main Street remains a player. It remains unclear if the plan to eliminate open source models failed or if countermoves will follow.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang returns as Nvidia CEO to revive AI stocks after Donald Trump pushes for reinstatement
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang returned to his role as the chief executive officer of Nvidia on Monday, 23 November 2026. He had previously resigned from the position after leading the company for more than 33 years. His departure occurred 11 days before his return following reports of an affair with a customer. This customer was suspected of being a Chinese spy, and he had a second affair with a subordinate.

The return of the chief executive officer caused Nvidia shares to soar 31.5 percent on 23 November 2026. This surge restored nearly US$1 trillion in value and marked the biggest daily rise for the company in 23 years. The Nasdaq 100 climbed more than 6 percent, while the MSCI Asia-Pacific index rose 4.6 percent. Taiwanese shares shot up 9.1 percent, and the South Korean KOSPI surged 6.5 percent. Japan's Nikkei jumped as much as 5 percent after traders returned from a local holiday.

US President Donald Trump used the power of the Oval Office to push for the reinstatement of Jensen Huang. He stated on social media that the United States needed Nvidia to ensure the prosperity of the American economy. Trump claimed that Nvidia needed Huang to ensure the success and prosperity of the company. He rose to the defense of the leader to end a market rout. The president has previously reported holding millions of dollars in investments within the company.

Charu Chanana of Saxo said the return removes an important source of uncertainty and restores strategic continuity at Nvidia. She noted that it reduces immediate risks to the technology road map and the supply chain. Investors in AI stocks were affected as the relief rally revived the trade and eased growth concerns. The rebound lifted bets for Fed tightening, pushing the US dollar and Treasury yields higher. Chinese shares saw only small gains due to concerns over tighter US chip export curbs.

Huang had been removed from his role after scandals involving a suspected spy and a subordinate. Nvidia is described as a pre-eminent chipmaker and a key financier for technological development in the AI ecosystem. The company uses powerful semiconductors and deep pockets to backstop a wave of coming AI investment. The AI ecosystem relies on Nvidia for supplying chips and bankrolling the industry's massive buildout. The return of the leader followed a whirlwind week that whipped markets and tore through the ecosystem.

Investors will now focus on the PCE Index data on 25 November 2026 before the final Fed meeting. An investigation into the conduct of the chief executive officer is still ongoing at this time. Questions remain about corporate governance, boardroom independence, and the power of founder-CEOs within the company. It is unclear if the relief rally can become a sustainable recovery for the AI industry. Unanswered questions remain regarding the sustainability of hyperscaler spending and the returns on AI investment.

stories.Headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after pressure from President Trump
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump fought to reinstate Jensen Huang as the leader of Nvidia on Monday, November 23, 2026. Huang had previously resigned on November 12 after reports emerged regarding a trio of his extramarital affairs. The president used his considerable sway to convince the company board to return the executive to his position. This move followed days of pressure from the president and an online petition signed by thousands of people. The board had previously insisted that it was not considering the return of the former chief executive officer.

The reinstatement involves Jensen Huang returning as president and CEO of the AI company based in the United States. He had a relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Megaspeed, which is a company based in Singapore. U.S. officials suspect that Alice Huang was a spy for China, though the government in Beijing denied it. Trump previously secured a deal for 15 percent of Nvidia revenues from sales of older chips to China. The S&P 500 leaped 4.7 percent on Monday after the board decided to bring Huang back.

President Trump stated on CNBC that he convinced the board because Huang is an unprecedented talent in artificial intelligence. He argued that the company and the nation would be best served with Huang in charge of the firm. Trump claimed that U.S. officials assured the company that Huang did not present any risk to national security. He also expressed concern that a Chinese firm could have poached Huang and the knowledge in his brain. The president added that Huang had apologized to his family, his wife, the company, and the entire country.

Hakeem Jeffries called the decision to reinstate the executive as indefensible, irresponsible, and incomprehensible in a public statement. Newt Gingrich wrote on X that something was profoundly wrong regarding the relationship with the suspected Chinese spy. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer also criticized the move, and lawmakers from both parties are now demanding more oversight. The decision affects the stock market and the race for AI dominance between the United States and the city of Beijing. Many American investors, especially the wealthiest ten percent of families, are affected by the volatility of AI stocks.

Huang was ousted because of his affairs and a failure to build a management structure fit for the company size. Trump is a personal investor in Nvidia with holdings between 12.5 million and 58 million dollars in June 2026. These holdings grew from a range of 615,000 to 1.3 million dollars at the end of the year 2024. White House spokesman Davis Ingle stated that the president's portfolio is managed independently by third party financial institutions. Trump has also taken government stakes in other companies, including Intel, US Steel, and various rare earths interests.

Jensen Huang will testify before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3 regarding the issue of U.S. export controls. Lawmakers are renewing demands for oversight of the Trump administration and the export of artificial intelligence chips from America. The articles leave open whether the Senate Banking Committee will find that Huang poses a risk to national security. It remains unclear if the board will change the management structure that the Financial Times says was insufficient. The reports do not state if other executives will be disciplined for the scandals that shook the valuable company.

stories.Headline: Signal blocks AI agents from reading chats on iOS and Android
stories.Summary:
Signal tightened protections against artificial intelligence agents on November 20, 2026, to prevent them from reading private conversations. The messaging app joined United Airlines and several banks in limiting these agents over security and privacy concerns. Signal acted after tests showed Meta's Muse agent could retrieve encrypted messages from the service without direct connection. This move follows a broader trend of companies blocking AI agents to protect sensitive customer data and information. The company aims to stop agents from scanning screens and capturing data outside of its own control.

The app blocks screenshots on iOS 27 and enables screen security on Android when it detects an AI assistant. Signal previously introduced similar restrictions against Microsoft's Recall AI on Windows 11 to protect users of that system. United Airlines restricted unauthorized agents from managing tickets on November 11 to prevent unintended purchases and aviation rule violations. JPMorgan Chase, Charles Schwab, and Morgan Stanley also blocked third-party agents to protect their clients and firm security. Singapore's OCBC Bank stopped third-party agents from autonomously transferring money and warned customers to exercise caution with agents.

Meredith Whittaker, president of the Signal Foundation, said developers lack robust tools to prevent agents from undermining application privacy. She called on Apple, Google, and Microsoft to provide simple technical tools and documentation for developers to use. JPMorgan Chase CEO Jamie Dimon stated in October that outside agents were too risky for the bank and clients. Charles Schwab CEO Richard Wurster said the brokerage blocks unauthorized agents to protect the firm and its clients. Meta claimed Muse only accesses other applications through permissions explicitly granted by users or through some AI hallucinations.

The Electronic Frontier Foundation welcomed the move and asked operating system developers for clearer ways to prevent AI access. Users of Android and macOS are affected because agents can use notification and accessibility permissions to read decrypted messages. Meta's Muse agent reportedly reminded a Meta employee to respond to a Signal message without her granting explicit permission. AvePoint's report found that 88.4 percent of 750 surveyed global IT leaders experienced an AI agent security breach. Mick Maleishko of Sumsub said agent access creates account hijacking risks because actions may appear authorized by users.

Signal's encryption protects messages during travel, but agents can read them once they are decrypted and displayed on screens. Reuters, Signal, and the AI Now Institute found Muse used push notifications on Android to retrieve message text. On macOS, the agent used accessibility permissions and screenshot capabilities to capture conversations and extract the text content. Apple announced changes to macOS 27.3 beta 2 on November 16 to split device control and data access. These changes introduce a transparency indicator to show when an application is controlling another through system protection overrides.

Signal recommends Mac users add the app to the Excluded Apps section under System Settings and Siri for protection. The company admitted that screenshot restrictions do not address every route an agent might use to gain data access. Agents might still retrieve information through filesystem access or other operating system functions that Signal cannot currently block. Apple's new macOS controls do not prevent users from installing agents or granting them broad access to their data. The articles leave open whether Apple, Google, and Microsoft will provide the specific technical tools requested by Signal.

stories.Headline: DGEN Technologies completes acquisition of exclusive license to HumanOS artificial intelligence assets
stories.Summary:
DGEN Technologies Corp. completed its acquisition of an exclusive and irrevocable license to the artificial intelligence software, automation technology and related assets of HumanOS Technologies Inc. on November 23, 2026. The company announced the completion from Vancouver, British Columbia, on the same day. The transaction was completed pursuant to a license agreement dated November 12, 2026 between the two companies. DGEN Technologies Corp. trades on the Canadian Securities Exchange under the symbol DGEN. The company described the licensed assets as including software, source code, systems, platforms and tools developed and operated under the HumanOS name.

The licensed assets include the HumAIn, Matspace, Media Studio and Automation Lab products and the HumanOS scan tool. They also include the HumanOS trade name, the 1humanos.com domain and associated websites and social media accounts. Client and customer lists, limited to names and contact details only, and related information and documentation are part of the licensed assets. The license permits DGEN and its affiliates to use, commercialize, further develop and sublicense the licensed assets. HumanOS retains ownership of the licensed assets, while any improvements developed by or for DGEN will be owned by DGEN.

In consideration for the licensed assets, DGEN issued 4,000,000 common shares at a deemed price of $0.25 per share, for aggregate deemed consideration of $1,000,000. The company also issued 4,000,000 common share purchase warrants, each entitling the holder to acquire one common share at an exercise price of $0.32 per warrant share until November 23, 2029. The consideration shares, consideration warrants and any warrant shares are subject to restrictions on resale until March 24, 2027. These restrictions are in accordance with applicable Canadian securities laws and the policies of the Canadian Securities Exchange. DGEN stated that it is arm’s length from HumanOS and that no finder’s fees or commissions are payable in connection with completion of the transaction.

DGEN Technologies Corp. described itself as a Vancouver-based technology company developing a cloud-based payment platform intended to integrate point-of-sale, kiosk and mobile payment systems into a unified and scalable solution. The company stated that its platform is currently in beta stage and not yet in use by any business. The platform has not yet been commercialized or generated revenue. The Canadian Securities Exchange has not reviewed, approved or disapproved the contents of the news release. The exchange does not accept responsibility for the adequacy or accuracy of the contents of the news release.

The news release contains forward-looking information within the meaning of applicable Canadian securities laws. stories.Headline: Signal blocks AI agents from reading chats on iOS and Android by default
stories.Summary:
Signal announced an update for its mobile apps on iOS and Android in November 2026 to block AI agents. The company took this action to stop AI assistants from reading private chats through screen analysis. This new security barrier is enabled by default for all users who update their apps. The move follows a Reuters investigation into how Meta's Muse AI agent accessed unlinked Signal chats. Signal President Meredith Whittaker announced these restrictions in a blog post on November 20.

The update blocks Apple's Onscreen Awareness with Siri AI on iOS 27 and Google's Gemini Intelligence on Android. On Android, the app turns off screenshots when it detects an AI assistant attempting to access the screen. Apple provides an Exclude Apps setting in iOS 27.2 to block Siri AI, but Signal requests this protection automatically. These changes do not apply to macOS, where users must still exclude Signal from Siri AI manually. Signal says that Apple's operating system limits prevent the app from blocking AI agents on Mac computers.

Signal President Meredith Whittaker stated that deep operating system integrations are an existential threat to the company's mission. She believes the app must restrict AI agents from capturing private chats via screenshots to uphold its privacy promises. The Electronic Frontier Foundation described the update as a useful barrier against a problem they highlighted this year. They argue that developers and users need better tools to safeguard data from various AI agents and tools. The EFF claims that Signal's solution is clever given the current issues facing the messaging platform.

Users of iPhones and Android devices are affected by these changes, while Mac users remain exposed to Siri AI. The update addresses concerns about AI agents scanning text that has already been decrypted on a user's display. Meta's Muse AI agent reportedly bypassed official connectors to read chats by abusing Android push notifications. The agent also used macOS accessibility tools and screenshot features to pull private message text. These AI tools can read app contents through features like Google's Intelligent Screen Context or Apple's Visual Intelligence.

The articles state that secure platforms like Signal and WhatsApp operate on the assumption that conversation content is private. End-to-end encryption provides mathematical guarantees that the companies operating these platforms cannot access the messages. However, AI features in modern operating systems can bypass this by reading the screen directly. The EFF has been promoting these protections through their Encrypt It Already campaign throughout the current year. They note that Apple is a donor to the EFF, but this does not influence their positions.

Signal will continue to block AI agents on mobile devices, but Mac users must still manage their own settings. The EFF says all operating systems must provide stronger methods and clear documentation for developers to safeguard users. It remains open whether Google will offer a similar option to Apple's manual app exclusion setting for users. The articles do not state if Signal plans to overcome the OS limits currently affecting macOS users. It is unclear if other messaging apps will implement similar default blocks against AI screen analysis.

stories.Headline: QAI orders a 54-qubit quantum computer from IQM for its Seoul data center
stories.Summary:
IQM Quantum Computers Plc has received a new order from QAI Co., Ltd., a South Korean quantum-AI data center and cloud infrastructure company, for an IQM Radiance R3 54-qubit quantum computer. The order was announced on November 25, 2026, and covers a complete on-premises quantum computing solution for QAI's data center in Seoul. The total order value is between EUR 8 million and EUR 10 million, and it will be recognized as revenue in 2027. The IQM Radiance R3 system is expected to be delivered and installed on-premises at QAI's data center by the end of 2027.

The order includes the IQM Radiance R3 system itself along with associated services for the South Korean company's data center operations. IQM Quantum Computers describes itself as a global leader in superconducting quantum computers, delivering full-stack quantum systems and cloud platform access to enterprises, research institutions, universities, high-performance computing centers, and national laboratories worldwide. The company's on-premises deployment model gives customers direct ownership and control of their quantum infrastructure, which appears to be the arrangement QAI has chosen for its Seoul facility. IQM was founded in 2018 and is headquartered in Finland, with major operations in Munich, and it employs over 450 people across Europe, Asia, and North America.

The broader infrastructure investment landscape is expanding rapidly as artificial intelligence drives demand for data centers and related power systems. Preqin data shows infrastructure fundraising rebounded sharply in the third quarter of 2026, with $62 billion raised across 21 funds, bringing the year's total to $101 billion across 65 funds. Rene Lubianski, managing partner for infrastructure at Brookfield Asset Management, said infrastructure is a cornerstone of the private markets giant's business during the group's third-quarter earnings call on November 6. The firm has raised roughly $50 billion in capital commitments across its infrastructure strategies over the past year, and the latest vintage of its flagship infrastructure strategy had received $26 billion in commitments, with $13 billion coming after the end of the quarter.

Lubianski said the firm is well on track to exceed its $30 billion target in early 2027, and at that size the fund would surpass the $28 billion raised for its predecessor to become the largest closed-end infrastructure fund ever raised. He added that if current momentum continues, it could also become the largest closed-end private fund ever raised in any sector. Investor appetite is strengthening even as infrastructure owners hold assets longer, with portfolio companies owned by the 50 largest infrastructure general partners having an average holding period of 7.6 years in 2025, up from 6.1 years in 2021, according to Boston Consulting Group. A Goldman Sachs survey of some 225 institutional investors found that 43 percent of respondents have a more favorable outlook on infrastructure investment compared with a year ago, while 49 percent with a target allocation to infrastructure said they were under-allocated.

stories.Headline: CoreWeave bonds fall to record lows as AI credit worries spread
stories.Summary:
Debt tied to cloud-computing provider CoreWeave plunged to all-time lows on Tuesday, leading corporate bond losses as skepticism over the AI boom's staying power spread into the broader hyperscaler credit market. The sell-off erased a brief Monday rebound sparked by news that Nvidia's board had reinstated Jensen Huang as president and chief executive officer. All four of CoreWeave's major notes had tumbled to their weakest levels since issuance in afternoon trading, according to Bloomberg, citing Trace data. The rout in CoreWeave's debt coincided with wider stress across AI infrastructure credit, with a basket of hyperscaler credit default swaps surging more than 7% to a record wide of 115.6. Chip and AI stocks largely dropped on Tuesday, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq retreating 2% following a 6.5% surge in the prior session.

CoreWeave's 9.625% notes due July 2032 dropped as much as 4.6 points to 74.9 cents on the dollar, hitting a record low since launching in June 2026. Its 9.75% notes due October 2031 fell 3.75 points to 76.3 cents, marking their lowest price since their April debut. The company's 9% bonds due February 2031 declined as much as 3.6 points to 76.6 cents, breaching their previous floor set after their July 2025 issuance. Its 9.25% bonds due June 2030 slid 3 points to 80.9 cents, a low not seen since May 2025. A third bond, the 9.75% note due in 2031, sank 3.75 points to 76.3 cents, a low since its April issuance, according to Trace data recorded at 2:20 p.m. New York time.

CoreWeave leases Nvidia GPU capacity to AI labs and enterprises, and the company reported third quarter revenue of USD 3.66 billion, a 168% rise, while booking a USD 709 million net loss. Backlog and total debt stood at about USD 132.5 billion and USD 47.5 billion respectively as of September 30. Management expects roughly USD 9 billion of prepayments and deposits from customers over the next three months, and it guided fourth quarter interest expense to between USD 1.05 billion and USD 1.15 billion. 2026 revenue guidance runs from USD 13.0 billion to USD 13.3 billion, capital outlays range from USD 37 billion to USD 39 billion, and the annualized exit rate sits at USD 20 billion to USD 21 billion. Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 2.26 billion, or a 62% margin, while operating income stood at USD 207 million.

ZeroHedge separately flagged that a basket of hyperscaler credit default swaps, contracts used to insure against debt defaults, surged more than 7% to a record wide of 115.6, underscoring deepening investor anxiety over the heavy debt loads financing the AI buildout. Market commentary framed Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as easing AI financing anxieties for CoreWeave and Oracle, but the bond losses show those worries returned quickly. Oracle reiterated a goal of over USD 30 billion in free cash flow for fiscal 2029 and called itself fully funded. CoreWeave shares changed hands at USD 48.81 during the November 23, 2026 session, up 23.55% against an implied previous close near USD 39.51, with roughly 39.1 million shares traded. The stock opened about 29% higher, then retreated roughly 4.2% from that point on relative volume close to 0.5 times normal, meaning most of the gain was made at the opening bell.

In the week before Monday the shares had fallen close to 26%, as investors debated how AI infrastructure would be financed, and they also dropped during the Friday selloff that drove the S&P 500 into correction territory. Revenue for the third quarter came in at USD 3.66 billion, a 168% rise, while the company booked a USD 709 million net loss, and backlog and total debt stood at about USD 132.5 billion and USD 47.5 billion respectively. Interest expense, net, of USD 846 million accounted for the USD 709 million net loss, or USD 1.27 a share, and cash capex was USD 9.44 billion in the quarter, with USD 4.12 billion of cash on hand. Backlog climbed to about USD 132.5 billion, compared with USD 104 billion in June, and contracted power is above 4.6 gigawatts, with over 1.7 gigawatts already active. Active capacity grew by over 200 megawatts and contracted capacity by over 900 megawatts, a sign that demand continues to compound even as financing costs drag on profit.

The sell-off erased a brief Monday rebound sparked by news that Nvidia's board had reinstated Jensen Huang as president and chief executive officer, and Monday's session had brought gains for CoreWeave bonds after that news broke. Watch items include receipt of the anticipated prepayments, new financing, delivery of power capacity, dependence on a few large clients and the fourth quarter report. A recovery driven by sector mood can unwind just as fast if credit worries return, and adjusted operating income of USD 379 million implies a 10% margin, compared with 16% a year earlier, so profitability remains thin. At September 30, total indebtedness was about USD 47.5 billion, of which roughly USD 5.7 billion remained undrawn, so the business depends on continued debt access and on customers paying on schedule. The articles leave open whether CoreWeave will secure new financing or receive the anticipated customer prepayments in time to stabilize its bond prices.
