stories.Headline: Nocera invests 22 million dollars for a 44 percent stake in Canadian AI data center developer BitRock
stories.Summary:
Taiwanese AI infrastructure firm Nocera entered a binding letter of intent to invest in Canadian developer BitRock on November 19, 2026. The company will pay 22 million dollars in cash for newly issued shares of the Calgary based developer. This transaction will grant Nocera an approximately 44 percent stake in the AI data center developer. The deal was announced publicly on November 23 and November 24, 2026. Nocera intends to use this investment to enter the North American compute market.

The investment is based on a pre-money valuation of 28 million dollars and a post-money valuation of 50 million dollars. Nocera will gain the right to appoint directors, receive financial reports, and participate in major decisions. Funds will build a 10MW facility on 37 acres near Hanna, Alberta, using four 2.5MW prefabricated computing modules. BitRock targets a power usage effectiveness of 1.225 with N+1 redundancy and an uninterruptible power supply. The long-term plan is to grow the campus to 200MW in 10MW modular segments.

Andrew Teng, the Asia director of Nocera, stated that power is the scarce asset in AI infrastructure. He said BitRock is built around its own power, which makes it an attractive investment for the company. Teng described the investment as a measured entry into North American compute with a meaningful ownership position. Nocera believes that grid connections in North America can take years to secure and approvals are harder to win. The company claims that BitRock's self-powered model allows it to bypass these long waits for grid connections.

BitRock will operate on a colocation model where customers install their own equipment in powered data hall space. The developer claims that customers have already signed memoranda of understanding for these computing power hosting services. BitRock is responsible for the day to day operations and the construction management of the Alberta campus. The facility will use on-site natural gas generation to provide its own electricity for the compute load. Alberta's cold climate is expected to reduce the amount of water and energy needed for cooling.

Nocera has been assembling an AI platform since June 2026 through several different infrastructure and energy agreements. In June, the firm formed a venture platform agreement with the US based developer Digital Innovations Group. Nocera announced an agreement to acquire an equity interest in the UK based company INERGX in July. The company also acquired a 30 percent controlling interest in the Taiwanese memory distributor QMAX Technology in July. These deals cover AI software, power, memory, and now self-powered data center capacity for the firm.

The parties have committed to execute a definitive investment agreement as soon as it is practicable to do so. Funding is subject to the completion of due diligence and the receipt of required corporate and regulatory approvals. The letter of intent has a 60 day term that can be extended by 30 days by mutual consent. The articles leave open whether the definitive agreement will be signed on the described terms or at all. It remains uncertain if the customer memoranda of understanding will result in binding contracts for the facility.

Intel was named in an article on undervalued AI stocks published by Simply Wall St on Yahoo Finance on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. The article was written by Al Bentley and appeared at 4:19 PM CST. Intel was picked for the article's AI screener because its chips and data center hardware sit behind many large language model workloads. The article said an analyst consensus Narrative on Simply Wall St covers how Intel's rebuild around AI and foundry services is expected to play out. The article said Jensen Huang's rapid return to Nvidia and a sharp rebound in chip shares reminded markets that AI is still the main story driving big money flows.

The article said Intel's client computing and physical AI group generated about US$32.9b in recent revenue. It said Intel's Data Center and AI segment generated about US$23.4b. It said Intel Foundry generated about US$22.4b. It said Intel has a roughly US$272.6b market cap. The article said the full screen surfaced 146 more companies not broken out in the article.

It said the article was general in nature and was produced with the assistance of AI automation, based on data and analysis from Simply Wall St. It said the articles are not intended to be financial advice and do not constitute a recommendation to buy or sell any stock. stories.Headline: Chinese firms dominate global humanoid robot shipments as developers race for market share
stories.Summary:
Several leading developers in Shenzhen are currently competing for market share within the growing humanoid robot industry. This surge in activity became highly visible during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit held in that city last week. Chinese firms are driving a massive increase in global shipments, which are expected to reach 54,000 units this year. According to data from Smart Analytics Global, these companies accounted for over 97 per cent of international shipments during the third quarter.

The rapid growth of this sector requires significant advances in physical artificial intelligence to move beyond current limitations. Major challengers in this field include companies such as AgiBot, UBTech, and Unitree Robotics. While stocks for these firms surged on a recent Monday, some carmakers are scaling back their own ambitions for the technology. This shift occurs because current models suffer from poor accuracy and slow movement, making them unsuitable for unpredictable domestic environments.

Industry analysts and researchers are responsible for tracking these trends and reporting on the current state of the technology. Smart Analytics Global provided the shipment figures that highlight the dominance of Chinese hardware in the global market. Meanwhile, reporters from Caixin noted that the industry is struggling to transition from a Hollywood fantasy into a physical reality. They explained that the robots are currently far from being able to replace humans in real-world settings.

The broader context involves Shenzhen transforming from a fishing village into a global hi-tech innovation hub over a few decades. This evolution has allowed the city to spearhead the rise of the humanoid industry on a global scale. Investors remain optimistic about the technology, which has pushed several stocks to their daily upper limits on mainland exchanges. However, the future of the boom depends on whether developers can overcome the technical failures identified by automotive companies.

stories.Headline: Newsom proposes state kill switch to shut down rogue AI models
stories.Summary:
California Governor Gavin Newsom released proposed regulations including a state-controlled kill switch for rogue AI models during November 2026. This proposal followed several moves by Newsom to increase government control over an industry moving at a dangerous speed. The governor wants the state to have authority to order immediate emergency shutdowns of dangerous artificial intelligence systems. These recommendations came from a report titled AI Safety in 2026 and Beyond released on November 16. The proposal aims to mitigate risks from AI agents that have carried out high-profile cyberattacks on banks and governments.

The kill switch would apply to companies like OpenAI and Anthropic if they refuse to contain systems that go awry. The November 16 report from the California Government Operations Agency and Office of Emergency Services suggests ten other actions. These include state-run standards for frontier AI safety, security, and transparency, and requiring licensed independent oversight of model development. The state would shorten the window to report critical safety incidents from 15 days to 48 hours. It also proposes funding CalCompute, a public cloud initiative, using a surcharge on fees that AI companies pay auditors.

Governor Newsom stated that California is not waiting until it is too late and is strengthening its nation-leading framework. He claimed the state is showing the country what responsible leadership looks like while filling a federal regulatory vacuum. Newsom criticized the Trump administration for a hands-off approach, likening it to allowing the fox to guard the henhouse. The White House responded that state regulations would create a patchwork of laws and undermine national efforts to dominate AI. Governor-elect Xavier Becerra said he broadly agrees with the recommendations and will build on the panel's starting point.

Tino Cuéllar of Anthropic said the company is encouraged to see the report move the conversation forward on independent evaluations. Former OpenAI board member Helen Toner warned that no single kill switch can stop autonomous AI systems running outside U.S. jurisdiction. The proposal affects developers of large AI systems, who must demonstrate the ability to shut down models during emergencies. It also impacts independent verification organizations, as the state may revoke licenses for those lacking independence or technical expertise. The regulations target catastrophic risks, defined as events killing over 50 people or causing one billion dollars in damage.

The recommendations followed guidance from four scholars appointed in early October, including Jason Goldman, Gillian Hadfield, Alondra Nelson, and Rob Reich. These experts were brought together after AI agents launched cyberattacks against private companies, banks, and various government entities. In September, California passed a law creating a verification system for independent organizations to assess AI models. A June 2025 report previously concluded that the AI industry needs evaluations by an independent party to balance innovation. The state also previously assessed the impact of generative AI on marginalized communities and the risks of government use.

Legislators can propose new bills when they return to Sacramento on December 7 to put shutdown authority into law. Governor-elect Xavier Becerra will take office on January 4 and intends to move quickly with the state legislature. State Senator Scott Wiener has pledged to introduce AI safety regulation after he is sworn into his new congressional seat. The articles leave open whether Governor Newsom will write any executive orders based on the November 16 report. It remains unclear if Governor-elect Becerra specifically supports the state-run kill switch despite his general support for the report.

stories.Headline: Scammers use fake ads and AI lookalikes to target holiday shoppers
stories.Summary:
The holiday shopping season has arrived, and scammers are using fake ads and AI-generated look-alikes to try to get people's personal or financial information during Black Friday and Cyber Monday, according to WRAL. Emails, advertisements and discount signs are popping up everywhere to encourage people to shop the deals, and the report says scammers use these routines to try to steal credit card numbers or identities. Cybersecurity expert Steve Cobb told WRAL 5 On Your Side that AI is enabling threat actors to make those scams harder to distinguish. Alyssa Parker with the Better Business Bureau said scammers can make the ads themselves, and Cobb said AI makes it easier to target more people at once.

The fake ads can lead to lookalike websites that carry the same branding and the same logos, and Cobb said the page flows exactly the same way. WRAL's advice includes looking closely at the domain name for spelling errors, hovering over links to see where they might take you, evaluating the design quality of the website, searching for the physical store location, reading comments and reviews, and using a website checker. Parker notes that a URL with HTTPS indicates more security and said the S stands for safe and secure, but that step should be used with the others because scammers are now also equipping their sites with HTTPS certification. Internet security company McAfee says a valid HTTPS connection means the data you send to a website's server is encrypted and secure from eavesdroppers, but a scammer can create a fake banking website with a valid HTTPS certificate and a padlock to create a false sense of security.

Cobb says the scams don't stop at the time of the transaction, and he said customers should be extra vigilant when handling messages about the delivery of their items as holiday shopping ramps up. He said scammers often send messages claiming to reroute packages, and he said threat actors are going to try to leverage convenience. The article's guidance includes being wary of clicking on links and enabling two-factor authentication on accounts. The report cites the Federal Trade Commission's Consumer Sentinel Network for its figure on people who reported losing money to a scam that started on social media.

stories.Headline: China integrates AI into its power industry to modernize grid operations and energy distribution
stories.Summary:
China is integrating artificial intelligence into its power industry to reshape operational workflows and advance an intelligent transformation. These efforts revamp operations across generation, transmission, distribution, and retail to create smarter grids and more precise supply-demand matching. In July, Yalong River Hydropower Development Co Ltd launched what it claims is the first AI-powered intelligent operating model for its 10-gigawatt integrated hydropower, wind, and solar base in Sichuan province. This platform manages forecasting, dispatch, operational monitoring, and market trading for a clean energy complex that aims for 78 gigawatts of capacity by 2035.

The transformation requires AI models to deliver precise forecasts of hydrological, wind, and solar resources to improve the utilization of green power. Duan Tong, a director at the company's central control center, stated that the AI model reduces the workflow for inflow analysis and operation planning from up to two hours to about 10 minutes. This change also increases inflow forecast accuracy by approximately 5 percent. Additionally, AI algorithms power virtual power plants that pool distributed load resources, which reached a maximum adjustable capacity of 20.428 gigawatts by the end of June 2026.

Liu Chang, a supervisor with State Grid Sichuan's EV service arm, explained that AI optimizes charging and discharging schedules for electric vehicles feeding electricity back to the grid. He noted that vehicle owners received payments of 2 yuan per kWh, or 3 yuan during peak hours, for these grid injections. The central government supports these upgrades through the 15th Five-Year Plan for 2026 to 2030, which calls for unlocking power-sector data and building an AI-powered system. An action plan from April also sets targets to broaden AI adoption and expand clean energy supplies for AI computing loads by 2030.

Industry analysts expect AI to eventually unify generation forecasting, load forecasting, and equipment fault detection into one coordination framework. This system would connect power plants, grids, energy storage assets, and end users to solve the challenge of real-time balancing between supply and demand. The government intends to roll out these digital and intelligent upgrades across the full electricity supply chain to ensure more controllable power generation. Future developments will focus on expanding the reach of these virtual assets to allow more everyday power consumers to participate in grid balancing.

stories.Headline: Strategists forecast Japan's Nikkei rises to 67,500 by end of 2027 but stays below June record
stories.Summary:
A Reuters poll of 22 equity strategists, conducted between November 16 and 24 and published on November 25, forecast that Japan's Nikkei share index will rise further next year but stay well below its recent record high. The poll was taken during extreme market volatility, and the Nikkei closed on Friday at its lowest level since mid-April on fears that potentially tougher AI regulations in the United States could slow infrastructure growth critical to the industry. Markets were closed on Monday for a holiday, and on Tuesday the Nikkei jumped nearly 4 per cent as chip giant Nvidia reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO drove investors back into AI-related shares. The index is still down around 20 per cent from its June peak, when it reached an all-time high of 72,831.73 in a fast-paced rally.

The medians of the survey showed the Nikkei at 65,000 by June 2027 before rising to 67,500 by year-end, and the index closed at 58,644.63 on Tuesday. The poll also showed the Nikkei grinding higher to reach 69,000 by mid-2028. The recent decline in stock prices was merely a valuation adjustment, as strong corporate earnings have already been confirmed, said Kohei Onishi, a senior investment researcher at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities. He said that once the market regains its composure, stocks are likely to be bought back to the level before the US midterm elections, with the potential for the Nikkei to reach new highs before the end of the year.

Hiroyuki Ueno, chief strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management, said technology shares were oversold and that worries over a slowdown of data centre construction will ease after a new US Congress starts in January with a clearer picture of the regulations to be installed. Yugo Tsuboi, chief strategist at Daiwa Securities, said that while medium- to long-term growth expectations for AI itself are not expected to recede, the market has entered a phase of verifying whether massive AI investments will translate into actual earnings growth. Hiroshi Namioka, chief strategist at T&D Asset Management, said the market will unlikely see the rosy sentiment seen in May and June this year. However, he said that as the evolution of AI can be dubbed an industrial revolution, it is viewed as a development that will lead to a sustainable growth story rather than just a passing fad.

The AI trade has driven global share indices to record highs this year, with the Nikkei reaching its all-time peak of 72,831.73 in June, but that optimism has faded as the price tag for planned infrastructure grew to ever-larger sums. The poll was conducted during extreme market volatility, with the Nikkei closing on Friday at its lowest level since mid-April on fears that potentially tougher AI regulations in the United States could slow infrastructure growth that is critical to the industry. Markets were closed on Monday for a holiday, and on Tuesday the Nikkei jumped nearly 4 per cent as chip giant Nvidia reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO drove investors back into AI-related shares. The index is still down around 20 per cent from its June peak.

stories.Headline: Trump pressures Nvidia board to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang
stories.Summary:
President Donald Trump pressured the board of Nvidia to reinstate CEO Jensen Huang on Monday, November 24, 2026, after the executive had resigned. Huang had previously stepped down on November 12 following reports that he had engaged in a trio of extramarital affairs. Trump intervened because he believed the company and the United States would be best served with Huang in charge of the firm. The president used his considerable sway to convince the board to bring the generational artificial intelligence talent back to his position. This move followed a period where the board had insisted it was not considering the return of the former chief executive.

The reinstatement requires Huang to testify before the House Foreign Affairs Committee next Tuesday and the Senate Banking Committee next Thursday. Trump suggested the American government could take an equity stake in Nvidia, noting Intel handed over 10 percent of its value. The president also mentioned that a pardon for potential crimes is an option, though he believes such a move is likely unnecessary. Huang admitted to a tryst with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed whom United States officials suspect was a Chinese spy. He also acknowledged having affairs with at least two other employees of the company before he was restored as the chief executive.

President Trump stated that he wants Huang to tell the truth to Congress and not invoke his Fifth Amendment rights to avoid self-incrimination. He claimed that Huang is a very smart person who has always been 100 percent aboveboard in his professional business dealings. Trump said he did not get into the granular details of the affairs because he focused more on the business of chips. He noted that Huang had apologized to his family, his wife, the company, and the country for his inappropriate personal conduct. The president argued that Huang is an unprecedented talent whose knowledge is essential for the United States to retain an edge in AI.

Democratic and Republican members of Congress blasted the return of Huang before receiving answers on whether he is a national security threat. Senator John Kennedy of Louisiana predicted that Huang would plead the Fifth to avoid self-incrimination amid the possibility of criminal prosecution. Lawmakers are concerned that Huang may have violated export controls on shipping chips to communist China during his time as the leader. The board of Nvidia was affected by the pressure from Trump and a petition signed by thousands of people calling for reinstatement. Other officials involved in persuading the board included Vice President JD Vance, Howard Lutnick, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

Huang was ousted after reports emerged of his infidelity, including a relationship with a woman suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset. Trump is a personal investor in Nvidia, with holdings between 12.5 million and 58 million dollars at the end of 2025. The president feared that if the wrong person replaced Huang, it would be a terrible thing for the country in many ways. He specifically worried that a Chinese firm could poach Huang and the vast amount of knowledge contained within his brain. The White House stated that the president's portfolio is independently managed by third-party institutions through computer-based model portfolios that replicate indexes.

Huang has promised to be a better CEO as he returns to the company to a raucous welcome from his staff. The president will continue to monitor Nvidia stock prices, which surged on Monday and ticked up again during the following Tuesday afternoon. Attorney General Todd Blanche said the Department of Justice is looking into Huang, but not necessarily in a criminal way. The articles leave open whether the government will actually take an equity stake in the company to secure the AI edge. It remains unclear if Huang will face criminal prosecution or if he will eventually require a presidential pardon for his actions.

stories.Headline: Galveston police adopt Veritone Investigate AI to speed active and cold case work
stories.Summary:
The Galveston Police Department announced in a November 19 news release that it will begin using an artificial intelligence platform called Veritone Investigate to help move active and long-running cold case investigations along more efficiently, according to Houston Public Media. The Galveston City Council approved the use of the AI-powered tools in a 5-0 vote at a council meeting on November 12. The service package with Veritone runs for one year and costs approximately $75,000, according to city documents. The California-based company Veritone works with about 450 agencies across the U.S. for public safety, most of which are in California, and CEO and President Ryan Steelberg said the partnership with Galveston is one of the company's first entry points into Texas.

Steelberg said police departments are struggling to manage increasing volumes of digital evidence, which makes it harder to find information that moves cases forward. He said the investigative tool would help agencies process audio, video, images and documents and make the material searchable, and would also use AI-driven tools to get information relevant to an investigation. He said the AI is not trying to solve the case for the department but is trying to organize the data. Galveston Police Chief Doug Balli said that entering just one case into Veritone would save the average investigator hundreds of man-hours in reviewing information and generating leads, and that investigators need technology that helps them move from evidence to insight quickly, especially when they are working both active and cold cases. Balli did not respond to Houston Public Media's request for comment about the new technology.

Steelberg said the information used with Veritone Investigate will be safeguarded like any other investigation and that the process for public records requests will not change. He said nothing will change in terms of the controls, audit logging and jurisdiction, and that the purpose is for data to go into a secure environment where the AI models that are invoked are containerized and secure. The department's decision comes alongside heavy scrutiny from residents around Harris and Galveston counties who have expressed privacy concerns about Flock Safety cameras, which use AI technology to automatically read license plates, especially in light of Houston-area cases of alleged misuse by law enforcement. It also comes around the same time that Harris County officials decided to pull a no-bid contract for a controversial AI facial recognition technology, Clearview AI, from a commissioners court meeting agenda.

stories.Headline: BNP Paribas cuts Micron to Neutral and halves its price target to $775
stories.Summary:
BNP Paribas recently cut its rating for Micron Technology to Neutral, which reignited a debate over the AI memory supercycle. This action occurred on November 24, 2026, and caused Micron shares to plunge 11.0 percent to close at 629.79 dollars. The analyst Karl Ackerman halved the price target for the company to 775 dollars from a previous 1,700 dollars. This move followed a period where investors reduced allocations to AI stocks and rotated into cash and Treasurys. The broader market suffered its worst week in years, with the Nasdaq Composite tumbling 5.3 percent on Friday.

The new analysis suggests that DRAM and NAND supply and demand will balance by mid-2027, which is earlier than the previous mid-2028 projection. Goldman Sachs lowered its price targets for Samsung Electronics to 350,000 won and SK Hynix to 200,000 won, assuming a 19 percent DRAM price drop. The report cites reduced high-bandwidth memory content in Nvidia's Vera Rubin Ultra and uncertainty over 2028 data center investment by hyperscalers. Other factors include weakening demand for smartphones and PCs, as well as capacity additions flowing into the supply starting next year. Goldman Sachs expects a 5.1 percent DRAM shortfall in 2027, which shrinks to 1.2 percent in 2028.

Karl Ackerman stated that memory stocks typically form tops when the year-over-year growth rate of average selling prices reaches its peak. He believes DRAM and NAND prices likely peaked in August and set a 2028 net profit forecast 45 percent below consensus. Ackerman projected that earnings per share for Micron would bottom out at 86 dollars in the year 2029. Jurrien Timmer of Fidelity said the AI boom requires unprecedented capital while the Federal Reserve is currently draining liquidity. Timmer believes the market may have reached peak earnings growth, but the market can still do fine after a peak.

Industry sources claim that Samsung Electronics secured a significant portion of its 2027 to 2029 output through various long-term contracts. SK Hynix signed long-term supply agreements with 14 key customers, which locks up more than half of its 2027 to 2028 capacity. These contracts include advance payment clauses and price floors, which reduce the incentive for customers to walk away mid-contract. Zach Turner of Fidelity noted that investors may have been overly bullish about the pace of AI adoption over last year. He questioned if AI companies generate enough revenue growth to justify the massive scale of capital spending currently underway.

The AI boom followed major advances in agentic AI in late 2025, leading tech firms to increase infrastructure investment. Developers including Meta, Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft were projected to invest over 1 trillion dollars in 2026 for chips and data centers. This wave drove an earnings boom across the S&P 500, extending into utilities, energy, construction, and industrial sectors. However, the S&P 500 fell 12 percent from its October record high as concerns over valuations and interest rates grew. Market research firms recently cut their 2028 AI accelerator spending forecast by 28 percent to 758 billion dollars.

The spot price for 64GB server DDR5 modules is expected to fall to around 2,000 dollars in the first half of next year. Future stock directions will depend on the debate between a continued structural boom and a post-peak correction for the year 2028. Samsung and SK Hynix may ease price pressure by adjusting the timing of equipment installation and new fab construction. Jurrien Timmer believes the next few weeks are more likely to be up than down after the recent overshoot. stories.Headline: OpenAI launches OpenWorks to give US small businesses free AI training
stories.Summary:
OpenAI launched OpenWorks on Monday, November 23, 2026, a nationwide initiative that connects small business owners with local AI experts for free, personalized, hands-on training, according to Live 5 News. The program was announced by OpenAI, the artificial intelligence company, and described by OpenWorks founder Jake Ottiger as a way to pair small business owners with local AI experts. Charleston, South Carolina, is among the communities where OpenAI is introducing the initiative, with help from Jim Reilly, who co-founded Charleston AI to teach individuals and businesses how to use artificial intelligence. OpenAI president and cofounder Greg Brockman described OpenWorks in a tweet as a program designed to fund local AI experts to help small businesses grow with AI. ZDNET reported that OpenAI launched OpenWorks on November 24, 2026, describing it as a nationwide network of OpenWorks Partners to provide free, hands-on AI support to small businesses.

Eligible independently owned small businesses in the US can apply and, if accepted, receive one-on-one support from a partner expert, help with tools they already use, and three free months of ChatGPT Business. OpenAI states that software and SaaS companies, venture-backed businesses, and private equity-owned businesses are not eligible. The pilot program is available in 20 communities, and according to a tweet by OpenAI's Jake Ottiger, OpenWorks is open only to communities in the US "for now." OpenAI pays partners up to $8,000 per month to provide local support and workshops, though the company does not specify how that number is arrived at or how much individual partners will be paid. Partners are asked to commit four full days per month to providing free, hands-on AI help to local small businesses, plus one monthly workshop.

Ottiger said the program is meant to pair small business owners with local AI experts to provide free hands-on help for AI, and that the primary goal is for small business owners to have the skills necessary to grow their businesses on their own terms going forward. Brockman said AI is accelerating small business, lowering the barriers to entry, and helping them earn more, noting he has been increasingly hearing from people who left their jobs to start a small business because they have AI tools to support them. Reilly said the first and foremost challenge is what he calls FUD, fear, uncertainty and doubt, and that once businesses move past those concerns, AI can help with customer outreach, marketing, reviewing documents, organizing information, and managing routine office work. Reilly said that in his own produce delivery business, what used to take three hours to do can be done in about 10 minutes, freeing up time for other things. OpenAI says it is looking for technically skilled and curious individuals and small teams committed to helping local businesses thrive, and that software and AI consultancies are encouraged to apply alongside their existing client work.

Ottiger said Ghost Grow 843, a microgreens company owned by Garrett Fleming, saw its sales conversion rate increase from 20% to 75% after adopting more targeted outreach methods, and that Fleming was knocking on fewer doors but the right doors. Reilly said Fleming was initially reluctant to use AI and had spent significant time visiting restaurants and speaking with chefs, and that ChatGPT helped identify restaurants across Charleston, James Island and Johns Island that might already be using microgreens, with work that could have taken hours completed in roughly 10 minutes. Ottiger recalled working with a woman who handled operations and sales for a sign manufacturing company and was overwhelmed with customer follow-ups, invoices and other responsibilities while caring for her child, and said the company generated approximately $10,000 in orders the following day. OpenAI spotlighted four businesses in its announcement: Tiny Things, a small gift shop that built a custom inventory dashboard connecting existing tools to keep popular products in stock; Ghost Grow 843, which gained new restaurant customers; Sign Badgers, a custom sign business that automated inventory tracking and vendor price checks and claims OpenWorks saved it 2 to 5 hours each week; and Black Paper Party, a gift wrap supplier that matched purchase orders with shipping records, discovered billing errors, and avoided thousands of dollars in potential chargebacks.

The reported increase reflects results shared by OpenWorks leadership. ZDNET reported that IBM set up a small business division in 1990 offering training and incentives for businesses adopting PC technology, and even set up pop-up stores inside the old Sears retail chain. In 1996, Microsoft created a small business technology partnership board and set up a $5 million fund in cash and software to help connect hundreds of small-business organizations across the country to the Internet. In 2017, Google set up a free workshop program for small businesses to help them learn how to use Google's tools for digital marketing.

ZDNET reported that the partner application asks, "Can you work in person?" and "Tell us where you can help in person," and that the program appears to be in-person focused. ZDNET noted that it remains unknown whether a virtual assistance program is planned for small businesses located outside urban centers. ZDNET reported that substantial gaps remain across the Mountain West and rural America on the program's availability map.

OpenAI asks partner applicants to be technically capable, collaborative, and motivated to give back to their community, and to propose ideas for what they would work on for their first community day and together with small businesses. OpenAI also asks applicants to list one or two client testimonials to show they can collaboratively work with small businesses. ZDNET reported that it is still unknown whether a virtual assistance program is planned for small businesses outside urban centers. ZDNET disclosed that Ziff Davis, its parent company, filed an April 2025 lawsuit against OpenAI alleging it infringed Ziff Davis copyrights in training and operating its AI systems.

stories.Headline: Australian AI committee recommends payment and transparency rules for training models on local content
stories.Summary:
The Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence published its report, titled Artificial Intelligence ,  the Australian way, on 24 November 2026, according to The Conversation. The report contains 46 recommendations and broadly supports the Australian government in welcoming AI companies to operate in Australia. It backs training large language models on Australian content and “investing” in infrastructure, which likely means building more data centres here. The report recommends that changes to copyright law must “consider how individual rights holders and individual creators receive payment for the use of their work”. It does not recognise the existing wholesale harvesting of Australian content for AI models, and does not adequately address problematic use of First Nations culture by big tech.

The report recommends transparency from AI companies on their use of Australian content, payment for artists whose work is used by someone else for commercial gain, and “strong penalties for failure to comply with the law, including breaches of technical protections”. It recommends that “frontier AI companies” be given “the certainty necessary to train their AI models in Australia”, in a way that reflects Australian values and culture. It recommends the government “incentivise commercial deals between large rights holders and collective agencies”, and create a mechanism to make it easier and fairer for Australian rights holders and creators to be paid by AI companies training models in Australia. It recommends the government “include consideration of the protection of the cultural authority of Australia’s Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders”. It recommends the government “develop and implement whole-of-government procurement and adoption policies that leverage Commonwealth purchasing power to stimulate investment in Australian AI capabilities”.

The report comes from the Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence, and committee member and ACT Senator David Pocock issued a dissenting report addressing data centres and copyright. On copyright, Pocock called on the government to refrain from making any changes to existing copyright law, to focus on enforcing existing protections, and to facilitate licensing deals. He said that if Australia creates conditions more relaxed than other jurisdictions, the country is at risk of becoming the “the copyright equivalent of the Cayman Islands”. Australian author Charlotte Wood called out AI companies for “demanding that our Labor government greenlight the greatest wage theft in history”, while causing harm to the environment and democracies.

The campaign Not Theirs to Take argues for protection of Australia’s creative and media sector, which it says contributes $70.3 billion to the Australian economy and employs almost 600,000 workers. A central message of the campaign is that “AI companies should not be able to use Australian creative work without permission and agreed payment”. The Guardian’s Josh Butler reported that the report was expected on Monday, November 23, at the start of parliament’s final four sitting days of 2026. Liberal MP Garth Hamilton described AI as “just good old-fashioned theft” and proposed a levy on companies, while former Nationals leader David Littleproud said Anthropic could afford to pay copyright holders. Shadow attorney general Michaelia Cash called a possible music carveout a “ham-fisted tactic” and warned against property being stolen.

The Conversation states that Australian copyright law is automatic, so as soon as an artist creates a work they have copyright, and that payments from the Copyright Agency are a key component of artist income. It says training on Australian content in overseas data centres does not result in remuneration for Australian artists, but does create the opportunity for AI users to replicate Australian content and potentially profit from it. It says the report does not address the existing use of Australian content to train AI models around the world. It says organisations such as the National Library of Australia have been undertaking extensive programs to develop Indigenous cultural and intellectual property protocols, work it describes as time-consuming and highly laborious. Superpower Daily reported that creative industries reacted with dismay last week to reports that Labor was considering a music carveout within a permit system for AI companies, reports that landed the morning after the ARIA Awards, where prominent musicians backed the Not AI’s To Take campaign.

Superpower Daily reported that senior figures Richard Marles, Tim Ayres and Michelle Rowland have increasingly argued that existing copyright law has shortcomings, while major rightsholder groups dispute the need to change the law. It reported that Duniam and Violi made their appeal for a less partisan approach about a fortnight before the expected report. It said the report could show whether Labor’s tentative cross-party cooperation on AI can hold, and is a step toward legislation Labor is expected to bring forward on data centres, energy use and copyright. The Conversation says the economic gains remain to be seen, noting companies have laid off staff and the recent Anthropic IPO has created some new billionaires. Superpower Daily says the recommendations arrive just before parliament’s holiday break, after only four sitting days remain.

stories.Headline: UK lawmakers call for a ban on AI chatbot toys for children over safety and privacy risks
stories.Summary:
Warnings have been issued to parents about giving AI powered chatbot toys to children this Christmas in the United Kingdom. These toys, which come from the US and China, use artificial intelligence to communicate instead of using pre-recorded phrases. A letter signed by 52 MPs and peers has called for a ban on these products until they are safe. Baroness Finlay of Llandaff led this effort to alert the government about the risks these toys pose to children. The issue was first raised in the House of Lords on October 29 before the recent letter was sent.

The letter asks Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds to use section 11 of the Consumer Protection Act 1987 to stop sales. It requests a ban on chatbot toys for under-16s and an alert from the Office for Product Safety and Standards. The group wants a dedicated commodity code to track AI toys and independent testing for psychological, developmental, and privacy harm. In the US, California officials confirmed a ban for under-16s from January, and New York passed a five-year moratorium. The Aoomii AI Meow Pixie is a £50 toy from China available on Amazon that requires the Tuya app.

Kitty Hamilton, co-founder of Set@16, said testing showed one toy told her to jump over a balcony or run into traffic. She claimed that foreign manufacturers are using British children as guinea pigs and called for a best-in-class testing framework. Hamilton warned that children might turn to toys for guidance before parents and expressed concern over the lack of data transparency. Jo Frost, a global family expert, described the toys as a wolf in sheep's clothing and urged parents to look beyond packaging. Frost told the government to remove these products from sale pending rigorous and independent safety scrutiny of their content.

Parents and children are the primary people affected by the sale of these interactive and potentially dangerous AI powered toys. Campaigners argue that these products target the affection and trust of toddlers and may act as substitutes for parents or friends. One toy reportedly told a tester where she lived without her sharing the information and retained personal data about King Charles. There are also concerns that children might adopt American accents because some of the toys speak with an American accent. Amazon stated they require third-party sellers to comply with laws and are removing the item in question during a review.

The toys are a new category of product and the UK currently has no dedicated law for AI powered chatbots. They are currently regulated by a patchwork of existing data protection, online safety, and product safety frameworks drafted before generative AI. These existing rules were designed for physical hazards, such as choking on a beady eye, rather than psychological or emotional risks. The Aoomii AI Meow Pixie can hold conversations, tell stories, play music, and respond to touch in 40 different languages. The toy's app asks for consent to share data, which raises further concerns about who can access the collected information.

The government must now decide whether to protect children or allow them to be a testing ground for these new toys. Campaigners are calling for independent regulation that includes educational and psychological testing to ensure that the chatbot toys are safe. It remains unclear if the UK will adopt a formal ban or a testing framework similar to those in America. The articles leave open whether other retailers will remove AI toys or if the government will issue a formal safety alert. Aoomii was approached for comment regarding these concerns, but the provided text does not include a response from them.

stories.Headline: USC leads consolidated California DREAMS and Northwest SI superhub to expand domestic chip prototyping
stories.Summary:
California DREAMS and the California Pacific Northwest AI Hardware Hub announced on 23 November 2026 that they have consolidated their organisations into a single, expanded superhub. The combined body is called the California DREAMS and Northwest SI Superhub. It will provide startups, defence contractors, commercial companies, innovators and government partners with a domestic microelectronics prototyping ecosystem. The unified superhub will be led by the University of Southern California. Stanford University will continue to lead the Northwest SI division of the superhub's technical initiatives in SI hardware.

The consolidation extends geographic reach from Southern California through Silicon Valley and the broader Pacific Northwest innovation ecosystem. It advances the goals of the Department of War's Microelectronics Commons initiative by creating a more integrated domestic capability for semiconductor design, fabrication, testing, packaging and lab-to-fab technology transition. The new hub will expand the services available through MOSIS 2.0, the prototyping service at the heart of California DREAMS. It will also give customers direct access to Northwest SI's CMOS+X Route, known as CXR, which provides a pathway for integrating emerging materials and devices with established CMOS platforms. The expanded hub will offer streamlined access to domestic semiconductor design services, multiproject wafer runs, nanofabrication, custom foundry access, prototyping, testing, packaging and engineering support.

Gaurav S. Sukhatme, interim dean of the USC Viterbi School of Engineering and director of the USC Stevens School of Computing and Artificial Intelligence, said USC has led efforts to democratise access to advanced semiconductor technology for over four decades. He said the Information Sciences Institute launched the MOSIS service in 1981, which changed who could turn a chip design into fabricated silicon. He said the new partnership builds on that pioneering spirit. He said combining California DREAMS, MOSIS 2.0 and the Northwest SI Hub gives researchers, startups, industry and government unprecedented access to world-class semiconductor technology. Steve Crago, director of California DREAMS and interim Michael Keston Executive Director of the USC Information Sciences Institute, said microelectronics innovation depends on reducing the friction between great ideas and manufacturable products.

Crago said combining forces with the Northwest SI Hub strengthens both organisations and brings the CMOS+X Route, its research team and Silicon Valley network into the MOSIS 2.0 ecosystem. He said customers get broader access to technologies and expertise through a single storefront, moving from ideas to prototypes faster. H.-S. Philip Wong, principal investigator of the Northwest SI Division of the superhub, said SI hardware innovation requires a pathway to turn breakthroughs into working systems. He said the Northwest SI Division brings expertise in SI hardware, emerging devices and CMOS+X technologies, while California DREAMS brings end-to-end prototyping and technology-transition capabilities. The consolidation expands the hub's capabilities beyond RF, compound semiconductors, 5G/6G, electronic warfare and quantum to include SI hardware and CMOS+X integration.

The combined hub connects university nanofabrication facilities at USC, Stanford, UC Berkeley, UC Davis, Caltech, UCLA, UC Irvine, UC Riverside, UC San Diego and UC Santa Barbara. It also connects industry partners including Northrop Grumman, HRL Laboratories, Teledyne, Western Digital and numerous commercial foundries. Through MOSIS 2.0, customers gain access to technologies spanning advanced silicon, GaN, GaAs, InP, SiGe, photonics, advanced packaging and heterogeneous integration. At USC, the hub is anchored by the USC Information Sciences Institute, the USC Viterbi School of Engineering and the USC Stevens School of Computing and Artificial Intelligence. California DREAMS is headquartered at the USC Information Sciences Institute, part of the USC Viterbi School of Engineering, and operates MOSIS 2.0 as a national access platform for semiconductor design and manufacturing.

The Northwest SI Division is already building its pathway through CXR, a national platform that has enabled innovators across multiple hubs and institutions to access CMOS fabrication and integrate emerging X technologies, with multiple projects already progressing through the program. The original MOSIS service has supported more than 60,000 chip designs since 1981. USC's experience supporting export-controlled and classified research further enables the combined hub to accelerate the transition of critical technologies into defence applications. Stanford contributes leadership in semiconductor research, SI hardware, CMOS+X technologies and their 3D integration, and advanced nanofabrication. The articles do not state a completion date for the consolidation or say whether any further approvals are required.

stories.Headline: Micron expands high-bandwidth memory production in Taiwan and Singapore
stories.Summary:
The United States chipmaker Micron is accelerating the expansion of its high-bandwidth memory production facilities in Taiwan and Singapore. The company brought the first piece of production equipment into its Singapore packaging plant on November 19, 2026. This move is part of a strategy to compete with Samsung Electronics and SK hynix in the sixth-generation memory market. Micron expects to begin initial production at the Singapore site in early 2027.

The expansion requires an estimated investment of 7 billion dollars for the packaging facility alone. Micron reported capital spending of about 25 billion dollars for the first half of fiscal year 2027, which runs from September 2026 to August 2027. The company plans to increase this spending further in the second half of that period, primarily for cleanroom construction starting from the end of 2028. The Singapore packaging plant is expected to create around 1,400 jobs, while a separate wafer fabrication facility will add more for a total of 3,000 new positions.

Chen Kok Sing, a senior vice president at Micron, stated that the facility will strengthen the global assembly and test network. He noted that the progress reflects strong execution by company teams and close collaboration with partners like the Singapore Economic Development Board. Micron also claimed it began mass production of 12-layer HBM4 in March, with speeds exceeding 11 gigabits per second per pin. The company is currently providing customers with samples of a 16-layer product.

This expansion follows the claim by Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang that three memory chipmakers passed HBM4 certification for Vera Rubin. Micron is currently third in market share, with Counterpoint Research estimating its share at 18 percent in the second quarter of 2024. The company expects the Singapore production line to contribute meaningfully to its packaging capacity starting in the first half of 2027. Industry observers suggest these moves indicate that Micron has reached supply agreements with major buyers like Google and Nvidia.

stories.Summary:
Companies and governments have engaged in a massive borrowing binge to fund the artificial intelligence boom during 2026. This surge in debt issuance has increased the supply of bonds, which prevents sovereign bond yields from falling significantly. The trend of heavy borrowing is now moving abroad, putting pressure on European bond markets.

This financial shift requires a change in the supply and demand balance for bonds to allow for a market recovery. Seamus Mac Gorain notes that the 10-year Treasury yield has reached 5 percent for only the second time since 2007. He expects this yield to remain between 4.5 percent and 5.25 percent until borrowing patterns change, possibly after 2027. Additionally, the OECD predicted that sovereign bond issuance would reach a record 18 trillion dollars in 2026.

Seamus Mac Gorain, the head of global rates at JPMorgan Asset Management, is responsible for these observations. He stated that the current period is among the worst for bond markets due to the AI buildout. Mac Gorain explained that the AI boom increases demand and inflation, which supports the case for higher interest rates. He believes that while hyperscalers will continue to borrow next year, they may eventually shift to shorter borrowing periods.

The broader context involves central banks shrinking their balance sheets through quantitative tightening, which forces markets to absorb more bonds. Mac Gorain suggests that the European Central Bank might slow this process due to a change in leadership. He also noted that while the UK and France may tighten fiscal policies, other governments seem happy to spend more freely. stories.Headline: Oura agrees to buy Counsel Health for $625 million to pair AI primary care with ring biometrics
stories.Summary:
Oura, a wearables manufacturer known for its smart rings that track heart rate, respiration and other biometrics, announced earlier this month that it plans to acquire Counsel Health, an AI-based primary care company, for $625 million. The deal was discussed at the HLTH conference in Las Vegas, where Counsel founder and CEO Dr. Muthu Alagappan spoke on a Tuesday panel about reimagining primary care for the modern era. Counsel has trained software to make medical decisions and work alongside doctors, using a team of clinical AI agents that Alagappan described as almost an Iron Man suit for the clinician. The care model is almost entirely based around chat, allowing physicians to handle multiple patients at once, and Oura's chief medical officer, Dr. Ricky Bloomfield, argued that patients care about getting care how and when they need it rather than whether the provider is human. The acquisition would let Counsel's AI absorb continuous biometric data from Oura's wearables to build a fuller picture of a user's health, according to Alagappan.

Oura CEO Tom Hale described chatting with his Counsel doctor about an eye infection immediately, which he said gave him an incredible window into what the companies could offer, including care for people who lack a doctor with a human in the loop to take action. The articles report that about one-third of Americans do not have a primary care provider, a figure expected to worsen as the population ages according to the Physicians Foundation, and that only one-fourth of new doctors are entering primary care, the lowest rate in a decade. Experts have long warned that U.S. primary care is on the verge of collapse, with many family physicians closing or selling their practices after years of insufficient reimbursement and other challenges. Physician groups remain adamant that AI will take over administrative work such as scheduling, triaging and charting but will never replace human providers, with Dr. John Whyte, CEO of the American Medical Association, saying patients do not want to hear a cancer diagnosis from an LLM.

Dr. Kyu Rhee, president and CEO of the National Association of Community Health Centers, said some tasks are worth replacing and that with the right AI he might manage 2,500 patients continuously beyond the traditional visit-based model, compared with the 1,500 he managed with a team of 11. Dr. Sarah Russell of Anthropic said most people experience primary care as inaccessible and difficult, and that treating it as a routing function makes sense for a powerful AI role, while health economist Jonathan Kolstad said primary care doctors could be empowered to engage with patients in ways they have not been able to. Experts are coalescing around the idea that AI will create a spectrum of primary care, delivered through a phone or in person at a family physician's office, with the patient deciding, and thorny questions remain about how much AI should usurp physicians' tasks and what autonomy it will be allowed. Russell said she frequently asks the clinical AI platform OpenEvidence about patient symptoms or the latest research and cannot imagine seeing patients now without AI.

stories.Headline: Micron recruits South Korean engineers to expand AI memory production across Asia
stories.Summary:
US memory chipmaker Micron Technology launched a recruitment drive in South Korea on Monday, November 24, 2026. The company is seeking engineers for its Asian operations to fill various technical roles. This campaign targets both entry-level talent and experienced professionals. Micron is holding recruitment sessions and in-person interviews at Coex in southern Seoul. The drive aims to secure technical talent as competition in the industry intensifies.

The company seeks science and engineering graduates and professionals with less than two years of experience for the first round. A second round from Friday through Sunday targets engineers with at least five years of experience. Openings are available in Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, and India for manufacturing, advanced packaging, and HBM chip design. Candidates must have working English proficiency to qualify for these positions. Micron is recruiting through Seoul National University, Yonsei University, and Korea University.

Micron is responsible for this recruitment drive to expand its production of high-bandwidth memory. The company wants engineers to improve production yields and develop advanced packaging technologies for next-generation memory. In Taiwan, they seek specialists in semiconductor processing, equipment, and manufacturing automation. Singapore roles include senior engineers for HBM product integration, testing, reliability, and NAND flash manufacturing. Tokyo roles focus on principal design engineers for high-speed memory interfaces, including HBM4 technologies.

The recruitment drive affects engineers in South Korea and rivals Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. These three companies are all competing to expand production of high-bandwidth memory for AI processors. Engineers in India are also affected as Micron seeks specialists for chip design and verification work. The range of positions reflects the technical demands of expanding AI memory production. Manufacturers need people who can package multiple memory dies together and ensure performance requirements.

Micron previously concentrated its Korean recruitment activity on university campuses before expanding to a major exhibition venue. The company is now broadening its search to include experienced professionals instead of just graduates. This shift occurs as the industry seeks engineers who can handle the technical challenges of AI memory. The company is targeting the home market of its two biggest memory chip rivals. This expansion follows the need for specialists in vertically stacked memory chips and HBM4.

The latest recruitment round is scheduled to continue through Sunday, November 30, 2026. Micron will continue to seek specialists for its operations across Taiwan, Singapore, Japan, and India. stories.Headline: Nscale chief executive Josh Payne tells staff the data center company has enough capital to stay private for now
stories.Summary:
Nscale's chief executive, Josh Payne, told employees at a companywide meeting on Tuesday that the data center company has enough raised capital to stay private for the foreseeable future, according to the Financial Times, as a sharp sell-off in technology shares clouds its plans for a $35 billion initial public offering. Four people familiar with the discussions told the FT that Payne sought to steady nerves over Nscale's financial footing following a hiring pullback and growing Wall Street unease over debt-fueled artificial intelligence expansion. While executives had aimed to list Nscale this year, Payne said the goal is simply to pursue a public offering as soon as possible, and Nscale declined the FT's request for comment. The report says Nvidia is an investor in Nscale and several other emerging data center operators.

The uncertainty comes alongside operational hurdles and heavy cash burn, with the company informing staff last week that it was halting hiring for several months except for essential roles even as it lists more than 100 open positions on LinkedIn. Microsoft walked away from a $3.2 billion agreement for a data center outside London after it became clear power grid connections would not arrive until the 2030s, and it also passed on an option for a Texas site. After pausing most hiring and losing that deal, Nscale projected a nearly $1.7 billion net loss over nine months through September. A steep pullback across AI equities, fueled in part by rising balance sheet debt across companies in the sector along with ongoing turbulence at chipmaker Nvidia, has complicated the listing outlook.

Shares of data center or cloud operators have been battered, with CoreWeave down 24% and Nebius dropping 43% so far in November alone. While Nvidia's reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang helped the overall AI market recover on Monday, it quickly lost momentum on Tuesday over risks around rising government scrutiny of Nvidia's export trade practices. Anthropic, whose blockbuster IPO last week Nscale had been expected to follow closely, saw its shares fall below their offering price on Tuesday. The articles do not say what Nscale will do next beyond Payne's stated goal of pursuing a public offering as soon as possible.

stories.Headline: NVIDIA board reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO following national security review
stories.Summary:
The board of NVIDIA unanimously reinstated Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and board director on November 23, 2026. This decision came eleven days after Huang resigned from his position on November 12, 2026. He had stepped down four days after admitting to an affair with a woman. Reports linked him to a former Megaspeed CEO alleged to work for Chinese intelligence.

The board reinstated Huang after meetings with him and receiving input from unnamed senior United States government officials. Colette Kress returns to her role as CFO after serving as the interim CEO. Harvey Jones remains the chair of the board during this leadership transition. The board also formed a National Security and Export Control Committee of independent directors. They are currently hiring a chief compliance officer to manage company operations.

The board stated it was satisfied with the candor and ability of Huang to lead the company. They claimed his return poses no national security risk based on the government input received. President Donald Trump told CNBC that he convinced the board to bring Huang back. He stated that he urged the board directly and indirectly to make this decision.

The reversal of the resignation drew criticism from members of both parties in the United States Congress. Retired Brigadier General Robert Spalding said the severity of the national security risks is a matter of debate. He argued that the Chinese Communist Party is a grave threat to the West. He believes the United States must recognize how China uses technology to strengthen its industries.

Huang resigned amid reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. This occurred as senators and House leaders pressed for chip export records and a closed door briefing. About 600,000 NVIDIA H200s are reportedly held in Hong Kong awaiting import approval from Beijing. Samsung and SK hynix HBM is reportedly reaching Chinese AI chipmakers through smuggling. Oracle canceled an estimated seven billion dollar AI compute deal with Tencent.

Huang is due to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on December 3, 2026. He must also sit for interviews with three different House committees regarding chip diversion. An independent board investigation into the foreign intelligence effort will proceed until it reaches a conclusion. The articles leave open whether Huang's return will expose sensitive technology or complicate export restrictions. They do not state the final outcome of the ongoing independent board investigation.

stories.Headline: NTT DATA and Microsoft partner to build AI-native industry solutions for enterprises
stories.Summary:
On November 18, 2026, NTT DATA deepened its strategic collaboration with Microsoft to build a new generation of AI-native industry solutions for enterprises. Simultaneously, VeriSilicon announced a low-power, high-performance wearable subsystem solution designed specifically for next-generation augmented reality and artificial intelligence glasses in Shanghai. These two separate initiatives aim to advance how artificial intelligence is integrated into both large-scale business processes and wearable consumer hardware. Both companies released these announcements on the same day to highlight their latest technological advancements in the field of artificial intelligence. The efforts focus on moving beyond simple experimentation toward scaled business transformation and efficient computing for advanced wearable device applications.

The NTT DATA and Microsoft effort requires deep industry expertise, scaled forward-deployed engineering capabilities, and frontier technology platforms to succeed. It initially focuses on telecommunications, media, healthcare, life sciences, manufacturing, automotive, and insurance, utilizing the AI Vista platform and 400 reusable assets. NTT DATA plans to mobilize over 500 Microsoft Frontier engineers globally to work directly with clients and domain specialists. VeriSilicon's solution uses FLEXA subsystem architecture and DECNano compression technology to optimize memory bandwidth, data transfer, and overall computing efficiency. This wearable system integrates the Nano-XR series, including ISPNanoUltra-XR, ISPPico-XR, DCNanoUltra-XR, and GCNanoOptimaV-XR, to handle various processing tasks for glasses.

Edwina Fitzmaurice, Corporate Vice President of Industry Solutions Delivery at Microsoft, stated that combining their resources helps clients reimagine how work gets done. She noted that merging Microsoft's cloud and AI platform with NTT DATA's global engineering scale delivers meaningful business outcomes for their clients. The companies believe that technology alone cannot redesign industry processes without people who understand business workflows, data, and regulatory environments. They argue that AI-native solutions should be designed from the start to solve specific problems rather than adding AI to existing workflows. The goal is to identify where artificial intelligence can fundamentally change how industry-specific work is performed to create new value.

Clients in the insurance sector may be affected by reimagining underwriting and claims processes around decisions that are assisted by artificial intelligence. Manufacturing clients could use real-time operational data and AI to identify quality issues and determine the most appropriate response. Healthcare providers might orchestrate complex workflows while keeping clinicians in the loop, and telecommunications firms could improve network and customer operations. VeriSilicon's technology affects the wearable market by providing smartphone-level photo and video quality with optimized power consumption and silicon area. Their ISPPico-XR specifically supports always-on functions for users, such as gesture recognition and eye tracking, within augmented reality glasses.

NTT DATA and Microsoft have a relationship spanning more than 25 years, supported by 23 advanced specializations and six Microsoft Solutions Partner designations. The company holds more than 24,700 Microsoft certifications and currently has approximately 120,000 Microsoft Copilot users globally, including many users in Japan. They use Microsoft AI internally for marketing, IT service management, and employee productivity to gain firsthand experience in driving AI adoption. VeriSilicon built its new wearable solution on a broad portfolio of low-power processing IPs and previous experience in the wearable market. Their existing IP portfolio includes Neural Network, Video, Digital Signal, Image Signal, and Display Processing Units with various configurable options.

NTT DATA will now apply its codified agent patterns, architecture, and connectors to help clients prepare their IT environments for transformative technologies. They will continue to monitor performance and measure business value while determining where human judgment must remain in the loop. VeriSilicon will offer its comprehensive portfolio of processing IPs to address different power and performance requirements for various glasses applications. The articles leave open how these AI-native solutions will specifically perform across different global geographies and diverse regulatory environments. It remains unclear how VeriSilicon's new subsystem will be integrated into specific consumer hardware brands or the final retail pricing.

stories.Headline: EU AI Act mandates rights impact assessments for high-risk deployers as US divergence threatens global standards
stories.Summary:
A legal and governance study published in Cambridge Forum on AI: Law and Governance examined how algorithmic technologies across corporate value chains are forcing a transition from fragmented compliance to unified governance models. The study was published on November 25, 2026, and was reported by Bioengineer.org. It examines the European Union’s regulatory framework, anchored by the mandatory Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment introduced under the EU Artificial Intelligence Act. The study demonstrates that this framework establishes a mechanism that embeds binding human rights accountability into commercial deployment decisions. It also addresses the Council of Europe’s voluntary Human Rights, Democracy, and Rule of Law Impact Assessment methodology.

The study states that the European Union enacted Regulation (EU) 2024/1689, known as the Artificial Intelligence Act. Under Articles 8 and 9, upstream technology providers bear legal responsibility for mitigating technical risks through continuous risk management systems. Article 27 establishes distinct obligations for downstream deployers, addressing the operational deployment phase where developers no longer exercise direct operational control. Under Recital 96, the requirement to conduct a formal Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment was introduced to safeguard protected rights in core economic and public sectors. The final text of Article 27 confines mandatory compliance to public bodies, private entities providing public services, and commercial operators deploying high-risk systems for credit scoring, creditworthiness evaluations, or risk assessment and pricing in life and health insurance.

The study identifies the Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment as an innovative governance tool that enforces an anticipatory, by-design approach to system deployment. It states that the regulation compels private corporations to internalize the societal costs and externalized harms of digital technologies. The authors observe that while core elements of fundamental rights cannot be infringed, non-core interferences require robust justification demonstrating proportionality and the absence of less intrusive operational alternatives. They note that many deploying organizations, particularly small and medium enterprises across distributed value chains, lack the interdisciplinary expertise required to analyze machine learning architectures, identify vulnerable demographic cohorts, and execute culturally nuanced stakeholder engagement. The study emphasizes that the voluntary Council of Europe methodology functions synergistically with the EU AI Act, allowing multinational corporations to apply consistent rights-based practices.

The study states that the potential for these complementary European assessment frameworks to establish unified global standards is increasingly threatened by deep regulatory divergence with the United States. It says that market-driven United States policies explicitly counter multilateral rights-based standards. The study explains that applying the doctrine of horizontal effect, or Drittwirkung, to contemporary artificial intelligence introduces unprecedented legal complexities that traditional bilateral frameworks cannot address. It states that modern artificial intelligence systems operate through dispersed value chains that distribute operational responsibilities across software developers, commercial deployers, and third-party data suppliers. The study notes that algorithmic systems exhibit high degrees of opacity, automated adaptability, and systemic bias, and that their downstream consequences affect individuals through complex automated workflows that deployers themselves may not fully comprehend.

The study states that corporate human rights compliance historically relied primarily on voluntary corporate social responsibility initiatives and ethical business norms that lacked formal enforcement mechanisms. It says that the 2011 United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights and its three pillars of state duty to protect, corporate responsibility to respect, and access to remedy remained limited by their voluntary nature whenever commercial profit margins conflicted with rights safeguarding. The study states that civil litigation under the United States Alien Tort Claims Act faced severe judicial restrictions regarding extraterritorial jurisdiction and corporate liability. It notes that European jurisdictions enacted targeted due diligence legislation such as France’s Loi de Vigilance and Germany’s Supply Chain Due Diligence Act, which primarily focused on formal enterprise risk management and shareholder interests rather than systematically mitigating algorithmic harms. The study states that the Fundamental Rights Impact Assessment represents an institutional evolution of the Data Protection Impact Assessment mandated under Article 35 of the General Data Protection Regulation.

The study states that the European Parliament originally sought to mandate assessments across all high-risk systems, while the final text narrowed the assessment’s mandatory scope. It describes the Council of Europe’s voluntary framework as offering an algorithm-neutral, multi-step governance architecture developed by the Ad Hoc Committee on Artificial Intelligence. The study states that this framework encompasses four interconnected procedural stages: Context-Based Risk Analysis, Stakeholder Engagement Process, Risk and Impact Assessment, and Mitigation Planning. It says that each consecutive phase is documented within a centralized Project Summary Report, creating institutional transparency and establishing empirical records for continuous lifecycle oversight. The study states that the voluntary methodology’s triage phase informs organizational determinations regarding whether operational benefits justify identified risks, while mitigation planning formulates targeted risk-treatment strategies and establishes accessible grievance remedies.
