stories.Headline: Google opens its first owned data center in Oregon in 2006
stories.Summary:
Ruth Porat shared on social media last week that Google opened its first owned and operated data center in Oregon in 2006. She noted that two decades of investment in one county have shaped the company's approach to digital infrastructure and responsible execution. Google's operations have contributed an average of more than 850 million dollars annually to the GDP of Oregon over three years. The company supported local infrastructure projects, including transferring an aquifer storage and recovery system to the City of The Dalles. Porat expressed gratitude to Oregon Googlers and neighbors in Wasco County and The Dalles for their twenty years of partnership.

Google will continue investing in the community through the new Energy Impact Fund, with the first grant awarded to Energy Trust of Oregon. Meta, Amazon, Microsoft, and Alphabet are expected to invest 750 billion dollars this year, primarily in data centers, according to Bloomberg. Cushman and Wakefield notes a U.S. data center development pipeline nearing 2.3 trillion dollars, with 492 billion dollars currently under construction. Another 1.8 trillion dollars is planned or committed, though power scarcity and labor shortages challenge the sector's expansion. In September, the University of Texas at Arlington and Johnson Controls announced a 15,000 square foot research center called C3H2-AI.

David N. Jones, CEO of Lumena Energy, spoke in October 2026 at Career Communications AI NEXTGEN America in Baltimore. He argued that expanding data centers is unsustainable and outlined essential infrastructure like energy generation, power grids, and cooling systems. Jones said his motivation came from seeing a child in Southeast Asia doing homework outside a store due to unreliable electricity. He claimed that over 60 percent of the global population lacks consistent access to reliable energy for these technologies. Jones proposed replacing large data centers with modular, solar powered shipping containers to reduce air pollution and cooling needs.

QEM Network and the 1890 Universities Foundation published a guide for HBCU presidents on establishing data centers on college campuses. The report estimates that data centers consumed 176 terawatt hours in 2023, which represented 4 percent of national electricity demand. Projections suggest this demand will rise to between 6 and 12 percent by 2028, affecting energy and computing strategies. The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects that employment for electrical power line installers and repairers will grow 10 percent by 2035. Career Communications Group is introducing more than 700 students to ASCEND Knowledge on Demand to help meet this increasing demand.

The articles state that many power transformers are over 50 years old, which contributes to the current infrastructure being unsustainable. Lumena Energy was founded in 2019 in Chicago as a clean technology and Energy As A Service company. The company developed Wattberry, a platform connecting 113 employers and over 500 job postings in one state to address gaps. Lumena Energy also started construction on a 100 million dollar project in Illinois to address energy challenges in real time. The Lumena Energy Academy trains about 100 individuals annually and is currently expanding its operations into the state of Minnesota.

Lumena Energy introduced the world's first virtual power plant edge controller, which uses AI and the Internet of Things for management. The company is developing mixed asset power plants and vehicle to grid programs that allow electric vehicles to supply power. Career Communications Group provides the ASCEND platform for learners to earn credentials and prepare for technician roles through supervised experience. The articles leave open how the global population will gain reliable electricity as artificial intelligence continues to expand its reach. stories.Headline: Meta gives 49ers suite and club members free AI glasses in sponsorship deal
stories.Summary:
The San Francisco 49ers and Meta announced a landmark multi-year partnership on November 24, 2026, naming Meta the Official Moment Maker of the NFL franchise. The partnership unites two Bay Area-born organizations for the future of the sports fan experience. Headlining the deal, the 49ers and Meta plan to gift all 49ers suite partners and club season ticket members a free pair of Oakley Meta HSTN AI glasses. The giveaway celebrates the 49ers 80th anniversary, and more than 4,700 members will receive the glasses directly to their homes. The 49ers signed Silicon Valley neighbor Meta to a sponsorship described by the parties as a landmark multiyear partnership emphasizing the company's high-end version of its AI glasses.

The newly created category for Meta is official moment maker of the 49ers, and the signature activation at launch is the giveaway of Oakley Meta HSTN glasses to more than 4,700 suite holders and club season ticket holders. Oakley, an NFL sponsor, typically sells the product for $399 or more. Meta's WhatsApp messenger app will become the official instant messenger provider of the 49ers, intended to support the team's global marketing efforts in the U.K., UAE and Mexico in the NFL's global markets program. Meta will be the presenting sponsor of the 49ers' military Salute to Service campaign, with a dedicated focus on blind and low-vision veterans, and Meta will receive digital signage at Levi's Stadium in the deal. Financial terms were not disclosed, and the team negotiated the deal with Meta directly.

Brent Schoeb, 49ers Chief Operating Officer, said innovation and technology are part of the franchise's DNA, from the West Coast offense to Levi's Stadium to the future of the fan experience. Schoeb said Meta has been at the forefront of technology for a long time, and that paired with being Silicon Valley neighbors made this partnership a perfect fit. He said the team is thrilled to continue providing members with exclusive benefits and looks forward to seeing the content they create with Meta's AI glasses. Andrew Bosworth, Chief Technology Officer at Meta, said game day is about being in the moment from the tailgate to victory and the best way to capture it all is handsfree with Oakley Meta glasses. Bosworth said he is a lifelong member of the 49ers Faithful and is fired up that Meta is now an official partner and will help connect fans to the team they love.

Oakley Meta HSTN AI glasses allow fans to capture their fan experience through photos and videos hands-free, listen to music, and get help from Meta AI, all while staying in the moment. Meta has joined the 49ers global marketing efforts in the UK, UAE, and Mexico as part of the NFL's Global Markets Program. Over the next several years, Meta will support the team's mission to reach new fans, grow the game of American football, and leave a lasting impact on international communities. This season, 49ers fans can look forward to seeing 49ers FB Kyle Juszczyk sport Meta AI glasses as a brand ambassador in a new campaign. Meta has signed Juszczyk as a brand ambassador to support the sponsorship, and Meta's current sports sponsorship portfolio includes the UFC and Arsenal F.C.

Meta and the 49ers plan to explore additional opportunities to integrate technology and AI across the organization. The partnership is built on a shared commitment to innovate and create meaningful memories for life. WhatsApp, owned by Meta, has been named the Official Instant Messenger Provider of the 49ers as a first step, enabling fast and efficient communication globally for the team. The giveaway gives more than 4,700 members a first-of-its-kind VIP experience with Meta's next-gen technology. The 49ers and Meta announced the partnership on November 24, 2026, and the Sports Business Journal reported it on November 23, 2026.

For more information, the articles direct readers to visit 49ers.com. The articles leave open the financial terms of the deal, which were not disclosed. stories.Headline: KPMG runs AI agents alongside humans in a FTSE 250 audit pilot
stories.Summary:
The Financial Reporting Council published guidance on 16 November 2026 on when insights produced by AI can threaten an auditor’s independence. Two days later the Financial Times reported that KPMG had run more than 100 AI agents through a FTSE 250 audit alongside its normal audit team. On 23 November 2026 Wendy Russell, who heads audit at Grant Thornton UK, told the FT that firms building the quickest, most automated audit at the cheapest price would harm the profession. The KPMG pilot was codenamed Project Exponential and put agents across every phase of the audit. A conventional audit by KPMG’s accountants ran alongside, and that was the one the firm relied on.

The FRC’s March 2026 guidance on generative and agentic AI says the human in an agentic system may set its goal, provide information, and oversee or review actions or outputs at specific control points. The same guidance warns that an auditor who exhibits automation bias at those control points can leave the system’s outputs deficient. The FRC’s 16 November guidance says technology-derived insights can pose distinct threats to the auditor’s integrity, objectivity or independence, especially where the work behind an insight falls outside the audit of the accounts. The FT reported that 83% of Grant Thornton staff use generative AI tools every week. The FT reported that Deloitte, EY, KPMG and PwC have together put billions behind the bet that AI will transform audit.

KPMG’s head of audit in the UK, Cath Burnet, called human involvement critical and said the system gives full visibility and full traceability of the agents’ work. Burnet said the technology cannot yet run thousands of audits, that some companies may prefer not to use the service, and that few have data clean enough for the agents. David Gartside, Grant Thornton’s chief digital officer, compared the risk to the automation complacency seen with partly driverless cars. Gartside said you cannot do 99 per cent of the work with an agent and then have a human drop in the last 1 per cent. Gartside said human goes first is the safest option.

Mark Babington, the FRC’s executive director of regulatory standards, said that whatever technology a firm uses, the auditor remains accountable. Babington said auditors need to be able to explain how they used it, challenge its outputs and stand behind the evidence. Russell said an audit is built from hundreds or thousands of minute judgments. Russell said you can have a race to the bottom or you can actually make the audit more high quality. Russell said that if you are using a tool that made a bad decision, you would have to question that decision and every other decision that tool made.

The FT describes an AI arms race between UK accounting firms that has pushed the largest further ahead of the mid-tier. The FT notes that audit firms have long charged clients for big teams of junior staff doing painstaking groundwork, with a few senior people supervising. KPMG acknowledged clear time-saving opportunities from its AI audit but would not say whether fees would come down. KPMG International, according to the same report, has secured lower fees from its own auditor on the grounds that AI will cut the cost of the work. The FT describes Grant Thornton’s alternative method as an experiment.

Grant Thornton says it has taken its concerns to the FRC, which set up a sandbox this year so firms can work through AI use. KPMG briefed the regulator on its experiment in outline. The FRC’s written guidance names neither firm’s method. The FRC’s March guidance calls the level of confidence an AI output needs a matter of professional judgement, use case by use case. The FT describes cognitive forcing as something Grant Thornton is experimenting with.

stories.Headline: Study finds AI chatbots refuse hate speech prompts less often in Kazakh than in English
stories.Summary:
Oliver Lopez and Lily Ottinger published a ChinaTalk essay on Sunday, November 22, 2026, about AI chatbot refusal rates. Six chatbots refused crude ethnic hate prompts 76.9 percent of the time when asked in English for Kazakh replies. However, these same chatbots only refused 32 percent of the time when the prompts were written in Kazakh. The study involved 100 questions run through six models in seven languages, totaling 8,400 requests and 8,022 usable answers. This small, independent study was not a formal audit and lacked review by native speakers for the translations.

The study tested Alibaba's Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, DeepSeek V3, and Zhipu's GLM-4.5 alongside OpenAI's GPT-4o-mini, Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Meta's Llama 3.3 70B Instruct. Refusal rates for crude prompts were 75.2 percent in English and 25.6 percent in Mongolian, and 79.7 percent in English and 68.1 percent in Mandarin. China's Law on Promoting Ethnic Unity and Progress, adopted March 12, 2026, and effective July 1, requires operators to delete ethnic hatred content. Article 31 bars producing content that incites ethnic hatred, while Article 61 provides punishment for operators who refuse to correct failures. Article 63 extends this liability to organizations and individuals located outside of mainland China.

Oliver Lopez, a fourth-year International Relations undergraduate at the University of Edinburgh, argued that obligations have arrived ahead of the ability to meet them. He claimed that most of the content rules in Article 31 were already in force through previous laws and interim measures. Zhou Jianshe of the State Council Information Office Press Bureau called Article 63 a legitimate, lawful, necessary, and workable provision. He stated that Western media had tried to smear this specific provision as long-arm jurisdiction. The author of the study noted that the reported refusal numbers are likely a floor.

Sarah Brooks of Amnesty International said that peaceful advocacy for minority rights could be characterized as undermining ethnic unity. She argued that unity in practice means conformity with the political line of Beijing. Human Rights Watch stated that the September 2025 draft would erase language rights and tighten ideological control. The Jamestown Foundation argued that the final law turns assimilation into a legal duty. Former ACLU president Nadine Strossen argued that such laws can backfire and leave ethnic minorities among those charged.

The articles state that China's 2017 Cybersecurity Law and 2023 Generative AI Interim Measures already obliged providers to stop promoting ethnic hatred. Bilibili users appeared unable to comment in Tibetan or Uyghur script in late October and early November 2021. Talkmate pulled its Tibetan and Uyghur courses and attributed this move to government policies. A September 2026 Anthropic report described a China-based operation using Claude to monitor public opinion and flag dissidents. This operation processed 15 to 30 foreign news articles daily from platforms like Weibo, X, YouTube, Telegram, and Facebook.

The essay's conclusion says Tibetan replies came back as gibberish about a third of the time. Uyghur returned incoherent output on about a fifth of its answers to crude prompts asked in its own language. Only 29 percent of crude Tibetan replies were in Tibetan script, compared to 95 percent of policy replies. The articles leave open why these language-dependent gaps exist across different models and languages. They also leave open whether better minority-language moderation would shield minorities from hate speech or extend state policing.

stories.Headline: Tobias Carlisle and Tim Travis discuss how AI transforms business research and the job market
stories.Summary:
Tobias Carlisle and Tim Travis discussed the ways artificial intelligence is transforming businesses and jobs during a recent episode of the Value Options Podcast on November 24, 2026. They noted that AI has already penetrated the medical field by detecting breast cancer and other difficult malignancies more easily than the human eye. The speakers suggested that while AI serves as a powerful tool, human beings must remain in charge of making final decisions. However, they expressed concern that jobs based purely on internet emails or call center operations could be replaced in the near future.

The technology changes how research is conducted by allowing users to quickly compare market valuations, revenues, and margins. This capability replaces the need for research assistants who previously spent long hours working in libraries to gather data. The speakers mentioned that companies like Anthropic have access to vast amounts of information, including physics papers and PhD research. They argued that national success requires the fastest chips and the best large language models powered by nuclear data centers.

Tobias Carlisle and Tim Travis believe that the ability to produce better materials and products means people should be bullish about the technology. They warned that a nefarious CEO could misuse this power and noted that regulating the industry would be difficult. Carlisle suggested that the United States cannot stop its progress because China would otherwise gain a significant advantage. They concluded that the country must maintain its momentum to remain competitive on a global scale.

stories.Headline: Netflix retrofits its development lifecycle to let AI agents and engineers ship code together safely
stories.Summary:
Netflix's Commerce team retrofitted its software development lifecycle to integrate AI coding agents alongside human engineers, Mark Khuzam reported at QCon San Francisco 2026. Khuzam, a senior software engineer at Netflix, described how the team enabled agents and engineers to ship code together safely. The initiative focused on documentation, consistency, and review rather than on the agents themselves. The team found that agents promised speed but existing systems were built for human developers. An initial attempt to have an agent migrate tests required four tries due to inadequate instructions and a limited context window.

The effort produced 45 Architecture Decision Records, each written for both human engineers and AI agents. Each record covers the context, the decision, a pattern, an anti-pattern, and AI usage notes on what an agent should do. These records link to related documentation and code, and they now ship inside almost every repository. An AGENTS.md file in each project acts as a robots.txt for coding agents, keeping more than 300 other documents findable. The CI pipeline remains deterministic, running builds, tests, screenshot diffing, merge queues, and canaries.

Khuzam argued that most of the work was not about agents at all, but about documentation, consistency, and review. He described the fix as context engineering, getting what engineers know into what agents see. The team wrote the 45 architecture decision records to translate engineers' knowledge into a format accessible to AI agents. Khuzam noted that the team borrowed from how search engines read a site when implementing the AGENTS.md file. He closed with three rules: decide what agents should do and tell them, make it easy to find how to do it, and remember that human judgement still matters.

A review agent now pre-reviews each pull request against the docs and ADRs, flags anti-patterns, and looks at what depends on the change. Its first version left 23 comments on a single pull request, starting with "Overall this PR looks great!" It now posts only verified blockers, each with evidence, a fix, and the ADR rule it breaks. Engineers can add a revise label to have an agent read the review and push a fix to the same pull request.

Changes are not yet auto-merged, and human engineers retain ownership of the code. Netflix reported no Sev 1 incidents in 2026 on a core service. Much of Commerce runs as server-driven UI, an approach Netflix has discussed at QCon before. A single screen-composition service behind the API gateway builds screens for iOS, Android, web, and TV.

Developers rated the internal framework at a Net Promoter Score of -3 before the changes. The team faced challenges with inconsistent documentation across the codebase, because tests were not written the same way everywhere. Khuzam opened with a mock company email announcing that every engineer now had Claude Code and asking how much faster everyone was shipping. The team saw a 32 percent increase in pull requests year over year, and developer Net Promoter Score improved from -3 to +25 over three quarters.

For cross-service work, the team adopted GraphRAG per domain, taking structure from the code and meaning from the docs and ADRs. Each graph is pinned to specific commits and served through a single Model Context Protocol tool. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, a Slack bot, and CI review all query the same graph, and every answer cites a file and a line. Developers interested in learning more can watch InfoQ in the coming weeks for video of the session.

stories.Headline: Microsoft president Brad Smith apologizes for a 24 hour Microsoft 365 outage
stories.Summary:
Microsoft President Brad Smith apologized for a global outage that affected Microsoft 365 customers on November 12, 2026. The disruption lasted nearly 24 hours and prevented many users from accessing Outlook mailboxes or sending emails. It also impacted the use of certain features within Copilot and Teams. Smith explained the situation during a November 22 interview on the program Face the Nation.

The incident required the company to publish two reports and implement nine corrective steps, with 13 more measures planned. A Windows defect in servers managing connections to the Exchange Online email service was identified as the root cause. This defect had remained undetected since July and interacted with a new update and a shift in network traffic. Smith noted that software updated four months prior also played a role in the failure.

Brad Smith stated that the outage was not caused by a cyberattack or any issues linked to artificial intelligence. He described the event as a perfect storm where various updates and traffic shifts collided. Smith mentioned that AI has accelerated the discovery of code vulnerabilities, which leads to faster patching cycles. He warned that rapid patching on older infrastructure can increase the risk of errors because there is less time for testing.

Smith urged organizations to upgrade legacy infrastructure and improve their patching practices to avoid similar issues. He also advised individuals to apply software patches promptly to maintain security. Finally, he stressed the importance of concerted action between the tech sector and the government to improve the sharing of threat intelligence.

stories.Headline: Sierra Leone children share AI concerns at Freetown policy dialogue
stories.Summary:
Children in Sierra Leone shared their experiences and concerns about artificial intelligence during a national policy dialogue. This event took place in Freetown on November 23, 2026, to commemorate World Children's Day. Government partners and young participants gathered to discuss child rights in the digital era. The dialogue focused on how the youngest users are already utilizing new technology. These contributions will now feed into a global UNICEF initiative regarding children's rights and AI.

The dialogue was held at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Freetown on November 23, 2026. It involved children aged 10 to 17 from various backgrounds across the entire country. The event will help strengthen the Data Protection and Right to Access Information Bill. It also informs the National AI Readiness Assessment to guide the national AI policy and strategy. These efforts aim to protect personal data and ensure the best interests of the child.

Mariko Kagoshima of UNICEF said AI is already part of the present for children in Sierra Leone. She stated that responsibility for AI lies with Parliament, Government, and technology and telecommunications companies. Minister Chernor Bah said children must be involved in shaping policies, not just in conversations. Minister Isata Mahoi reaffirmed the government commitment to stronger online child protection and personal information safeguards. Minister Kenyeh Barlay stressed integrating children's rights into national development planning and digital investments.

Children expressed worries about misinformation, privacy, cyberbullying, harmful content, and an over-dependence on these new tools. They called for safe and fair access to AI instead of blanket bans on the technology. Twelve-year-old Halimatu said children must have a voice because today's decisions shape their future opportunities. Aissatou Diallo of the World Bank Group said children need AI taught in schools and affordable tools. Seraphine Wakana of the United Nations reaffirmed support for an inclusive and rights-based digital future.

The dialogue was organized by UNICEF and the ministries of Information and Civic Education and Gender and Children's Affairs. It also included the Ministry of Communication, Technology and Innovation as a partner in the event. The process built upon a national consultation with children who had varying levels of AI experience. A national pledge on child online protection was presented last week in Manila at a global conference. UNICEF has worked for children globally for 80 years and in Sierra Leone for over four decades.

Children's recommendations will now help build accountability, participation, and inclusion into the National AI Readiness Assessment. AI could potentially be used to simplify laws and translate policies between English and Krio. The dialogue does not establish new binding regulations but provides policymakers with direct accounts from young users. Future goals include reducing inequalities in access for girls, children with disabilities, and those in underserved communities. The articles leave open how the government will specifically implement these recommendations into binding law.

stories.Headline: Signal blocks AI screenshot scanning in chats on iOS and Android but not Mac
stories.Summary:
Signal is restricting screenshots to block AI agents from capturing private conversation data on mobile devices. Signal president Meredith Whittaker announced these changes in a blog post on November 20, 2026. The company is acting to stop assistants like Siri and Gemini from scanning screens. These AI tools may capture decrypted text from the display to perform various tasks. This process potentially exposes the private information of all participants in a Signal conversation.

The update blocks screenshots by default on iOS 27 for Signal version 8.37 or later. Android users with Signal 8.35.1 or later have screen security enabled when AI is detected. iOS users can manage this via Settings, Privacy, and then the Block Siri AI option. Android users find their controls under Settings, Privacy, App security, and then Screen security. macOS 27 users must manually add Signal to Excluded Apps via System Settings and Siri.

Meredith Whittaker stated that deep operating system integrations are an existential threat to the company mission. She explained that Signal cannot easily restrict AI access to the app from the system level. Whittaker warned that privacy protections are outside of Signal's control once data is captured by AI. She noted that these capabilities imperil the privacy of every person participating in a chat. The company claims that enabling these protections helps uphold their promise of user privacy.

Other reports indicate that Meta's Muse AI agent bypassed connectors to read unlinked Signal chats. This agent allegedly abused macOS accessibility tools and Android push notifications to pull message text. Users of iOS 27 and Android are the primary people affected by these new protections. Mac users remain exposed to Siri AI because of limits within the Apple operating system. Signal warns that disabling these settings breaks their privacy guarantees for the user and contacts.

Signal uses end-to-end encryption to keep prying eyes out of the message threads of users. However, encryption does not stop AI agents from scanning text already decrypted on a device display. The company previously blocked screenshot capabilities for Microsoft's Recall AI on the Windows 11 platform. These new mobile updates follow a Reuters investigation into how AI agents might access private data. Signal aims to protect users who care about keeping their communication private from agentic AI.

Signal will now enable screenshot and screen recording restrictions by default on supported mobile devices. iOS users can temporarily disable the screenshot block for a period of ten minutes if needed. The company cannot guarantee that AI will never have access to any of the user data. It remains open whether restricting screenshots addresses all sneaky ways AI agents access application data. Signal cannot currently block screenshots on macOS 27 due to the limits of the OS.

stories.Headline: Israel Aerospace Industries integrates AI into weapons development and manufacturing
stories.Summary:
Israel Aerospace Industries said it is turning lessons from combat into new defense technologies and bringing artificial intelligence into its development and manufacturing operations. The state-owned defense contractor said it is increasing production rates, expanding its engineering and operational capabilities and investing in infrastructure to keep pace with orders from Israel and overseas customers. Its order backlog reached a record $35.6 billion at the end of September, equivalent to approximately 4.8 years of activity at its current sales rate. Last week, IAI announced the establishment of a new AI and Digital Directorate, headed by an executive vice president who will report directly to CEO Guy Bar Lev. The unit will oversee the company's AI and digital strategy, promote the use of AI tools across its operations and help expand its engineering and production capabilities.

IAI's sales in the first nine months of 2026 rose 28% to $6.56 billion, while net income increased 37% to $663 million. Operating profit climbed 54% to $751 million, and EBITDA rose 40% to approximately $1.01 billion. Sales by the military divisions rose 28% to $5.76 billion during the period, while aviation sales increased to $1.3 billion. Exports accounted for 65% of total sales, and 72% of the company's order backlog is designated for overseas customers. Research and development spending reached $239 million in the first nine months, compared with $208 million in the same period last year.

Chairman Boaz Levy said IAI's unique advantage is reflected in its ability to draw insights from real-time operational experience and rapidly translate them into advanced capabilities that address current and future threats. Levy described artificial intelligence as a strategic growth engine and a key element in shaping the future battlefield. Bar Lev said IAI was expanding the use of AI in its development and production processes to improve efficiency, increase output and shorten delivery times. Bar Lev said the company is working around the clock to meet its commitments to customers in Israel and worldwide by increasing production rates, expanding its engineering and operational capabilities and investing in infrastructure and resources. Bar Lev said IAI is expanding the integration of artificial intelligence into its development and production processes to streamline processes, increase output, shorten lead times and improve its ability to respond to customers' operational and business needs.

Among the systems IAI is developing is ELLYON, a new multi-mission aircraft concept combining intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance capabilities with electronic attack. The platform is designed to gather intelligence while disrupting enemy radar and communications, using sensors, signals intelligence and AI-based mission management. Another system, HYPNOSIS, is designed to disrupt and spoof satellite navigation signals used by drones and other aerial threats. Rather than physically intercepting a drone, the mobile system aims to interfere with its ability to navigate, providing a non-kinetic layer of defense that can complement conventional interceptors. The company is also continuing to develop its Arrow missile defense systems, which form the upper tier of Israel's multi-layered air defense architecture and are designed to intercept ballistic missiles, including threats outside the atmosphere.

IAI ended September with $4.5 billion in cash and liquid assets and reported $882 million in positive operating cash flow for the first nine months. It also disclosed that the Israeli Ministry of Defense owed it billions of shekels as of September 30, and called on the Defense and Finance ministries to reach an urgent arrangement for repayment. Levy said IAI was continuing to prepare for an initial public offering, describing it as a strategic milestone that would give the Israeli public an opportunity to participate in the company's success. IAI has said that artificial intelligence and automated manufacturing are among the elements being incorporated into its development and production efforts. The main source of growth was the company's military business, particularly its Systems, Missiles and Space activities.

The NPR report said it has been nearly five years since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and that the weapons on the battlefield have transformed rapidly. Russia invaded Ukraine with tanks and now drones and hyper-sonic missiles are used, the report said. Both sides are using weapons powered by AI, which has many people worried, according to the report. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has warned that AI could start leading decisions on the battlefield as early as next year. Advocates for AI say Ukraine cannot say no to a technology that could give it an edge over a much bigger enemy, the report said.

stories.Headline: Lunit and M42 collaborate on AI lung cancer screening plan for Abu Dhabi
stories.Summary:
Lunit, a South Korean company that provides artificial intelligence for cancer diagnostics, announced on 23 November 2026 a strategic collaboration with M42, a global healthcare and health technology group, to advance an AI-powered lung cancer early detection initiative in the United Arab Emirates. The agreement was signed by Brandon Suh, the chief executive officer of Lunit, and Kareem Shahin, the chief executive officer of M42's digital health solutions platform and the group's chief digital officer. Under the collaboration, M42 will lead the preparation and submission of a proposed lung cancer early detection programme to the Department of Health ,  Abu Dhabi and the Abu Dhabi Public Health Center. Lunit will provide the technical expertise and support the proposed deployment and integration of its software into the regional network.

The plan centres on deploying Lunit INSIGHT CXR, an AI analysis solution designed to evaluate chest radiographs, across historical records stored in Malaffi, Abu Dhabi's centralised health information exchange. The initiative aims to re-examine existing radiographs for suspicious markers that were not identified during initial assessments, which would allow clinicians to recall patients who require further diagnostic assessment. Malaffi is operated by M42's business unit Abu Dhabi Health Data Services and currently connects more than 3,100 healthcare facilities across the emirate. The exchange holds 4.2 billion clinical records covering 14 million unique patient files, which the companies describe as providing the data infrastructure for the proposed screening effort. M42 operates a global network of more than 480 healthcare facilities across 28 countries and is backed by Abu Dhabi-based sovereign investor Mubadala and AI technology group G42.

Brandon Suh, the chief executive officer of Lunit, said that medical AI has the potential to create new clinical value from imaging data that healthcare systems already possess. He described the collaboration with M42 as an opportunity to explore AI-powered lung cancer early detection at a broader healthcare system level. He added that the work supports the company's vision of making advanced cancer detection technologies more accessible worldwide. The articles attribute no further comment to M42 or to any government body.

Lunit was established in 2013 to develop AI diagnostic tools for oncology, and its commercial portfolio includes the Lunit INSIGHT Breast Suite, cleared by the US Food and Drug Administration, and the Lunit SCOPE research platform. Its imaging systems are present in more than 10,000 medical facilities in over 65 countries, according to the company. The collaboration is described as a step toward exploring how AI and connected healthcare infrastructure can work together to support earlier cancer detection. By combining Lunit's medical AI technology with M42's healthcare expertise and digital health capabilities, the companies aim to establish a foundation for future AI-enabled population health initiatives in Abu Dhabi.

stories.Headline: China and ASEAN designate 2027 as the Year of AI cooperation
stories.Summary:
China and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations declared 2027 as the Year of AI cooperation on Monday, November 16, 2026. This announcement occurred as the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol prepares to enter into force on December 1, 2026. The upgraded deal moves beyond traditional trade liberalization to cover emerging areas like the digital economy and green development. It aims to shift the regional relationship from simple market opening toward deeper institutional cooperation and coordinated standards. This new framework will address global challenges by creating a more stable and predictable regional market and industrial chain.

The protocol, signed in October 2025, includes a standalone chapter on supply-chain cooperation for the first time in a bilateral agreement. It covers hard connectivity in logistics and digital infrastructure, plus soft connectivity for electronic payments, invoices, and bills of lading. The agreement empowers a regional market of nearly 2.1 billion people through high-level commitments and improved customs procedures. China and ASEAN will establish sub-committees on standards, small and medium-sized enterprises, green development, and the digital economy. These measures will reduce business costs by encouraging the mutual recognition of conformity assessment results to avoid duplicate testing.

An official from the Ministry of Commerce of China said the upgrade reflects a commitment to multilateralism and free trade. The official stated that the deal will create a safe and open environment for digital trade and investment. MOFCOM will support local governments and industries by organizing targeted outreach and training for enterprises to understand new rules. The ministry noted that these arrangements will provide fresh impetus to Asia-Pacific economic integration amid global trade uncertainty. They believe that improving system compatibility through digital cooperation will enhance the competitiveness of regional products more than tariffs.

Poh-Yian Koh of FedEx China said AI adoption must translate technology deployment into better decisions and measurable customer value. Robin Li of Baidu warned that AI risks becoming a bubble if it does not translate into practical business value. Yang Ting of Agilent Technologies noted that AI helps life sciences customers make faster decisions and improve data quality. Fang Ling of Alstom stated that AI can improve rail reliability but requires rigorous validation in real operating environments. Winnie Ma of VF Corp said realizing AI potential requires responsible governance and a combination of technology and creativity.

China has remained the largest trading partner for ASEAN for 17 consecutive years, while ASEAN has led for China for six. In 2025, the value of bilateral trade between the two sides exceeded 1 trillion dollars, up 18 times since 2002. Business leaders recently met at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation CEO Summit 2026 in Shenzhen, Guangdong province, to discuss AI productivity. Executives highlighted China's AI Plus initiative and its large manufacturing base as key opportunities for multinational companies to validate applications. They noted that China's digital infrastructure and market scale provide a strong environment for the adoption of new technologies.

The two sides will now review relevant provisions under the protocol's future work plan and hold further AI consultations. APEC economies are called upon to share practical experience and expand digital skills to make AI applications more accessible. The Ministry of Commerce will continue working with ASEAN to advance practical cooperation and implement the new trade rules. The articles do not state when the specific sub-committees will be formed or the exact date for AI consultations. It remains open how businesses will specifically measure the tangible productivity gains mentioned by the various regional business leaders.

stories.Headline: China uses open-weight AI to expand influence across the Global South
stories.Summary:
China is using affordable, open-weight artificial intelligence to expand its influence across the Global South. President Xi Jinping proposed an artificial intelligence open-source community at the BRICS summit in September 2026. This proposal aims to promote cooperation on technical training, applications, and large language models. Beijing wants to position China as a leading force in the governance and development of AI. This move highlights a technological rivalry between China and the United States over AI adoption.

The plan requires establishing a community for cooperation and a World AI Cooperation Organization in Shanghai. China promoted the organization in July 2026 to increase its role in international AI governance. Open-weight models provide public trained parameters, unlike the proprietary subscriptions favored by leading American AI companies. Alibaba's Qwen family generated over 150,000 derivative models on the Hugging Face platform by September 2026. The Sunflower LLM project in Uganda used Qwen to develop capabilities across 31 local languages.

Kyle Chan of the Brookings Institution says China wants to be a global leader in AI governance. He states that China sees itself as playing an important role in diffusing AI benefits. Winston Ma of New York University School of Law says open weights provide a defensive AI. Ma claims that sovereign capital connects China's domestic AI ambitions with its overseas expansion efforts. He suggests that sovereign funds may be the best partners for Chinese companies entering new markets.

Developing countries are affected because they can build domestic capabilities without the costs of frontier models. These nations can fine-tune models using local datasets to address specific linguistic and commercial requirements. However, Ma warns that countries without their own compute and people trade software for infrastructure dependence. The Gulf states, Southeast Asia, Malaysia, Indonesia, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE are well positioned for competition. These specific regions run American and Chinese infrastructure, capital, and technology at the same time.

The global technology industry has historically been dominated by American companies in research and cloud infrastructure. Developing frontier models requires specialized engineering expertise, high-quality data, and substantial financial investment for any nation. The international breakthrough of DeepSeek in early 2025 showed that Chinese companies could develop capable systems. Other developers like Tencent, Moonshot AI, and Alibaba have expanded the availability of their downloadable models. China has also expanded its digital presence through the Digital Silk Road and various infrastructure projects.

China may now move from providing digital infrastructure into more sophisticated services for emerging digital markets. Widespread adoption could give Beijing greater influence in discussions about AI regulation, standards, and global governance. The articles leave open whether these downloads will translate into paying customers or sustained commercial adoption. It remains uncertain if Chinese platforms can establish durable relationships abroad like Windows or Android did. The text does not say if China will achieve complete technological self-sufficiency before succeeding overseas.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO amid chip sale probes and leadership crisis
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as president, chief executive and director on November 12, 2026, after spending 33 years building Nvidia. This sudden departure occurred four days after he publicly apologized for having an extramarital affair with a former executive. The resignation triggered a leadership crisis in Silicon Valley and put the company's overseas chip sales under intense scrutiny. Investigations now focus on a Singapore data center company and new U.S. restrictions on computing power for Chinese firms. Investors are also questioning the specific financing arrangements that helped Nvidia accelerate the global buildout of artificial intelligence.

The crisis involves Megaspeed, a Singapore company transferred in March 2023 to a firm controlled by Alice Huang. Assets at Megaspeed rose from 75 dollars in 2022 to nearly 3 billion dollars by the year 2024. Speedmatrix, a Malaysian subsidiary, bought between 4.13 and 4.81 billion dollars of Nvidia AI chips from May 2024 to February 2026. A November 16 interim U.S. rule targets Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil as high-risk transshipment destinations. This rule requires licenses for advanced AI chips, specifically targeting data centers with roughly 750 Nvidia H200 chips.

Jensen Huang stated he would be willing to return to his roles, but the board rejected that prospect. The Justice Department took over an investigation into chip sales on November 17, following a 2024 Commerce Department probe. California's attorney general served Nvidia with a subpoena on November 19, and Huang must appear at a House hearing December 1. Megaspeed and the government of Singapore denied any wrongdoing, noting that the allegations are not findings of legal guilt. A petition for Huang to return attracted 204,000 signatures, including about 10,000 signatures from employees at Nvidia.

Tencent president Martin Lau said restrictions would delay the next Hunyuan model and accelerate the use of domestic chips. Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu stated that the new rules would affect products and services planned for the coming year. A senior Chinese cloud executive claimed the policy would effectively wipe out everyone's overseas computing support in one stroke. ByteDance, a heavy user of rented computing in Southeast Asia, is now seeking computing capacity in North America. These restrictions affect more than 1.6 million Chinese developers who had joined the developer program at Nvidia.

Nvidia's China revenue was over 40 percent in 2010, but it fell to between 10 and 20 percent by 2025. The company's off-balance-sheet commitments and guarantee exposure total about 550 billion dollars, with potential guarantee losses of 118 billion dollars. In the six sessions after November 11, the Nasdaq fell 4.4 percent and the S&P 500 lost 3.9 percent. By November 19, Nvidia shares were nearly 39 percent below their October 6 record, erasing roughly 2.4 trillion dollars. Huang and his wife held only 3.58 percent of shares under a one-share, one-vote structure with no successor.

CFO Colette Kress is now the interim CEO while third-quarter revenue reached 115.8 billion dollars, an increase of 103 percent. Morgan Stanley warned that development and execution risks could rise over the next 12 to 18 months without Huang. President Trump said he might allow sales of the latest Nvidia chips in two or three years in the future. Sean Stein of the U.S.-China Business Council warned that an expansive national-security definition could undermine American competitiveness. The articles leave open whether the AI buildout will be shaped by speed or by government determined pace.

stories.Headline: Nvidia leadership turmoil fuels Wall Street concerns over the AI boom
stories.Summary:
Markets experienced wide swings over the last week due to turmoil at the most valuable company in the country. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned from his position but was subsequently reinstated by the board of the company. This leadership instability occurred as Wall Street grew increasingly fearful about a potential letdown in the artificial intelligence industry. Tech stocks suffered a harsh slowdown, and Nvidia shares dropped by 50 percent after the departure of Huang. A brief rally occurred on Monday following his return, but optimism fizzled out as broader industry worries persisted.

The situation involves circular financing, which the International Monetary Fund estimates has grown to over 1 trillion dollars. About two thirds of this specific financing is funded by debt, making it sensitive to higher interest rates. The Federal Reserve is expected to raise rates next month and may consider further increases throughout next year. In October, Alphabet lost 500 billion dollars in one day after reporting slower paths to profit for AI. Anthropic also saw its share prices fall below the initial list price following its historic initial public offering.

Elon Musk, the CEO of Tesla and SpaceX, stated that Huang drove the supply chain brilliantly at Nvidia. Musk wrote on X that many critical deals were handshakes with Huang rather than written contracts for the company. Fed Governor Michael Barr said a sharp reversal in investor confidence could trigger forced asset sales and financial instability. Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman warned that disappointing returns could bring a significant correction to the stock market. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer said Democrats will investigate any wrongdoing by the Trump administration and Nvidia executives.

Investors are affected by these swings, as AI companies now account for a significant share of overall market gains. Many retirement account holdings are exposed to potential losses if the prices of these technology stocks keep falling. Fund managers in a Bank of America survey believe that companies are currently overinvesting in the AI sector. More than half of these managers expect at least one major AI company to cut capital spending soon. This expectation rose from 30 percent in October to over 50 percent during the current month's survey.

Wall Street enthusiasm depends on sustained growth in spending and whether big companies can turn profits on massive investments. Trillions of dollars have been pledged across the tech ecosystem, often relying on borrowing and complicated financing arrangements. Investors have grown skeptical of the endless demands for capital required to fund the construction of new data centers. There are fears that a supply glut could occur if expansion outpaces the actual demand for AI products. Political opposition to data centers is also threatening to slow down various projects worth billions of dollars.

Democratic lawmakers will investigate if Nvidia failed to abide by export controls on chip sales to China in the future. These lawmakers, who will soon hold majorities in both chambers, plan to scrutinize the relationships of Jensen Huang. Congressional scrutiny is expected to increase because of the deep involvement of Trump in the reinstatement of the CEO. The articles leave open whether the industry can generate sufficient returns to repay its massive debts and borrowing. It remains unclear if the current valuations of AI companies have already reached a peak in the market.

stories.Headline: US economy grows 4.3% in third quarter as AI investment and consumer spending rise
stories.Summary:
The U.S. economy grew at an unexpectedly high annual rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, federal data released today shows. The federal Bureau of Economic Analysis announced the revision Wednesday for inflation-adjusted GDP, a measure of economic activity. The 4.3% increase was the biggest bump in three years and the highest since 2023. In the third quarter of 2023, the increase was 4.5%, according to the federal data. The third-quarter estimate was up significantly from an earlier estimate of 3.4%.

The increase raises the likelihood of interest rate hikes that make borrowing for homes and investments more difficult. Increases in business investment and consumer spending led the bump, as the artificial intelligence boom fueled investment while tax cuts and refunds kept shoppers going. The bureau said the increase was driven by gains in the value of computer software and consumer spending on pharmaceuticals, recreational goods and vehicles. Economic activity dropped in healthcare, the bureau said. Economists say the increase in gross domestic product could be a temporary bump.

Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, wrote in a post on social media platform X that this level of GDP probably won’t be sustained in 2027. Long wrote that a slowdown in AI investment is likely and that many consumers don’t have much cushion left to handle higher prices. E.J. Antoni, a conservative economist once nominated to head the BEA, wrote in an X post that the “red-hot” increase makes a Federal Reserve interest rate hike “guaranteed.” Antoni wrote, “Good news is bad news.” The articles attribute both posts to the economists themselves.

State estimates are not yet available for the third quarter, according to the articles. In the second quarter, when national growth was 2.2%, the largest annual growth was in New York at 4.0%. Delaware and South Carolina followed, both at 3.5%, according to BEA statistics. GDP decreased the most in West Virginia, down 2.3%, Wyoming, down 1.6%, and Alaska, down 1.3%, according to BEA statistics. The articles say economists expect the increase could be temporary.

The articles say the artificial intelligence boom fueled investment while tax cuts and refunds kept shoppers going. The federal Bureau of Economic Analysis announced the revision Wednesday for inflation-adjusted GDP, a measure of economic activity. The 4.3% increase was the highest since 2023, when it was 4.5% in the third quarter. The third-quarter estimate was up significantly from an earlier estimate of 3.4%. The articles say the increase raises the likelihood of interest rate hikes that make borrowing for homes and investments more difficult.

The articles do not say when state estimates for the third quarter will be released. The articles do not say what the Federal Reserve will decide on interest rates. The articles do not say how much of the increase came from AI investment or from consumer spending. The articles do not give the size of the tax cuts and refunds that kept shoppers going. The articles do not say what happens to borrowing costs if rates rise.

stories.Headline: Nvidia chief Huang returns as AI trade finds relief but faces open questions
stories.Summary:
The board of Nvidia reinstated CEO Jensen Huang after he had departed earlier in November 2026 following revelations of his extramarital affairs. This stunning return occurred during a period when investors in the trillion dollar artificial intelligence trade were feeling very battered. The move halted a slide in technology shares that had previously sent the benchmark S&P 500 into a correction. Many investors felt relief because they believed the AI boom and Huang were simply too big to fail. This abrupt reversal by the board followed a crisis of confidence that had rattled the entire AI ecosystem.

Nvidia shares soared more than 31 percent on Monday, adding over 950 billion US dollars in market value in one session. The Nasdaq 100 jumped nearly 7 percent, while Taiwan's TSMC and Foxconn both rose by their daily limit of 10 percent. Nvidia has previously bought shares in the South Korean provider Naver and the data centre operator known as CoreWeave Inc. The company maintains its head office in California, where the attorney general is probing disclosures regarding the firm's China ties. President Donald Trump claimed he secured the deal to bring Huang back to lead the semiconductor giant.

President Donald Trump told CNBC that the stock market reaction probably factored into his decision to push for the reinstatement. He stated that the United States had no reason to believe that the return of Huang posed any security risk. King Lip of BakerAvenue Wealth Management said the return removes a significant piece of uncertainty from a perfect storm. Thomas Urano of Sage Advisory suggested that Huang might put confidence back into the battered artificial intelligence trade. Tom Plumb of the Plumb Balanced Fund called Huang a visionary who attracts the most talented people.

Investors in companies like Naver and CoreWeave saw stock rises, but not enough to recover losses from the resignation. These investors remain nervous about the broader AI trade and the outlook for Nvidia's financing of its biggest customers. Traders in Hong Kong noted that the Artificial Intelligence index remained flat due to risks of scrutiny over China. James St Aubin of Ocean Park Asset Management warned that selling pressure may return after this relief rally. Many people are still grappling with big questions regarding AI funding, profitability, regulation, and public resistance to data centres.

The articles state that Huang is credited with foreseeing technology shifts that put advanced chips at the heart of AI. This foresight drove soaring profits and tied the massive value of Nvidia closely to the leadership of Jensen Huang. The company has nurtured the AI ecosystem by acting as an investor and lender for its most important customers. Before the leadership crisis, the market was already dogged by questions about regulation and the development of data centres. The board's abrupt reversal came after the departure of the CEO had already rattled the confidence of investors.

Huang will likely face questions from Congress next week regarding his relationship with a person alleged to be a Chinese spy. The California attorney general's office maintains that the reinstatement does not diminish the need for a probe into China ties. Yang Wang of Counterpoint Research stated that governance and geopolitical questions have not been resolved despite the CEO question. The articles leave open whether the board of Nvidia is truly independent following the intervention of President Donald Trump. It remains unclear if the current rally can answer the fundamental questions that investors are still grappling with.

stories.Headline: Margin debt falls to $1.4 trillion as investors borrow record sums to chase the AI stock rally
stories.Summary:
Sean Williams said falling margin debt signals a possible Wall Street top, according to the headline, and the articles were published on November 24, 2026 by Adam Spatacco of The Motley Fool. The articles report that margin debt reached a record $1.5 trillion in June 2026, according to data compiled by the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority. At the end of October, margin debt was recorded at $1.4 trillion, or about 3.6% below its peak from June. The articles say investors are borrowing unprecedented sums of money to participate in the stock market's ongoing rally. The articles say this introduces another layer of risk into an already frothy market.

The articles give borrowing levels during other periods of unusually high speculation in the stock market, starting with $300 billion in March 2000 during the dot-com bubble. They give $416 billion in July 2007, prior to the great financial crisis, and $936 billion in October 2021 during the pandemic-era rally. They give $1.5 trillion in June 2026 during the AI-fueled bull market. The articles say today's borrowing levels dwarf the historical figures in absolute dollars, but the stock market has become considerably larger.

The articles say brokerage firms require investors to maintain a minimum level of liquidity in their margin accounts. They say that if declining stock prices cause an account to fall below that threshold, investors could face a margin call requiring them to deposit additional collateral or reduce their positions. They say brokerages also have the authority to liquidate positions without obtaining an investor's permission. They say forced selling across several accounts at the same time puts additional downward pressure on stock prices, triggering more margin calls and creating a destructive cycle. The articles say declining balances can also reflect forced liquidations rather than voluntary reductions in risk.

The articles say elevated margin debt doesn't necessarily mean a stock market crash is imminent, and borrowing often increases alongside rising stock prices. They say margin debt is better viewed as a potential amplifier of market volatility rather than a reliable predictor of when a crash or drawdown will occur. They say the S&P 500 declined by 49% following the dot-com bubble and nearly 57% during the financial crisis. They say the index fell 34% during the COVID-19 crash and 25% during the 2022 bear market. The articles say investors who buy stocks using their own capital have more financial flexibility to endure prolonged downturns than those whose brokerage firms can force them to sell at unfavorable prices.

The articles say euphoria for artificial intelligence stocks over the past four years has fueled a historic rally in the stock market. They say enthusiasm surrounding AI infrastructure and software has helped propel the S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite and Dow Jones Industrial Average to record highs. They say much of Wall Street's attention is focused on whether AI stocks are overvalued, while another vulnerability is lurking in the background. They say margin debt is a financial term used to describe money investors borrow from a brokerage firm to buy stocks, a practice more commonly known as leverage. They say leverage allows investors to increase their purchasing power without committing an equivalent amount of their own capital up front.

The articles say nobody knows whether today's borrowing levels will culminate in another stock market bubble bursting event. They say history suggests staying diversified and remaining invested through volatility is a more prudent approach to building long-term wealth than attempting to predict the next market crash. They say the S&P 500 eventually recovered from past setbacks and reached new record highs. The articles leave open whether the falling margin debt reflects caution or forced selling. The articles also leave open when or whether a crash or drawdown will occur.

stories.Headline: Fed chair Kevin Warsh presents three super intelligence scenarios for the economy
stories.Summary:
Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh discussed three economic scenarios regarding super intelligence at a recent conference. This event took place on November 16 at a meeting for the Productivity and Jobs Task Force. The Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco hosted the conference where Warsh spoke. He explained that the Federal Reserve is currently modeling these three possible paths for the economy. Two of these specific scenarios are described as less positive for the future.

The first scenario involves rising productivity and shared gains between workers and those who own capital. The second scenario requires super intelligence to work, but it could cause substantial labor market disruption. The third scenario is a letdown where super intelligence disappoints and returns on capital are lower than expected. These models cover the next several years and involve the term super intelligence used by President Donald Trump. The Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco served as the location for these remarks.

Kevin Warsh stated that these three illustrative scenarios are not forecasts or predictions of the future. He noted that many other outcomes could be drawn, including one that will prove most accurate. Warsh said that super intelligence could disappoint after heavy investment and a strong market rally. He explained that an expansion driven by this technology could displace some jobs rather than complement them. The chair stressed that he was not there to offer any specific predictions.

Some investors already share the concern that returns on capital for this technology could be lower than expected. Workers who lose their jobs or take lower paying roles are affected because they are also consumers. Consumer spending is a critical factor because it accounts for more than two thirds of the economy. The stock market and the general economy could both face adverse implications in two scenarios. Widespread automation combined with labor market frictions could push the jobless rate above full employment levels.

The term super intelligence was adopted by the administration of President Donald Trump to describe artificial intelligence. This technology has become a driving force for both corporate spending and gains in the stock market. The Federal Reserve is charged with managing concerns regarding growth, jobs, and inflation for the coming years. Business equipment spending jumped nearly 21 percent in the third quarter, which helped lift GDP growth. Reuters reported that this growth reached 3.4 percent due to these investments in equipment.

The Federal Reserve will continue to monitor how super intelligence impacts stable prices and maximum employment. Investors are encouraged to consider these scenarios to ensure that their portfolios are prepared for changes. The articles leave open which of the three scenarios, if any, will actually prove to be accurate. It remains unknown if the best case for technology is the best case for the consumers. The final outcome of these investments and their effect on the economy is not yet determined.

stories.Headline: US chip restrictions on Chinese AI labs threaten S&P 500 valuations
stories.Summary:
The United States government recently closed a long-standing loophole that previously allowed Chinese artificial intelligence labs to gain remote access to advanced American chips sold overseas. This policy shift occurred around November 2026 and has already caused the Hang Seng Tech Index to tumble 13 percent over two weeks. The e-commerce giant Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. suffered significantly because it rented compute from Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based operator. This specific operator is currently at the center of an alleged espionage scandal involving the chipmaker Nvidia Corp.

These restrictions may force the S&P 500 to retreat to about 5,600, which would represent a 19 percent decline. Such a drop could happen if consensus earnings estimates return to their 30-year trend and the price-to-earnings ratio falls to a long-term average of 17 times. The situation is complicated by the fact that semiconductors are expected to deliver more than half of S&P 500 earnings growth next year. Nvidia, the largest earnings contributor to the index, is still expected to generate 73 percent revenue growth over the next fiscal year.

Goldman Sachs Group Inc. warned that a return to normal corporate profits could deliver a double blow of weaker earnings and lower valuations. The US Securities and Exchange Commission is also investigating the accounting practices of Nvidia following a policy change in October 2025. This change involved reporting revenue based on customer headquarters rather than billing locations, which affected about 22 percent of sales billed through Singapore. Analysts worry that if the $104 billion billed through Singapore represented Chinese demand, a sizable chunk of revenue could disappear.

National security hawks in Washington are continuing to squeeze China despite the potential for significant economic damage to American firms. The global artificial intelligence value chain is so deeply integrated that it is almost impossible to diversify these risks away. Other industrial companies like Caterpillar Inc. and GE Vernova Inc. may see their orders diminish if capital investments in this sector slow down. The US will likely have to pay a hefty price for these actions as the trade becomes more pervasive.

stories.Headline: Noah Holdings hosts summit to discuss wealth security and asset allocation in the AI era
stories.Summary:
Noah Holdings Limited hosted the 19th Global Black Diamond Summit in Singapore starting November 23, 2026. The event drew hundreds of clients from various countries and regions to explore wealth security. Representatives from global asset management firms, business, government, and academia also attended the gathering. The summit focused on asset allocation and long-term investment judgments during the AI era. This specific event in Singapore was titled The Anchorage and ended on November 25, 2026.

The summit requires high-net-worth families to understand risk and avoid relying on any single future view. It focuses on the Singapore headquarters of Noah Holdings and its global Chinese family clients. The event theme was Safe Passage, Wider Horizons, and it addressed balancing growth with protection. Participants discussed how AI brings both opportunities and divergent views while markets fluctuated throughout the year. The gathering maintains a private character built over the past 18 years of annual events.

Chairwoman Norah Wang said families must understand if their net AI exposure is positive or negative. She stated that underlying cash flows may carry hidden concentration risk for families wealthy on paper. CEO Zander Yin said disciplined asset allocation helps maintain perspective when markets diverge and fluctuate. Yin noted that Noah uses AI to turn two decades of industry knowledge into institutional intelligence. He claimed that continued research and prudent judgment are needed to identify long-term opportunities.

Professor David Lee suggested evaluating asset allocation by a family's ability to meet financial commitments. He said families should assess liquidity needs using dates and currencies of debts and education expenses. Former MP Seng Han Thong noted that the second generation values investment autonomy and professional management. Former Ambassador Chan Heng Chee said the new world order would be an asymmetric multipolar order. These speakers addressed entrepreneurs to help them assess emerging opportunities in Asia and globally.

The articles state that Noah Holdings was founded in 2005 and is headquartered in Singapore. The firm has allocated more than 153 billion US dollars in cumulative assets for clients. It operates across nine countries and regions using three platforms for investment and legacy planning. An October 2026 CIO report observed that technological success is not the same as investment success. The firm provides integrated services supported by an AI platform and licensed professional teams.

The Tide will occur in Silicon Valley from December 14 to 15, 2026, to explore productivity. The Launch will take place in Hong Kong from January 18 to 20, 2027. Reunion gatherings are scheduled for Tokyo on November 28 and Vancouver on December 2, 2026. A final reunion event will happen in Melbourne during the last week of January 2027. The articles leave open the specific outcomes of the upcoming 2027 principal allocation themes.

stories.Headline: AI builder Will Thomas sees his model beat him in Fantasy Premier League
stories.Summary:
Will Thomas has played Fantasy Premier League for over 15 years, and last season the AI he built finished above him for the first time. He told Reuters it was a bit of a surreal moment and that he thought he was being beaten by his own creation. Thomas is an Englishman and the CEO and founder of Scoreline.ai, which delivers subscriber-based content including data, insight and analytics for fantasy sports players. Among its products is Fantasy Football Hub, which has around 60,000 paying subscribers and focuses on FPL, the official fantasy competition of the English Premier League. FPL offers match tickets and replica kits as prizes and had over 13 million registered teams in the 2025-26 season.

Scoreline.ai's purpose-built model finished in the top 0.5 per cent of those teams, ranking 67,829th in the world. A Reuters analysis of nine FPL teams, seven of which were run on the directions of AI chatbots, showed the chatbot teams scored an average of 499 points in the first eight gameweeks of the 2026-27 FPL season. The chatbot teams were operated by Scout Digital, a sports marketing firm that gives each separate chatbot the same instructions every week and, in most cases, has a staff member log in to carry out its decisions. Their performances were in line with the average human benchmark of 502, but about 75 points below the average of the top 1,000 human players. Scout Digital said newer versions of each AI model are used as they are released.

Thomas said there are still human managers beating the model, but it is getting harder to do, and he has a PhD in team leadership at the University of Sussex. Scout Digital managing director Mike Lewis said that so far they are two seasons in and the improvement they have seen is huge. Lewis said that in 2025-26 Scout Statto comfortably won, and that this season is looking neck and neck. Daniel Groos, head of AI at Groos Analytics, who built the open-source forecasting model OpenFPL, said the hardest question remains whether a player will even be in action on any particular gameweek and not dropped, rested or injured. Jonas Sand Labakk, the 2023-24 FPL champion, told Reuters that where you need human input is the expected minutes for players, because rotation, injuries and managerial choices are where he thinks the models miss the most.

Groos added that overall machines have an advantage because humans tend to be influenced by a spectacular performance, media narratives or a favourite player. The chatbot teams make about as few transfers as the best human managers, and the gap in transfer volume is small. The chatbot teams' captain picks trail those of the top 1,000 human players, and they also leave more points on the bench than the typical manager. The top 1,000 do not play against the grain, owning more popular players than the average manager, not fewer, which undercuts the idea that beating the field takes contrarian bets. Thomas also argues that the machines are weakest at the start of a season, when new managers and players give the models little data, and that fans of specific teams may have a slight insight advantage.

However, the early numbers do not clearly show that. The chatbot teams Reuters analysed were level with the official average in gameweek 1 of this season, pulled ahead in gameweek 2, and had dipped just below it by gameweek 8. According to industry research, Thomas is one of around 245 million people who play fantasy sports, where players take the role of manager or coach and build a virtual team made up of athletes whose real-life performances earn them points. As a control, Scout Digital also has a team titled Scout Statto, which is managed by the firm's co-founder Simon Gold and run without the use of AI tools. Beginning this season, FPL features its own conversational AI assistant titled FPL Companion.

While some predict a future where fantasy sports become a battleground purely for competing versions of AI, Groos does not expect the human element to disappear completely. Groos said the winning formula may turn out to be neither human intuition nor AI-based insights, but a combination of both. Labakk echoed that, adding that he thinks the best possible way is an engaged manager with the models rather than an AI with the models. Marcus Adebayo, 34, a software project manager from South London, uses Gemini by letting it do the structural heavy lifting but picks the team himself. Adebayo said treating it as a co-pilot works brilliantly, provided you are honest enough to admit that when the plane hits turbulence, it is usually because you grabbed the controls.

The company said the series uses cloud capabilities and AI technologies to help organizations make better use of their know-how. stories.Headline: HPE shares fall as rising AI server costs shrink margins despite strong revenue forecast
stories.Summary:
Shares of Hewlett Packard Enterprise fell about 16 per cent on Tuesday, November 24, as investors focused on the company's shrinking margins amid soaring costs, even though strong AI demand boosted its full-year revenue outlook. The stock had more than doubled this year through Monday's close, but it was set to lose about $10 billion in market value if the losses held. On Monday, HPE had soared more than 17 per cent as an Nvidia-fueled rally lifted AI stocks. The drop came as the company's upbeat forecast was overshadowed by concerns about profitability in its AI business.

HPE forecast an adjusted operating margin for the fiscal year ending October 2027 of between 14 per cent and 15 per cent, down from 15.1 per cent in fiscal 2026. At its Cloud and AI unit, which includes servers and storage and is a key growth driver, HPE expects an annual fiscal margin of about 14 per cent, down from 15.2 per cent in the previous fiscal year. Robust demand for AI servers helped drive a 50 per cent jump in HPE's fourth-quarter revenue to $14.55 billion, topping estimates. The company now expects fiscal 2027 revenue growth between 27 per cent and 35 per cent, up from its earlier forecast of 13 per cent to 17 per cent.

HPE finance chief Marie Myers said on an earnings call that costs were rising faster than pricing and that margins would take a hit in the second half of the year as the company ships more AI servers. Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B Riley Wealth, said that when input costs go up and not enough is passed along, margins have to take a hit, and that this clearly showed. He added that this raises concerns that pricing tailwinds are beginning to fade, and that supply shortages expected through 2028 will take a bite out of margins. Bob O'Donnell, chief analyst at TECHnalysis Research, said the market seems acutely sensitive to any potential changes in profit margins at tech companies these days, and that HPE's solid numbers and robust forecast certainly did not seem to justify the market's reaction that day.
