stories.Headline: China leads development of 78 international AI standards
stories.Summary:
The State Administration for Market Regulation announced on Tuesday that China has spearheaded the development of 78 international standards for artificial intelligence. This initiative aims to transform the country's technological innovations and industrial practices into global public goods for the international community. The effort involves a combination of foundational guidelines and specific applications to improve the overall architecture of global AI standards. These developments reflect a systematic approach to integrating advanced technology into the real economy across various sectors. The State Administration for Market Regulation led the creation of 29 foundational and common international standards covering security, trustworthiness, data governance, and human-computer interaction.

Additionally, the agency coordinated 15 technical standards bodies to develop 49 international standards for sector-specific applications like intelligent manufacturing and smart cities. Other key areas of focus for these application standards include smart logistics and smart water management to drive scaled implementation. The agency also collaborated with multiple countries to create a guideline for addressing risks in generative AI, such as model poisoning and deepfakes. This specific guideline is claimed by the agency to be the world's first international standards proposal targeting the governance of generative AI. Sun Wei, the deputy head of the department of standards innovation under the State Administration for Market Regulation, provided these details during a news conference.

He stated that the agency has made active efforts to help improve the international standards system architecture for artificial intelligence. Sun explained that China's application-oriented standards provide practical solutions and technical frameworks that support inclusive and shared digital transformation. He further noted that these efforts offer a basis for wider international adoption to support the development of the real economy. The agency believes these guidelines can provide essential support for forming a global consensus on the management of AI risks. More to follow.

Articles.Title: China leads development of 78 international standards on AI - China Daily Global Edition

stories.headline_source: China leads development of 78 international standards on AI

stories.Headline: China Meteorological Administration and Shanghai AI Lab launch ZHU·GE platform for Earth science research
stories.Summary:
The China Meteorological Administration and the Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory unveiled an AI-powered Earth system research platform on Monday, November 24, 2026. This new system, named ZHU·GE, was introduced during the 2026 Xiong'an International Symposium on Meteorological AI in Hebei province. The platform aims to accelerate the transition from initial research ideas to verified scientific findings within the field of Earth system science. It allows researchers to state their goals in natural language so the system can autonomously analyze literature, write code, and conduct experiments.

The ZHU·GE platform integrates approximately 10 petabytes of public scientific data and 1 petabyte of data authorized by the China Meteorological Administration. It also utilizes around 2 million literature records, more than 5,000 code tools, and over 10 general scientific research skills. The system supports the entire research process, including mechanism studies, forecasting-method development, and the optimization of both numerical and AI models. It employs stringent access controls and operational isolation to ensure data security while recording hypotheses and results to prevent incorrect research directions.

Zeng Qin, director-general of the Department of Science and Technology of the China Meteorological Administration, compared the platform to the ancient strategist Zhuge Liang. He stated that the system does more than provide advice by taking action to help researchers locate data and produce testable evidence. Ling Fenghua, head of the Astronomy and Earth Sciences Center at the Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory, noted that the platform features self-correction mechanisms. Ling explained that the system allows experimental evidence to inform decision-making rather than simply following preset steps.

The development team is currently optimizing data access and multi-agent collaboration to improve the analysis of satellite images, radar echoes, and weather charts. The China Meteorological Administration intends to create a research exchange community where scientists can publish results and seek peer review. The platform will be rolled out to meteorological research and operational departments across China. The administration also mentioned that they will explore providing international services for the platform in the future.

Articles.Title: New platform brings AI agents into Earth science research - China Daily Global Edition

stories.Headline: India should prepare to reuse AI infrastructure after a market crash, Arindam Goswami argues
stories.Summary:
The artificial intelligence infrastructure boom has shifted from using cash to relying on debt, according to a report by Arindam Goswami. This transition occurred as large technology firms struggled to prove that the technology was boosting their earnings. American non-financial companies issued 940 billion dollars of investment-grade bonds in the first ten months of 2026, which was a third more than the previous year. The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.5 percent on 5 November, while Nvidia reported revenue growth of 103 percent twelve days later. These events indicate that companies now have less time to prove the worth of their massive investments.

Fitch Ratings warned on 17 November that borrowing by the largest technology firms will make bond markets more volatile next year. The agency says markets expect the five largest hyperscalers to spend over 1 trillion dollars in 2027, up from 772 billion dollars this year. Until 2024, firms like Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, and Meta paid for data centres using profits from software, cloud, and advertising. Now, these profits cover a shrinking share of the investment, forcing companies to borrow to finance the rest. An October stability report from the IMF counted 14 deals since 2023 where large firms put 300 billion dollars of equity and 650 billion dollars of debt into weaker AI companies.

Arindam Goswami, a research analyst at The Takshashila Institution, suggests that India should prepare to use the infrastructure left behind after a potential crash. He argues that India has little capital at stake and would barely feel a sharp correction in the market. He recommends that the IndiaAI Mission tilt its compute budget toward inference in hubs with existing power and fibre infrastructure. He also suggests that public funds adapt open-weight models to Indian languages, health data, court records, and farm advisories. Finally, he believes the government should set common standards for interfaces and liability, similar to what was done for UPI payments.

The current cycle faces political pushback, such as voters rejecting data-centre-friendly measures in the 3 November midterms. In the eastern US PJM grid region, data centres added 9.3 billion dollars to power capacity costs in a single year. OpenAI pledged on 5 November to pay the full cost of power at its own campuses following these political shifts. McKinsey's State of AI 2026 survey found that while almost nine in 10 firms use AI, only 37 percent see an effect on earnings. This suggests that the real constraint is the slow pace at which organisations redesign their workflows and legacy systems.

Articles.Title: The AI boom now runs on debt. India should plan for what it leaves behind

stories.headline_source: The AI boom now runs on debt. India should plan for what it leaves behind

stories.Headline: Foreign executives say AI and innovation boost productivity in China
stories.Summary:
Foreign business executives shared their perspectives on how technological innovation and artificial intelligence boost productivity following the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting on November 19 in Shenzhen. These leaders discussed how China's continued opening-up and its integration of artificial intelligence into the real economy create new opportunities for companies across the Asia-Pacific region. They highlighted that strengths in green technologies and advanced manufacturing are helping to accelerate the ongoing green transition and deepen regional commercial ties. The executives believe that building more resilient and sustainable growth across the region is a broader opportunity than focusing on individual markets.

The current business landscape requires multinational companies to leverage advanced technology and talent to stay close to Chinese consumers in an open market. Alan Li of CBRE China noted that new office leasing by foreign companies in major cities rose 26 percent year-on-year during the first half of 2026. This growth was led by the consumer sectors with a 34 percent increase and financial and professional services with a 31 percent increase. Many of these clients come from the life sciences, advanced equipment, and new energy vehicle components industries. These changes allow companies to combine global expertise with local innovation to contribute to shared growth across the globe.

Several executives explained how their specific organizations are responding to these evolving market conditions and technological shifts. Rose Zhu of Deutsche Bank China stated that the opening of financial markets facilitates capital flows and strengthens trade links between China, Europe, and the Middle East. Hendrik Kohleick of Henkel Asia-Pacific said that demand for new materials is being driven by fast-growing sectors like humanoid robotics, data centers, and e-mobility. Teh-han Chow of Fonterra Greater China mentioned that consumers now seek higher-quality products with greater health benefits as China enters a phase of high-quality development. He credited the growth of his company to a gold standard free trade agreement between New Zealand and China.

The executives believe that greater market access and trade facilitation help bring solutions validated in China to customers around the world. They argue that connecting complementary strengths through stable cooperation and open trade creates lasting value for all participating economies. By utilizing diverse application scenarios and a strong industrial ecosystem, companies can accelerate the testing and adoption of new technologies at scale. These leaders suggest that the integration of regional markets will continue to reshape how multinational companies operate within the Asia-Pacific region. They aim to turn these opportunities into sustainable growth by connecting clients with international networks.

Articles.Title: Innovation, AI boosting foreign companies - China Daily Global Edition

stories.Headline: Bloomberg columnist warns US officials against aggressive AI chip restrictions on China
stories.Summary:
United States government officials recently closed a long-standing loophole that previously allowed Chinese artificial intelligence labs to access advanced American chips remotely. This policy change occurred around November 2026 and aimed to restrict the ability of China to develop its artificial intelligence capabilities. The move caused the Hang Seng Tech Index to drop 13 percent over two weeks, led by the e-commerce company Alibaba Group. Alibaba had been renting compute from Megaspeed International, a Singapore-based operator involved in an alleged espionage scandal with Nvidia.

These restrictions require American chipmakers to sever ties with Chinese entities and may change how companies report their global revenue. Nvidia changed its accounting policy in October 2025 to report revenue based on customer headquarters rather than billing locations. This change is significant because Singapore previously accounted for about 22 percent of total sales for Nvidia. Advanced Micro Devices also faces pressure as China represented 22 percent of its revenue in 2025. These companies must now navigate strict export controls while facing allegations that blacklisted Chinese firms still receive firmware updates.

National security hawks in Washington are responsible for these curbs and believe that squeezing China is necessary for security. However, Bloomberg columnist Shuli Ren suggests that officials should exercise caution because the global artificial intelligence value chain is deeply integrated. Ren argues that it is almost impossible to diversify risks away and that the United States will pay a hefty price. The author notes that any hit to chipmakers would reverberate far beyond Silicon Valley and hurt broader corporate profits.

The context of this situation involves a broader market concern that earnings for American chipmakers may have already peaked. Goldman Sachs warned that the S&P 500 could retreat to about 5,600 if earnings estimates revert to their 30-year trend. Investors are worried that companies like Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices cannot meet aggressive growth expectations. Future declines in artificial intelligence investments could also diminish orders for industrial companies like Caterpillar and GE Vernova. More to follow.

Articles.Title: US officials keen to squeeze China's AI dreams should exercise caution—here's why

stories.headline_source: US officials keen to squeeze China's AI dreams should exercise caution—here's why

stories.Headline: Tiruchi colleges train faculty to teach AI and machine learning
stories.Summary:
Higher education institutions in Tiruchi have begun integrating emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence and machine learning into their syllabi and into capacity building programmes for teachers and students in recent years, The Hindu reported on November 24, 2026. A growing number of institutes are opting for faculty development programmes that focus on how to integrate AI and ML in the pedagogy as well. The Tiruchi-based tech company Bodhi Multiverse UK has conducted six AI-related faculty development programmes for city colleges this year, according to its founder and director Anantha Ganesh. Capacity building programmes for educational institutions in Tiruchi typically cost upwards of ₹850 per person depending on the course and duration.

Many institutions offer degree programmes in emerging technologies, but there is a shortage of faculty qualified to teach them, the article said. Kevin Giftson, founder and CEO of Aske AI, a company that conducts tech learning modules for colleges, developers and healthcare professionals, said the syllabus has not been updated to cater to the new subjects, which has created problems for both students and teachers. He said it would be better for students to start industrial internships in the first year of their course so that they can get exposure to the technologies in real time. At National College, teachers are encouraged to complete at least two modules in emerging technologies every year through Massive Open Online Courses offered on government portals.

Ganesh said that though there is a buzz over the entry of AI into the classroom at present, it is not actually a new phenomenon, as it has existed in multiple forms before and is still developing newer versions. He said the best results are mainly down to prompting the machine, and that if one learns how to give an AI prompt one can create a product successfully and personalise it as well. He said the rapid increase in the number of AI tools and software can be frustrating for users and creators, but the company expects this to stabilise in the coming years. D. Prasanna Balaji, principal of National College, said that though AI and ML help to present lessons in an appealing manner, they cannot replace the teacher in making students actually understand what is being taught, and that the human factor is still important for the student's educational progress.

Articles.Title: Tiruchi colleges train faculty and students to adapt to AI, ML in classroom

stories.Headline: Apurva.ai opens call for development organisations to submit persistent challenges
stories.Summary:
Apurva.ai, a unit of the C4EC Foundation co-founded by Nilekani Philanthropies and supported by Rohini and Nandan Nilekani, launched an Open Call to Reimagine on November 24, 2026, according to The Hindu. The call invites development organisations to identify persistent challenges and explore new approaches to addressing them. The initiative seeks to engage NGOs, social enterprises, funders and other organisations working on complex social challenges where conventional approaches have struggled to deliver desired outcomes. A spokesperson for Apurva.ai said some problems do not need another solution but a different way of thinking.

Through the open call, participating organisations can submit one persistent challenge relating to programme implementation, impact measurement, knowledge management or organisational workflows. The exercise will examine existing processes, institutional knowledge and community experiences to identify alternative approaches, including opportunities where emerging technologies such as AI could contribute. The organisation cited the example of impact assessments that can take seven to ten months to complete, saying that by the time findings become available, community needs and priorities may have changed, limiting their usefulness in programme decisions. Apurva.ai currently works with over 50 organisations globally, using AI-powered products to connect community knowledge, research and institutional learning.

The articles do not say who is responsible for running the open call beyond Apurva.ai itself, and they give no closing date, selection process or further timeline for it. The only statement attributed to the organisation is the spokesperson's remark that some problems need a different way of thinking, along with the example of slow impact assessments. The articles do not say what happens after organisations submit their challenges or when results might be announced. More to follow.

stories.Headline: US prosecutors say ex-OpenAI engineer Alfozan likely recorded meetings to capture trade secrets
stories.Summary:
US prosecutors claim that former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan likely captured trade secrets by secretly recording meetings in an office conference room. The Justice Department reports that staff discovered a sophisticated recording device hidden behind a television in an executive conference room in October. Alfozan had worked for the artificial intelligence company since July 2025 and was fired on the day of his arrest. He has pleaded not guilty to the eavesdropping charge and is currently detained while the criminal case proceeds.

The government alleges that Alfozan used a hidden bug to intercept dozens of conversations throughout September 2026. Investigators found hundreds of audio files and AI transcripts on his personal computer that were meticulously categorized by date and content. Some of these recordings were allegedly uploaded to the cloud platform Dropbox for storage. Prosecutors also discovered a photograph on his mobile phone of a confidential term sheet for a strategic partnership between OpenAI and another company.

The US government argues that Alfozan should remain in custody because he has considerable resources and connections in Saudi Arabia. Prosecutors stated that he was in frequent communication with people affiliated with the Saudi government while he was recording and transcribing meetings. Alfozan has denied that he was stealing trade secrets for Saudi Arabia and is seeking bail set at one million US dollars. His lawyer argued in a November 20 filing that the defendant has no covert ties to the Saudi government.

US District Judge Vince Chhabria previously expressed concern about whether Alfozan should stay in custody without more serious criminal charges. In a filing dated November 23, prosecutors urged the judge to deny the latest request for the defendant to be released on bail. They claim that his relatively weak ties to the United States make him a flight risk before the trial. A hearing regarding the bond request was scheduled for November 24 in San Francisco.

Articles.Title: Detained ex-OpenAI engineer likely captured secrets on hidden bug, US says

stories.Headline: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urges global cooperation to establish AI guardrails
stories.Summary:
United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called for effective cooperation to establish guardrails for artificial intelligence on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. He delivered these remarks during a Security Council open debate focused on conflict resolution within an era of rapid technological change. The leader argued that artificial intelligence is reshaping security, societies, and economies faster than current institutions can adapt. He suggested that the Global Dialogue on AI Governance and the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI are essential tools for this cooperation.

This effort requires agreeing on common baselines for frontier systems and common methods to evaluate and verify risks. Guterres stated that the world needs safeguards for those risks and a multilateral framework for risk management backed by independent oversight. He insisted that accountability must extend to the companies building these systems, comparing the need for standards to those in aviation, medicine, and nuclear energy. The Secretary-General also urged the urgent launch of negotiations for a legally binding instrument regarding lethal autonomous weapons systems.

Guterres warned that unregulated technology poses three specific risks to international peace and security. He noted that AI is driving greater autonomy in military functions and could lead to catastrophe if integrated with nuclear command systems. He also claimed that AI has turbocharged the spread of falsehoods, which undermines trust in political processes and fuels polarization. Finally, he argued that commercial interests and geopolitical rivalry have sparked an uncontrolled race for the energy, water, and minerals that power data centers.

The UN chief stated that countries with the greatest capabilities carry the greatest responsibility to ensure competition does not destabilize peace. He expressed concern over the concentration of power in a few companies and countries, which leaves many developing states with little say in their futures. Guterres concluded that power must answer to law and that humans must always retain control over life and death decisions. He emphasized that the Security Council has a special duty to prevent an AI divide from instigating other types of global divides.

Articles.Title: UN chief calls for cooperation to set up guardrails for AI - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Podcast guests examine how AI politics and data centre protests shape South-east Asia growth
stories.Summary:
The Green Pulse podcast episode published on November 24, 2026, featured host Audrey Tan discussing with ST tech editor Irene Tham and Rajesh Sreenivasan, a partner at Rajah & Tann Singapore, how artificial intelligence has moved from a software issue into domestic politics and international relations. The episode examined what the global rise of AI and the data centres built to power it will mean for South-east Asia and its own plans to build more such facilities. It also looked at how the developing region will balance that growth against the environmental impact of data centres, which the episode said is driving protests globally. The discussion covered how AI evolved from a technology topic into a geopolitical one, and whether South-east Asia could see more protests against data centres. The episode asked whether the Nvidia controversy and United States efforts to clamp down on chip exports would act as a natural brake on the global expansion of data centres.

It also explored why Singapore chose to make environmental sustainability a key consideration for data centres alongside cyber security. The discussion covered what Singapore's digital infrastructure bill is about, and how data centres can contribute to the development of water and renewable energy infrastructure. The episode did not give further numbers, dates or names on these points. Sreenivasan is identified as a partner and the head of technology, media and telecommunications at the law firm Rajah & Tann Singapore, and Tham as ST's tech editor. The episode framed the spread of AI into politics and international relations as something that has dominated headlines globally.

It presented the protests against data centres and their environmental impact as a global phenomenon that the region will have to weigh against its growth plans. The podcast is hosted by Tan and produced and edited by Hadyu Rahim, with Ernest Luis and Zachary Lim as executive producers. The episode is part of Green Pulse, which is described as a podcast published every Tuesday to discuss how environmental issues intersect with business, politics and society. It was published on November 24, 2026, at 10:00 AM and updated at the same time. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the questions the episode raised.

stories.Headline: Jera weighs an IPO to fund expansion as AI drives power demand
stories.Summary:
Jera, the largest producer of electricity in Japan, announced on November 23, 2026, that it is considering various ways to raise funds for expansion. The company is weighing a possible initial public offering to secure the capital needed for its growth. This decision comes as the boom in artificial intelligence creates a new source of global power consumption. The company believes that this technological shift supports the case for increased investment in the power sector. The company requires significant cash to build new power stations and strengthen its liquefied natural gas terminals.

Jera previously unveiled a 5 trillion yen investment plan in May 2024 that focuses on hydrogen, ammonia, and renewable energy through 2035. It is now reassessing how it raises capital because of the growth of data centers, which it calls a new dimension. One specific project involves a 400-megawatt data center near its Chiba thermal power station with an expected investment of 15 billion dollars. This project is a collaboration with RHAELM Holdings and Dell Technologies to develop necessary AI infrastructure. Yukio Kani, the chairman and global chief executive officer of Jera, stated that the company needs a lot of cash for the whole LNG value chain.

He explained that the rapid development of AI is increasing the need to secure funds for expansion. When asked about the current status of a listing, Kani declined to provide specific details. He noted that Jera is currently talking to its shareholders about ways to maximize the value of the company. Kani believes there is huge potential because the company operates across shipping, trading, and upstream projects. More to follow.

The country's manufacturing industry benefited from this boom, which helped buoy electronics exports. This economic expansion occurred during the third quarter of the year 2026. The city-state now expects its economy to expand between 2.5 and 4.5 percent in 2027.

This future projection comes as uncertainty looms over the global technology sector. The growth in the third quarter was driven largely by the electronics sector. These figures reflect the impact of the global artificial intelligence trend on local production. The official data provided the details regarding the growth of the Singaporean economy.

The reports indicate that the manufacturing sector was a primary driver of the recent increase. These findings highlight how electronics exports have responded to the worldwide demand for new technology. The government data confirms the specific percentage of growth for the third quarter. stories.Headline: Australian Foreign Minister warns AI is transforming global economic and strategic power
stories.Summary:
Australian Foreign Affairs Minister Penny Wong spoke to the federal parliament on Tuesday, November 24, regarding the rapid rise of artificial intelligence. She warned that this specific technology is currently transforming the foundations and the dimensions of global economic and strategic power. According to Wong, these emerging technologies are spreading and disrupting the world faster than any previous revolutionary tools. She believes that these changes are reordering lives, economies, and militaries in ways that people cannot fully foresee. The Australian government announced in November that it will introduce new mandatory safeguards for developers of frontier artificial intelligence.

These new rules will require AI developers to report breaches and allow independent safety evaluations of their models. A new regulator will enforce these safeguards and hold the power to impose significant penalties against companies that fail to comply. Minister Wong stated that Australia welcomes investment and innovation in this field on terms that work for all Australians. Penny Wong expressed that Australia intends to work with international partners to ensure that the race for AI development does not reward speed over prudence.

She argued that the world must build trust between countries and cooperate effectively when things go wrong. The minister believes that the global response to these advancements must match the immense power of the technology. She emphasized the need for a balanced approach to maintain safety while pursuing technological growth. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Nikkei index jumps 5 percent as investors buy AI and semiconductor stocks
stories.Summary:
Japan's benchmark Nikkei stock index experienced a significant surge of 5 percent on Tuesday morning, November 24, 2026. This rapid increase was driven by heavy buying of shares related to semiconductors and artificial intelligence. Investors showed renewed optimism over the AI sector, which pushed the market higher after a national holiday on Monday. Many traders also stepped in to buy back shares following a plunge of more than 5 percent late last week. By the end of the morning session, the 225-issue Nikkei Stock Average had risen by 2,239.14 points.

This gain represented a 3.97 percent increase from Friday, bringing the index to a total of 58,675.79. The rally required a shift in investor sentiment toward technology stocks to reverse the previous losses. These specific movements in the chip and AI sectors were the primary drivers of the index's recovery. Brokers stated that the gains followed a sharp rally on Wall Street that occurred overnight.

Investors welcomed new developments involving the U.S. AI chipmaker Nvidia Corp, which helped ease concerns over the company's future outlook. This positive momentum in the United States encouraged Japanese investors to return to the market with confidence. stories.Headline: Malaysia develops crisis protocols and response mechanisms for high-risk AI
stories.Summary:
Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo informed the parliament on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, that Malaysia is developing crisis protocols and mandatory response mechanisms. These measures aim to protect the safety and well-being of people using artificial intelligence, especially within high-risk areas. The government intends to identify risk patterns through sectoral monitoring to determine how these mechanisms should function. One specific concern involves interactive chatbots and AI companions that might cause children to develop emotional dependence.

The proposed AI Governance Bill will introduce a reporting mechanism for AI incidents to help the government analyze vulnerabilities and risk patterns. This system will allow officials to introduce or improve safeguards over time by integrating with existing sectoral expertise channels. Gobind Singh Deo stated that this coordination will include the Health Ministry for mental health and the Women, Family and Community Development Ministry for social protection. Additionally, the government is creating the Malaysia AI Safety Institute under AI Malaysia to improve national capabilities regarding safety.

The new institute will focus on the research, testing, and assessment of safety risks associated with artificial intelligence. It will also work toward developing appropriate evaluation methods and safety standards for all sectors that require attention. Minister Gobind Singh Deo explained that these integrated efforts are designed to avoid overlapping functions across different government departments. By combining legislative actions with technical research, the state hopes to better manage the emerging challenges of AI technology.

stories.Headline: China provides AI media training to Kenyan professionals to strengthen digital cooperation
stories.Summary:
China launched a two-day artificial intelligence media training program in Nairobi, Kenya, on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. The initiative aims to deepen media cooperation between China and Africa while strengthening overall technological capacity. This program brought together various technical, digital, creative, and production professionals from across the country of Kenya. It was organized by the Academy of Broadcasting Science and China's National Radio and Television Administration.

The workshop includes hands-on sessions and live demonstrations led by Chinese film directors and AI digital artists. These sessions cover content monetization, television commercial production, scriptwriting, and the creation of AI-powered programs. Through a partnership with the Academy of Broadcasting Science, the Kenya Broadcasting Corporation will receive 100 hours of Chinese programming. This organization will also receive technical support for its digitized historical archives and 40 complimentary AI accounts.

Zhang Zhizhong, minister counselor at the Chinese Embassy in Kenya, stated that media cooperation is a vital part of relations between the two nations. He noted that this training follows the China-Africa Cooperation Initiative on Radio, TV and Audio-Visual Innovation from the 2024 Beijing Summit. Shi Zhiyan of the National Radio and Television Administration said the goal is to help Kenyan practitioners grasp these technologies. He believes this will allow Kenya to tell local stories and ensure African voices are not left behind.

Carol Wachira of Royal Media Services said that this cooperation will provide local broadcasters with modern tools while protecting cultural authenticity. She mentioned that collaborating with China allows Kenyan media to scale digital innovation and gain new insights. This effort is intended to ensure that African perspectives are effectively represented in a global media landscape driven by AI. The program seeks to help Kenya take its own seat at the AI table.

Articles.Title: China launches AI media training in Kenya to boost digital cooperation - Xinhua

stories.Headline: Anthropic grows Claude use tenfold in Japan through corporate sales push
stories.Summary:
The use of the Claude artificial intelligence model by Japanese organizations and companies has increased tenfold over the past year. This significant growth occurred because of a growing recognition of the capabilities of the technology. The American company Anthropic drove this expansion by focusing its sales efforts on corporate clients. These strategic business moves have allowed the firm to establish a stronger presence within the Japanese market. The enterprise focus of the American firm has led to several high profile partnerships with major Japanese corporations.

These specific collaborations include agreements with the companies known as Hitachi, NEC, and Fujitsu. The articles do not provide specific dates for these partnerships or the exact number of users involved. No other numerical data regarding the requirements or changes resulting from this growth was mentioned. The growth is attributed to the strategic focus of Anthropic on selling its services to corporate clients.

The company has targeted large organizations to increase the adoption of its artificial intelligence model. While the articles mention the company's focus, they do not provide direct quotes from the responsible executives. The reports simply state that the corporate sales strategy led to the increased usage. More to follow.

stories.Headline: KAIVERSE debuts H3ARUS, a five-member AI boy group, with the single CRUSH
stories.Summary:
H3ARUS, described by its company KAIVERSE as the first five-member AI boy group, released its debut single "CRUSH" on various online music platforms on the 23rd and unveiled the official music video as it began full activities, according to a report by Son Bong-seok published on November 24, 2026. The group is built on a universe in which five secret agents disguise themselves as idols to carry out undercover missions, and its members have different personalities and voices. The name H3ARUS comes from "HEAR US" and is meant to say listen to our voices and stories, a meaning the company says reflects the members' individuality. The debut track is a disco-based pop funk song about the intense flutter and rapidly growing feelings of love at first sight, built on a lively rhythm and an elastic slap-bass sound. The song moves from the moment of being drawn to a stranger to the desire to grow closer, expressing first-love emotions in a candid and upbeat way, with distinctive member vocals blending into a dynamic chorus.

The music video follows the five members as they fall in love at first sight with one woman and each feel different excitement, expressing their feelings in different ways while gazing at the same person. The company presents the meticulously lifelike visuals, with the members' differing appearances and moods realized through AI technology, as a key viewing point of the video. KAIVERSE says the debut is meaningful as a first step introducing both the group's musical individuality and the appeal of its characters. KAIVERSE CEO Park Geun-woo said AI is merely a technology for realizing artists and that what matters in the end are the appeal of the music and the characters and the stories within them. He added that he hopes H3ARUS grows not as a mere technological outcome but as artists who make people enjoy the music, feel affection for the members and look forward to the next story.

KAIVERSE describes itself as an AI entertech company that develops artist IP based on AI technology and plans and produces content including music, music videos and dramas. The company says it has built production capabilities in AI video content, including producing the "OASIS" music video by Kim Jaejoong entirely with AI technology. KAIVERSE plans to expand the H3ARUS universe through content covering not only music and music videos but also each member, their relationships and the stories hidden behind idol activities. Building on its technological prowess and content production experience, the company plans to expand its in-house artist IP business beginning with H3ARUS. It says it will continue to present entertainment content that combines music, characters and storytelling.

Articles.Title: ‘Five-member AI boy group’ H3ARUS, stakes its claim on the K-pop scene with ‘CRUSH’

stories.Headline: South Korea egg prices climb back above 7000 won as avian flu spreads
stories.Summary:
The average retail price for 30 eggs in South Korea stood at 7068 won as of the 23rd, according to the Korea Agro-Fisheries & Food Trade Corporation, which was 6.3 percent higher than the 6650 won recorded a year earlier. After the price had dropped into the 6000-won range from mid last month to early this month, it climbed back into the 7000-won range, the article reported. The report, published on the 25th, said the rise reflects reduced discount support by large supermarket chains and the government as supply increased. The article also asked whether egg prices will rise again amid the spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza.

According to the Korea Rural Economic Institute, the average farm-gate price for 10 extra-large eggs was 1661 won in mid-month, which was 133 won lower than the same period a year earlier and 173 won lower than the 1834 won of mid last month. The institute projected that the average farm-gate price in late this month would be 10 to 30 won lower than in mid-month. It attributed the decline to an increase in the number of laying hens and in egg production, expecting 58.96 million laying hens this month, up 1.6 percent from a year earlier, and average daily egg production of about 50.4 million, around 1.9 percent higher than a year ago. Whether highly pathogenic AI spreads is a key variable for future egg prices, the article said.

In this winter season, highly pathogenic AI was first detected on the 3rd, and 10 cases were confirmed by the 24th, according to the article. Last year, following the first detection on September 12, there were six cumulative cases by November 24, so within three weeks of this season's first detection the cumulative number of cases surpassed the tally at the same point last year. The article said that if AI spreads and more laying hens are culled, egg supply could shrink again and push up consumer prices. It noted that the sharp rise in egg prices this year was also largely due to last year, when 62 highly pathogenic AI cases led to the culling of 11.34 million laying hens, tightening supply.

stories.Headline: Jiro debuts fully AI K-pop group Seoria with generated faces, voices and performances
stories.Summary:
Generative AI company Jiro introduced its fully AI-generated girl group Seoria at a press briefing in Seoul on Tuesday, presenting the four-member act as its first original AI entertainment property and a showcase for its Dropshot AI platform. Seoria, whose members are named Riye, Cora, Iseol and Freya, debuted in August with the song "Burning," and every part of the group, including its faces, voices and performances, is generated using artificial intelligence rather than performed by hidden humans. Jiro co-CEO Hwang Gil-hwan said the company wanted to attempt the most difficult thing possible and to show how far its technology could be pushed, describing the creation of an attractive person as an extremely difficult task. The company said Seoria's video content had accumulated 2.54 million views as of early November, including 1.08 million for its debut music video, and that the group landed its first brand collaboration with athleisure company Andar in October.

Jiro said it spent four months taking Seoria from initial concept to debut, generating around 5,000 character images and tens of thousands of video clips while testing whether its platform could keep characters consistent and humanlike across different content. The company built the group much like a conventional K-pop act, giving the members distinct personalities and positions and a fantasy universe inspired by a legend about a secret female warrior group from the Goryeo kingdom, which spanned 918 to 1392, and it also produced album artwork, a custom typeface, dance challenges, variety-style videos and behind-the-scenes content. Jiro co-CEO Lee Jae-seok said AI idols are not bound by the same spatial, physical or time constraints as human performers, and he said the company plans to keep releasing music while expanding Seoria into animation, films, livestreaming, advertising and other content. Music critic Lim Hee-yun said AI idols face none of the human risks associated with private-life controversies or military enlistment and that content can be produced rapidly without the usual limits of time, place or language.

Lim also said K-pop fandoms form deep bonds through personal interaction with artists, and he said whether a being created entirely by AI can move beyond temporary curiosity and keep a loyal fandom over the long term still has to be proven. On Tuesday, the Korea Music Copyright Association proposed three principles for the AI era, namely responsible AI training, protection of artists' rights and fair distribution and compensation, arguing that commercial AI training should in principle require prior permission and agreed compensation. The association also called for clearer distinctions between fully AI-generated music and music made with AI assistance, while questions over how such music should be registered and compensated remain unsettled. The association is set to hold a public hearing on Monday to discuss issues including how much human creative contribution should be required for AI-assisted works to qualify for registration, as well as standards for royalty collection and distribution.

Articles.Title: After virtual idols, could fully AI-generated stars be K-pop’s next frontier?

stories.Headline: Hanwha Aerospace builds a defense AI data center in Changwon for 2028 operations
stories.Summary:
Hanwha Aerospace announced on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, that it is building a defense AI data center in Changwon, South Gyeongsang Province. The company briefed officials from the Defense Acquisition Program Administration and the National AI Strategy Committee, including Vice Chair Ha Jung-woo, at the construction site. This project is part of a larger 55 trillion won investment plan that Executive Vice Chair Kim Dong-kwan announced in July. The company intends to use its own power generation assets to expand these data center operations both in South Korea and abroad.

The first phase of this specific project has been allocated 10 trillion won, which is approximately 7.5 billion dollars. Hanwha Aerospace targets initial operations for July 2028 and plans to equip the completed center with high-density GPU servers. The facility is designed to reach an eventual capacity of 180 megawatts to support its defense AI goals. The company is also considering the possibility of including these data centers in future defense export packages.

Hanwha stated that a dedicated facility is necessary because of the military's security requirements and the need for uninterrupted operations. They are considering a model where the military retains control of its data while defense contractors operate the facility. The company claims this approach could accelerate the adoption of defense AI by four to five years over a government-led project. An official said the facility would be foundational national infrastructure that helps solidify the position of Korea among the world's top four defense powers.

Articles.Title: Hanwha to establish defense AI data center in Changwon

stories.Headline: South Korean asset managers hold back on Anthropic as AI sell-off deepens
stories.Summary:
South Korean asset managers are taking a cautious approach to Anthropic, in contrast to their rush to embrace SpaceX, despite the Claude chatbot developer's stock market debut on Nasdaq last week. Nineteen South Korean exchange-traded funds had added Anthropic shares by the second trading day after that debut, and their combined holdings were valued at 88 billion won, or $65.5 million. By comparison, the value of SpaceX shares held by 15 domestic ETFs stood at 597 billion won on the second trading day after its June listing, nearly seven times the Anthropic figure. Only one ETF has allocated more than 10 percent of its portfolio to Anthropic, while all the other funds held allocations below 5 percent. The Kodex US AI Agent Active ETF, managed by Samsung Asset Management, had the largest exposure at 19.4 percent, making the startup its second-largest holding.

The Time US Nasdaq 100 Active ETF, the largest fund among the 19 run by Timefolio Asset Management, allocated just 0.6 percent to Anthropic, making it the fund's 44th-largest holding out of 45 stocks. The cautious approach reflects growing uncertainty in global AI markets, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq falling more than 5 percent on Friday and entering correction territory. That sell-off spilled over into Korea, where the Kospi fell below 4,600 intraday on Monday, more than 50 percent below its June 19 intraday record high of 9,385.59. An official at a local asset manager said strong demand for AI and space investments at the time made planned allocations an effective marketing tool when SpaceX went public, but investor sentiment has shifted since then, particularly toward AI-related investments, making Anthropic a harder sell. Regulatory scrutiny has further dampened asset managers' appetite for the stock, with financial regulators cautioning against the promotion of Anthropic-related investments over concerns about potentially misleading or exaggerated marketing claims.

The warning comes against the backdrop of regulatory pressure on local asset managers during the rocket maker's listing, when some firms faced questions over whether they had overstated their exposure to the stock in their ETFs. The subsequent sharp correction in SpaceX shares following their inclusion in ETFs has also contributed to the subdued appetite for Anthropic, with related ETF products yet to recover their previous highs. Still, more asset managers are expected to add Anthropic to their ETF portfolios in the coming days as market conditions stabilize and the stock's initial volatility subsides. Mirae Asset Global Investment listed its Tiger Global LLM Active ETF on the Korea Exchange on Tuesday, announcing a target allocation of 25 percent to Anthropic. Passive ETFs, which can include newly listed stocks only after they have traded for at least two sessions, are also expected to begin adding Anthropic shares.

Articles.Title: Korean asset managers cautious on Anthropic

stories.Headline: AI agents threaten Naver and Kakao as their share prices fall to 2019 levels
stories.Summary:
Naver closed at 156,100 won and Kakao at 30,350 won on the stock market on the 24th, according to The Kyunghyang Shinmun. Both share prices edged up from the previous day's year-to-date lows but were pushed back to levels last seen in November 2019, seven years earlier. The article reported that both companies posted record-high revenue while their share prices kept falling. It said their scale has steadily expanded but the market's appraisal has moved in the opposite direction. The article said growing analysis holds that artificial intelligence is shaking the platform success formula that drove the two companies' growth over the past decade or so.

The article said third-quarter revenue and operating profit both more than doubled over the same period. It said price-to-earnings ratios based on next year's expected results are now 11 times for Naver and 14 times for Kakao, down from 41 times and 32 times seven years earlier. It said total time spent on domestic ChatGPT apps surged 114% in October from a year earlier. It said Naver's advertising revenue growth slowed from 9.3% in the first quarter to 5.5% in the third quarter. It said a McKinsey survey across 11 countries last month found 56% used general-purpose AI search or chatbots for shopping, against 27% for retailers' own AI.

The article said Naver amassed tens of millions of users through search and Kakao through its messenger service, then expanded into advertising and shopping. It said Junho Lee, an analyst at Hana Securities, wrote in a report that day that AI agents would establish themselves as a platform on top of platforms and reshape the existing market order. It said he said those unable to build their own AI agents may end up confined to paying fees to external AIs. It said Minsoo Shin, a professor in the Department of Business Administration at Hanyang University, said changes in the platform market do not happen gradually and cited NateOn users flocking to KakaoTalk all at once. It said he said Naver and Kakao's user bases are assets for now but network effects can disappear quickly once a new platform reaches a tipping point.

The article said Hyojin Lee, an analyst at Meritz Securities, analyzed in a recent report that with generative AI computation costs surge with usage, making it harder to turn a profit than with traditional platforms. It said Kyoungjeon Lee, a professor in the Department of Big Data Analytics at Kyung Hee University, said incumbents have abundant resources for new technologies but face the dilemma of eating into their own earnings. It said he said Naver and Kakao themselves grew by pushing aside former leaders during the transitions to the internet and to smartphones and now face the transition to AI. It said Kakao plans to release its own AI but cannot be complacent. It said Meta's Muse handles everything from product search to payment and the AI assistant Pickle calls restaurants to make reservations.

The article said the more Naver pushes AI search to the fore, the more the position of its traditional search advertising narrows. It said Kakao may see its conventional model of spreading traffic across its services to monetize weaken if AI performs tasks on users' behalf. It said the cost equation of legacy platforms, where margins expanded as users increased, no longer holds. It said the more AI substitutes for search, the greater the potential hit to advertising and shopping businesses, while noting causality cannot be asserted. It said simply adding AI does not guarantee the competitiveness of existing platforms.

The article said it has also become difficult to guarantee platform dominance solely by having a large user base. It said Kakao faces new competition with the emergence of AI agents that select products and even make reservations on behalf of users. It said the market's growth expectations for the two companies have fallen accordingly, reflecting an assessment that their established growth paths have hit a ceiling. It said controlling the daily gateways people pass through is the secret that let the two companies reign as platform behemoths for more than a decade. It did not say what steps either company will take next or when Kakao's own AI will be released.

Articles.Title: Record-high revenue, share prices back to seven years ago… In the AI era, Naver and Kakao's ‘platform success formula’ faces a crisis

stories.Headline: Gaon Cable raises 2027 US sales target 33 percent on AI data center demand
stories.Summary:
Gaon Cable raised the 2027 sales target for its US subsidiary LSCUS by 33.3 percent to 2 trillion won, or about $1.5 billion, on Nov. 24, 2026, according to a Korea Herald report, citing faster than expected orders from AI data centers. LSCUS is expected to post 870 billion won in sales this year, nearly double last year’s 440 billion won, and its 2027 target is about 4.5 times its 2025 sales. Busducts for AI data centers are driving the growth, and LSCUS has secured long-term supply contracts worth more than 5 trillion won with US tech giants through 2030. Under a three-year contract worth about 500 billion won signed with a US tech giant last year, LSCUS had received 330 billion won in purchase orders as of November, which the article says accounted for 66 percent of the expected supply value over the full three-year term.

The company also signed a contract in the first half of this year with another US tech giant for supplies expected to total about 4 trillion won over the next five years. Gaon Cable expects LSCUS’s 2027 sales to comprise 1.3 trillion won in busducts and 700 billion won in distribution cables. To meet rising demand, Gaon Cable plans to double distribution cable capacity at its Tarboro plant in North Carolina by 2027 from end-2025 levels, and it will also expand busduct production through LS Cable’s Gumi plant and a facility in Mexico. The article does not name who at Gaon Cable is responsible for the target or give any statement from the company about it.

Gaon Cable posted record third-quarter revenue of 986.5 billion won and operating profit of 52 billion won, up 51.9 percent and 99.1 percent year on year, respectively. Its operating margin reached 5.3 percent, topping 5 percent for the first time, the article says. The company was also selected for inclusion in both the KOSPI 200 and KRX 300 indices in the Korea Exchange’s second-half index rebalancing, making it the only industrial stock added to both indices, according to the article. The articles do not say what happens next beyond the capacity plans and the 2027 target.

Articles.Title: Gaon Cable lifts US sales target by over 30% amid AI boom

stories.headline_source: Gaon Cable lifts US sales target by over 30% amid AI boom

stories.Headline: Korea plans five-year maximum prison term for national technical exam cheating
stories.Summary:
Recent scandals involving hidden cameras and artificial intelligence have renewed calls for tougher laws in Korea. A group used miniature cameras in buttons and neckties to film exam questions dozens of times. The Seoul Central District Court sentenced an education company operator to one year in prison last May. Two colleagues received ten months in prison, while other acquaintances involved in the scheme were fined. This group conspired from October 2021 to April 2023 to sell reconstructed questions to test-takers.

The group targeted 43 exams from 10 public institutions, including Seoul Metro and Korea Railroad Corporation. These test sites were located across the country, including Busan, Daejeon, and the greater Seoul area. The scheme ended in February 2023 at a Gwanak District site after proctors noticed awkward sitting. The operator was convicted of violating the National Technical Qualifications Act and the Copyright Act. The government now plans to increase the maximum prison sentence for national technical exams to five years.

The Seoul Central District Court stated that these crimes undermined the fairness and credibility of national exams. Lawyer Kwak Joon-ho said that public concern over fairness has grown as cheating combines with technology. He noted that the top tax accountant scorer, Han, may receive a light sentence for cooperating. Kwak argued that penalties should be severe now because AI and other technology have changed the outcome. The court explained that the defendants caused considerable disruption to the operation of the national qualification exams.

Critics say that penalties for cheating remain lenient even as sophisticated AI and smart device use spreads. Most cases end in fines or suspended sentences because no general law punishes exam cheating specifically. A test-taker received a six-month suspended sentence in September for using AI on an English test. The top tax accountant scorer, Han, admitted to cheating and was questioned by the police. Lee Jin-woo, who earned a perfect score on the Legal Education Eligibility Test, also faced allegations.

Cases are typically brought under charges of obstruction of business or violating the Copyright Act. Obstruction charges are used because cheaters interfere with the work of assessing candidates for the exams. AI cheating currently carries no separate penalty and draws punishment similar to that for ordinary cheating. Lee Jin-woo was accused of cheating on the College Scholastic Ability Test and the eligibility test. He was found dead on Thursday after failing to appear for a planned livestream event.

The government will introduce legal penalties for cheating on national professional exams to combat AI-assisted cheating. Authorities are currently investigating the methods used by the top scorer of the tax accountant certification exam. The government intends to raise the maximum prison term for technical exam cheating from two to five years. The articles do not state when these new legal penalties for professional exams will be implemented. It remains open whether the new laws will successfully deter the spread of AI exam cheating.

Articles.Title: AI exam cheating might be spreading in Korea, but punishments remain light, critics say

stories.headline_source: AI exam cheating might be spreading in Korea, but punishments remain light, critics say

stories.Headline: Samsung promotes 131 staff in 2027 reshuffle to back AI, robotics and foundry experts
stories.Summary:
Samsung Electronics promoted 131 employees during its annual executive reshuffle for 2027, which the company announced on Tuesday, November 24, 2026. This move followed record earnings in the semiconductor division and prioritized experts in artificial intelligence, robotics, and foundry services. The total number of promotions decreased by 18.6 percent, or 30 people, compared to the 161 promotions made in the previous year. The reshuffle included 39 executive vice presidents, 78 vice presidents, 12 masters, and two fellows.

High bandwidth memory experts Ha Kyung-soo, Park Tae-hoon, and Park Jin-pyo were elevated to executive vice president, while Kim Myeong-o and Jang Se-jeong received the same rank for their work on DRAM and solid-state drives. In the foundry business, Song Tae-joong, Lee Ho, and Ryu Hyo-gyeom became executive vice presidents, and Lee Ki-jo was promoted to vice president. Robotics and AI leaders including Koo Dong-han and Hyung Seung-yong became vice presidents, while Mathieu Apotheker was promoted to executive vice president. Additionally, 11 women were promoted, including Lee Yoon-kyong, who attained the rank of executive vice president.

The company stated that it prioritized personnel with proven track records and technology experts who can drive future growth. These appointments reflect a commitment to strengthening future businesses through both internal development and the acquisition of external companies. This process follows a leadership change where Hwang Sang-joon, Cho Sang-yeun, and Lee Jong-myeong were named presidents in the semiconductor division. Vice Chairman Jun Young-hyun and President Roh Tae-moon remain as dual CEOs, but they handed over their roles as heads of the Memory and Mobile eXperience businesses.

The new structure allows Vice Chairman Jun to focus on the foundry business while President Roh concentrates on growth areas like robotics. This reshuffle is intended to provide the technological leadership necessary to support the broader business restructuring. Samsung has now completed its executive appointments for the year. The company plans to finalize and announce its organizational restructuring and executive assignments in the near future.

Articles.Title: Samsung promotes chip, robotics, AI leaders after record semiconductor earnings

stories.Headline: TEPS test-takers wear disposable gowns and aprons from December to curb AI cheating
stories.Summary:
Test-takers sitting the TEPS English proficiency exam will have to wear disposable gowns and aprons from next month, amid growing concerns over AI-assisted cheating on exams. TEPS, the Test of English Proficiency developed by Seoul National University, is widely used for university admissions and job applications in Korea. According to the TEPS Council at Seoul National University on Tuesday, candidates will be given the gowns and aprons to wear starting with the 413th regular test on Dec. 5. The council has already banned hats and introduced metal detectors at each test site, starting with a regular test held on Saturday.

Using artificial intelligence, or using or wearing a smart device during the test, will be treated as cheating. Offenders will lose their eligibility for the test and may face legal action. A council official said the measures are intended to protect test-takers and to detect cheating, and that preparations are complete, including the purchase of the supplies.

More to follow.

stories.Headline: Kyunghyang Shinmun requires 2027 contest entrants to disclose AI use and verify creative process
stories.Summary:
Earlier this month, Kyunghyang Shinmun issued its call for entries for the 2027 New Year Literary Contest and included wording requiring entrants to state whether they used AI. The notice asks entrants who used AI during the writing process to specify the tools used and the purpose and scope of use in detail. Entrants who did not use AI must mark it as "Not used" when submitting, according to the notice. The judging panel may request a phone interview or additional materials for shortlisted entries to verify the creative process and any AI use. If it is confirmed that an entrant deliberately omitted the fact of AI use or falsely stated the scope of use, the award may be canceled.

The core principle of the Kyunghyang Shinmun New Year Literary Contest, that it evaluates works written by humans and selects the outstanding among them, remains unchanged. This year an AI-related notice was prepared for the first time, given that generative AI has become commonplace and is widely used in writing as an auxiliary means such as for research. Marking its 79th iteration, the contest has also changed its submission method to online only starting this year. To improve convenience and fairness in receiving and sorting manuscripts, submissions by mail or in person will not be accepted. Online submissions are open until December 4, and application instructions can be checked online.

One novelist who served as a judge for last year's Kyunghyang Shinmun New Year Literary Contest said about adding a ban on AI that it should go without saying that you must not use AI. The novelist said it is strange to warn people not to do what is obvious. Novelist Hwang Sok-young said earlier this year that he uses AI as an aid to writing. Novelist Moon Ji-hyeok said you cannot punish someone for driving with navigation on, but asked whether we should not at least distinguish whether a human really drove or a machine did. Moon added that going forward, pure literature contests may remain as "small-scale artistic arenas" among those who can generate text on their own and those who can discern it.

Publishing critic Kim Sung-shin said it appears to symbolically show that the side effects of AI confronting literature and publishing have become visible. Kim said that with the government placing emphasis on promoting AI technology, publishing and literature are collapsing badly, and the lack of protection for them is also a problem. Kim added that it is meaningful that authors and rights holders are facing up to these issues and trying to find solutions. The literary world calls it "a symbolic incident that makes AI side effects visible." For last year's Kyunghyang Shinmun New Year Literary Contest, submissions increased over the previous year by 2,289 in poetry and 132 in fiction.

Notices banning AI use began appearing in Korean literary contests around 2023, when AI's capabilities in writing advanced rapidly after the release of ChatGPT in November 2022. Some newspapers that host New Year Literary Contests and publishers that run literary prizes added brief warnings stating that if AI use in a work is confirmed, the award may be revoked. This year, the French Goncourt Prize excluded Telisson Aurelien's from the final shortlist after allegations arose that AI wrote it, even though it had made the first-round list. The Canadian publisher that released the book also said it had confirmed indications of AI use and terminated its contract with Aurelien. In one domestic literary competition as well, a work suspected of using AI made it to the final screening, and after deliberation the judges concluded the prize with "no winner."

Munhakgwa Jiseongsa, which had not included AI-related rules in its rookie contests, plans to add language containing AI use guidelines starting next year. Changbi has stated since last year that "works produced by AI cannot be submitted." Most organizers of this year's New Year Literary Contests added wording to their calls stating that judges may verify, through interviews and other means, the creative process and any AI use for shortlisted works. This year, after Anthropic, developer of the generative AI Claude, was reported to have illegally downloaded digital copies of books by well-known authors at home and abroad, including Han Kang, awareness also grew of the problem of using results produced by AI that trained unlawfully on existing works. The announcement for the 1st Kyunghyang Shinmun New Year Literary Contest was made in 1946.

Articles.Title: “Did you really write this novel?”···From confirming AI use to interviews, a changed New Year Literary Contest

stories.Headline: South Korea files criminal complaints against five students over AI cheating in national exams
stories.Summary:
Cases of cheating using advanced artificial intelligence tools surfaced in qualification exams and the College Scholastic Ability Test around November 2026. Authorities issued several emergency disaster alerts to trigger audible alarms on banned smartphones during the examinations to stop these activities. The government is now filing criminal complaints against five students who were accused of using devices during the College Scholastic Ability Test. These incidents have caused widespread fear that AI cheating is spreading into university essay exams as well.

The government plans to combat this trend by increasing the maximum prison sentence for cheating on national technical exams from two years to five years. New legal penalties will also be introduced for those who cheat on national professional exams to ensure stricter enforcement. These changes aim to protect the promise that abilities developed through diligent effort will be evaluated fairly. Such measures are intended to prevent dishonest individuals from gaining an unfair advantage over those who follow the rules.

Choi Hoon, a professor of psychology at Hallym University, stated that AI cheating carries serious social consequences for the public. He explained that people feel betrayed when a psychological contract is broken and dishonest success goes unchecked. According to Choi, individuals may stop valuing rules or lose their belief in social fairness if honesty is not rewarded. He argued that society must ensure that those who lead honest and hard working lives are not betrayed.

The author suggests that this crisis reflects a wider social issue where honest work increasingly feels unrewarded in many areas of life. He noted that simply attending classes is often not enough to secure a job in the current competitive environment. This situation may lead people to live like gamblers who hope for one big break rather than relying on steady effort. The rise of these tools threatens the traditional belief that people can shape their lives through their own abilities.

Articles.Title: AI cheating threatens the promise of honest effort

stories.headline_source: AI cheating threatens the promise of honest effort

stories.Headline: Kyung Hee professor Kim Sang-kyun urges teachers to ask questions and foster student judgment in the AI era
stories.Summary:
Kim Sang-kyun, a professor at Kyung Hee University's Graduate School of Business, wrote the column published on November 24, 2026, about AI use in classrooms. He wrote that AI-assisted cheating has shocked society and that students using AI to write book reports have become commonplace in schools. He said their assignments may appear authentic, but closer reading often reveals strange details absent from the books. He said that when asked whether they read the books and wrote the reports themselves, most students protest their innocence. He said adults face a dilemma over whether children should be prohibited from using AI or allowed to use it freely.

The column cites a 2025 experiment published by MIT Media Lab that compared groups writing four essays, some using AI and others working without it. It says brain connectivity was significantly weaker among AI users. It says 83 percent of the AI users reportedly gave incorrect answers when questioned about their essays. It says Samsung Electronics announced on Nov. 17 that it will introduce hands-on sessions featuring its Galaxy XR extended reality headset as part of its Galaxy AI Class educational program. It says students participate in a Galaxy AI Class session using Galaxy XR headsets at Daebang Middle School in Seoul.

Kim said the question is not whether children should use AI but whether they understand it properly. He said generative AI frequently produces incorrect answers with remarkable confidence, a phenomenon known as hallucination, and children may mistake these confident responses for facts. He said understanding AI's limitations and learning to use it responsibly remain fundamentally human responsibilities. He said teachers must become people who ask questions in return, asking students which part reflects their own thinking, how to verify an answer and what AI has overlooked. He said students should spend at least five minutes thinking independently before using AI for homework and should close their screens and rewrite their work in their own words afterward.

Kim said he calls the phenomenon of middle school students treating AI like a friend "artificial relationships." He said children confide worries to AI that they hesitate to share with friends or teachers. He said adults should ask, from the child's perspective, whether after talking with AI the child wants to spend more time with friends or less. He said he recently delivered a special lecture at a teacher training program organized by the CJ Welfare Foundation through its CJ Donors Camp initiative for teachers working in child welfare facilities. He said some children were already proficient AI users while others had encountered the technology for the first time at community child centers.

Kim said every technological advance, from calculators and the internet to smartphones, has provoked anxiety, and older generations have always worried about new technologies, but humanity has adapted. He said AI can create the illusion of intellectual effort because it produces finished work, and repeated dependence risks weakening children's capacity for inquiry. He said the traditional role of teachers as providers of correct answers is diminishing because children increasingly turn to AI first when they have questions. He said relationships among peers inevitably involve friction, making an AI companion that consistently takes their side particularly appealing, but people develop closer relationships by resolving conflicts. He said the program sought to strengthen the capabilities of teachers working in child welfare facilities, and together they considered what education should look like in the AI era.

Kim said teachers who patiently ask questions, examine answers alongside children and give them time to develop their own ideas create lasting educational experiences. He said children need adults who think alongside them rather than simply supply correct answers in the AI era. He said teachers should cultivate curiosity, judgment and confidence, not merely supervise technology use. He said children who learn to reason through problems with others will eventually become adults capable of cooperating, resolving differences and building a better society together. The column does not say what specific policies schools should adopt or how AI use in classrooms will be regulated.

Articles.Title: AI can write homework, but can it replace thinking?

stories.headline_source: AI can write homework, but can it replace thinking?

stories.Headline: Seoul medical students post video solving Suneung Korean section
stories.Summary:
Three first-year medical students at Seoul National University posted a YouTube video in which they worked through the Korean language section of this year's Suneung, the national college entrance exam held on Thursday, and then shared their results along with footage of how each reached their answers. Two of the three entered the medical school through early admissions and the third through regular admissions, and one of them said in the video that none of them had known about AI glasses or such cheating methods during the admissions process, let alone used them. Lee Jin-woo, a first-year dentistry student at Seoul National University who scored perfectly on this year's Legal Education Eligibility Test, had pledged to take the Korean language section on a livestream, and he was found dead in an apparent suicide on Thursday, hours after he failed to show up for the demonstration he had proposed in response to the cheating allegations. On Nov. 12, the second-highest scorer on this year's tax accountant qualification exam posted a YouTube video of themselves solving questions from the tax accounting section, extending the trend beyond the Suneung.

The trend follows a series of high-profile cases of AI-assisted cheating that have fueled growing distrust of academic achievements and professional credentials. The Ministry of Education announced that 111 cases of cheating involving electronic devices were detected during Thursday's Suneung, and five of those involved devices such as smart glasses and miniature cameras. On Nov. 15, Han Won-seok, 34, who ranked first in both stages of this year's tax accountant exam, admitted to obtaining answers with the help of a miniature camera, a generative AI model and a smartphone. Han, who correctly answered 159 of 160 questions in the first round, also confessed to using the same method in the first stage of the certified public accountant exam in March, which he failed.

Investigators at the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency have searched Han's residence and secured digital forensic evidence as part of their ongoing investigation, and he underwent his fourth round of police questioning on Monday. Han reportedly photographed test questions with a camera attached to a correction tape dispenser and used a modified calculator to relay the images to a laptop at his home via a smartphone hidden inside an abdominal support belt. He then viewed the AI-generated responses on a miniature monitor concealed on his body. The articles do not say what further action is planned in the investigation or what consequences the students and professionals who posted the videos may face.

Articles.Title: No AI needed: Exam high-flyers put their skills on display
